# Future Directions

Four Lean files now carry the fluctuation-theoretic side of this thread.  All of them
compile against Lean 4.28 / Mathlib with no `sorry`, no stubbed signature and only the
standard axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

* `Catalog/Computation/FluctuationRobustDemon.lean` — the finite Jarzynski/Crooks model and
  the **independent** concentration bound
  `P( ∑_{i<n} W_i ≤ n·w ) ≤ exp( -n·β·(ΔF - w) )` (`FluctDemon.deficit_concentration`).
* `Catalog/Computation/AdaptiveFluctuationDemon.lean` — the **adaptive** version.  An
  adaptive demon is a fixed-depth decision tree of work systems
  (`FluctDemon.AdaptiveDemon`); if each stage dissipates at least `ΔF` in the sense
  `⟨e^{-βW}⟩ ≤ e^{-βΔF}`, then `P( total work over n stages ≤ t ) ≤ exp( -β·(n·ΔF - t) )`
  (`FluctDemon.adaptive_deficit_bound_of_dissipative`).
* `Catalog/Computation/StoppingTimeDemon.lean` — the **stopping-time** version.  A
  `FluctDemon.StoppingDemon` may halt at any node, so the number of erasure stages `N` is a
  random variable and the depth index is only an a priori horizon.  Proved:

  ```
  P( total work ≤ t  and  N ≥ m )   ≤  exp( -β·(m·ΔF - t) )      stopping_deficit_bound
  P( total work ≤ w·N and N ≥ m )   ≤  exp( -m·β·(ΔF - w) )      stopping_rate_deficit_bound
  ΔF · E[N]                         ≤  E[total work]              stopping_wald
  ```

  together with the reliability bound `m ≤ log(1/δ)/(β(ΔF-w))`
  (`FluctDemon.stopping_reliability_bound`), the vanishing of the success probability
  (`FluctDemon.stopping_deficit_tendsto_zero`), and two non-vacuity witnesses: `coinStop`
  (random horizon, `E[N] = 3/2`, exact sub-threshold probability `1/4` against the bound
  `4/9`, strict Wald slack `(3/4)log(4/3)/β`) and the unbounded-horizon family `geoStop`
  whose exact sub-threshold probability is `(1/2)^n` at every horizon `n`, against the
  bound `(2/3)^n`.

* `Catalog/Computation/CrooksCompleteness.lean` (this cycle) — the **converse direction** of
  the model.  Conjecture 4 of the previous cycle ("Crooks-completeness of the finite
  model") is resolved affirmatively, and in a stronger form than conjectured:

  ```
  Jarzynski β ΔF S  ↔  ∃ C : CrooksPair β ΔF Ω, C.fwd = S      jarzynski_iff_exists_crooks
  ```

  The partner lives on the *same* outcome space and the time reversal `flip` may be
  prescribed arbitrarily (`FluctDemon.reverseSystem`, `FluctDemon.crooksCompletion`); it is
  unique given `(fwd, flip)` (`FluctDemon.crooks_rev_unique`); it charges the time reverse
  of every outcome the forward protocol charges (`FluctDemon.reverseSystem_prob_pos`), so
  the conjectured obstruction ("an outcome of zero forward and nonzero reverse
  probability") is vacuous (`FluctDemon.no_jarzynski_system_lacks_crooks_partner`).  In
  addition:

  ```
  Jarzynski β (-ΔF) C.rev                                        crooks_rev_jarzynski
  CrooksPair.reverse : CrooksPair β ΔF Ω → CrooksPair β (-ΔF) Ω  (an involution)
  P( W ≤ w )  ≤  e^{-β(ΔF-w)} · (reverse mass of the reversed event)
                                                                 crooks_deficit_le_rev
  ```

  the last being a strict sharpening of the one-shot Chernoff bound
  (`FluctDemon.crooks_deficit_strict`).  Non-vacuity: for the catalog's `coinDemon` the
  reverse protocol is `(q(true), q(false)) = (1/4, 3/4)` and the sharpened bound is
  *exactly attained*, `e^{-β(ΔF-w)}·(3/4) = (2/3)(3/4) = 1/2 = P(W ≤ w)`
  (`FluctDemon.coinCrooks_sharpened_bound_eq`), against the unsharpened value `2/3`.

  The moral of the cycle: in the finite model, Jarzynski compliance and Crooks compliance
  carry *the same information*; the reversal is free data, and what genuinely constrains a
  demon beyond `⟨e^{-βW}⟩ = e^{-βΔF}` is the reverse mass of the deficit event.

The conjectures below are what remains open, restated against this baseline.

---

## 1. Exact large-deviation rate and the equality case

**Conjecture.** For a fixed finite-outcome protocol `S` obeying Jarzynski at cost `ΔF`,

```
lim_{n→∞} -(1/n) log P( ∑ W_i ≤ n·w )  =  I_S(w)  ≥  β (ΔF - w),
```

where `I_S` is the Legendre transform of `Λ_S(λ) = log ⟨e^{λ W}⟩`, and equality
`I_S(w) = β(ΔF - w)` holds **iff** the sub-threshold mass of `S` sits at the single work
value `w` (the "all-or-nothing" protocol).

*Status.* `FluctDemon.single_deficit_bound` gives `≥` at `n = 1`, and the new
`FluctDemon.crooks_deficit_le_rev` identifies the exact one-shot slack: the bound is
`e^{-β(ΔF-w)}·m_rev(w)` with `m_rev(w)` the reverse mass of the time-reversed deficit
event, and this is attained with equality for `coinDemon` at `w = ΔF - log(3/2)/β`.  So the
sharpened one-shot statement is tight; the open content is now purely the `n → ∞`
tensorisation of the factor `m_rev(w)`, which we conjecture contributes the missing
`I_S(w) - β(ΔF - w)`.

*Falsifiable:* a two- or three-outcome protocol with `I_S(w) = β(ΔF-w)` whose sub-threshold
mass is spread over two distinct work values; equivalently, one whose reverse mass
`m_rev(w)^n` fails to capture the `n`-fold slack.

## 2. Almost-surely finite demons with no horizon at all

**Conjecture.** Let a demon be an infinite decision tree with an almost surely finite
stopping time `N` (rather than a tree of some finite depth `n`), every node dissipative at
`ΔF`.  Then the three displayed stopping-time bounds hold verbatim, and moreover
`E[total work] ≥ ΔF·E[N]` requires no integrability hypothesis beyond `E[N] < ∞`.

The stopping-time theorem covers every tree of *some* finite depth, uniformly in that
depth, which already forces the conclusion for the truncations `N ∧ n` of an infinite tree.
The open content is the passage to the limit: is `lim_n E[W_{N∧n}] = E[W_N]`, or can a
demon smuggle work into the tail?  We expect uniform integrability to fail exactly when
`E[N] = ∞`, which would make this the horizon-free counterpart of the `T → 0` analysis in
§5.

*Falsifiable:* an infinite tree, all nodes Jarzynski compliant, with `E[N] < ∞` and
`E[total work] < ΔF·E[N]`.

## 3. Erasure-count lower bound for reusable workspace

**Conjecture.** Fix a family of decision processes whose size-`n` instance discards `b(n)`
bits in the sense of the catalog's size-indexed dissipation theory.  Then every
implementation reusing a workspace of `s(n)` cells performs at least `b(n) - O(s(n))`
dissipative stages, hence by `FluctDemon.stopping_reliability_bound` no implementation can
spend below `(1-ε)·b(n)·k_B T log 2` with probability `Ω(1)` unless `b(n) = O(s(n) + log n)`.

The thermodynamic half is proved in the form the computational half needs: the reliability
bound is stated for a *random* number of stages, so an implementation whose number of
erasures depends on the instance is covered.  The open content is the *identification
step*: which reuse patterns of a polynomial-time workspace force stages that are genuinely
dissipative at the Landauer value, rather than merely logically irreversible?

*Falsifiable:* a polynomial-time family with `b(n) = n`, workspace `s(n) = O(log n)`, and a
constant-probability sub-Landauer implementation.

## 4. Rigidity of the time reversal: self-dual Crooks pairs

Crooks-completeness shows that the reversal `flip` is *free data* — every Jarzynski system
admits a partner for every `flip`, even the identity.  A physically meaningful reversal must
therefore be pinned down by an extra axiom, and the natural one is self-duality.

**Conjecture.** Call a Crooks pair *self-dual* if `flip` is an involution, `rev = fwd` as
work systems, and `ΔF = 0`.  Then a finite work system `S = (p, W)` is the forward half of a
self-dual pair **iff** there is an involution `flip` with `W ∘ flip = -W` and
`p(ω) = e^{βW(ω)} p(flip ω)` for all `ω`; and every such `S` has `⟨W⟩ ≥ 0` with equality iff
`W ≡ 0`.  Consequently the self-dual systems are exactly the equilibrium (zero-free-energy,
detailed-balanced) protocols, and no demon is self-dual at `ΔF > 0`.

*Status.* The "only if" direction is immediate from `FluctDemon.crooks_rev_prob_eq`; the
content is the converse construction and the equality case, which should follow from the
proved `FluctDemon.crooks_rev_jarzynski` applied to `CrooksPair.reverse` together with
`FluctDemon.meanWork_ge_of_jarzynski` at both `ΔF` and `-ΔF`.

*Falsifiable:* a self-dual pair with `ΔF > 0`, or a work system satisfying the displayed
detailed-balance identity with `⟨W⟩ < 0`.

## 5. Zero-temperature degeneration of the exponent

**Conjecture.** As `β → ∞` with `ΔF = k_B T log 2` fixed at the Landauer value, the exponent
`β(ΔF - w)` tends to `-βw`, so the bound is vacuous for every fixed `w > 0` and informative
only for `w ≤ 0`.  Consequently an apparent zero-work erasing demon obtained in the `T → 0`
limit must have diverging resources: with `w = 0`, `FluctDemon.stopping_reliability_bound`
gives `m ≤ log(1/δ)/log 2`, a *`β`-independent constant* on the number of erasures the
demon can complete at fixed success probability — and by `FluctDemon.stopping_wald` the
expected work still grows like `ΔF·E[N]`, so the only escape is `E[N] → ∞`.

This turns the "Zero-Temperature Boundary Classification" conjecture of the original
direction into a quantitative dichotomy: at `T → 0` the loophole closes as a divergence of
the *resource* `E[N]`, not of the exponent.

*Falsifiable:* a family of finite stopping strategies, parameterised by `β`, with `w = 0`,
`ΔF = k_B T log 2`, deficit probability bounded below, bounded `E[N]`, and outcome-space
size `O(poly)`.

# Future directions

Derived from the five Lean files of this thread, all of which compile against
mathlib4 (Lean 4.28.0) with no `sorry` and use only the standard axioms
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`:

* `Catalog/Applications/WallpaperRhythm/QuotientEntropy.lean` — the abstract
  `InvariantPattern` capacity theorem (earlier cycle);
* `Catalog/Computation/WallpaperRhythm/OrbitCounting.lean` — instantiation of
  that setoid by a group action, Burnside evaluation, exact counts on the
  toroidal grids `ZMod p × ZMod q`;
* `Catalog/Computation/WallpaperRhythm/OrbitEntropy.lean` — probabilistic
  entropy, strict monotonicity of capacity, the `IsCanonAt` predicate with its
  onset-count obstruction, the quarter-turn descent criterion;
* `Catalog/Computation/WallpaperRhythm/QuarterTurnCapacity.lean` — realizability
  of symmetry groups, the exact quarter-turn capacity of every square torus, and
  the point-group descent dichotomy;
* `Catalog/Computation/WallpaperRhythm/BernoulliEntropy.lean` — the exact entropy
  of the orbit-Bernoulli model and the per-orbit entropy deficit;
* `Catalog/Computation/WallpaperRhythm/CanonSharpness.lean` — the complete onset
  spectrum of canons;
* `Catalog/Computation/WallpaperRhythm/GlideCapacity.lean` — glide reflections of
  a torus: fixed-point freeness and the capacity `2 ^ (p q / 2)`.

## Status of the conjectures posed in the previous cycle

All five are now **theorems**.

* **C1. Realizability of symmetry types — proved, and in greater generality.**
  `symmetryGroup_subgroupPattern`: for the translation action of any group `G` on
  itself, every subgroup `H ≤ G` is *exactly* the symmetry group of the indicator
  pattern of `H`.  `symmetryGroup_torusSubgroupPattern` transports this to the
  cyclic time-shift action on the `p × q` torus, so on a drum grid every
  symmetry type is realized by an explicit pattern.
* **C2. Sharpness of the canon onset obstruction — proved.**
  `isCanonAt_onsetCount_iff`: a number `k` is the onset count of some canon at
  time distance `g` on the `p × q` torus **iff** `addOrderOf g ∣ k` and
  `k ≤ p * q`.  The divisibility obstruction of the previous cycle is therefore
  complete, not merely necessary.  The general mechanism is
  `exists_invariant_finset_card` (a free action of a finite group has an
  invariant subset of every size `|Γ| · j` with `j` at most the orbit count).
  Worked instance: `canon_onsetCount_four_one` (`{0, 2, 4}` on the four-beat
  grid).
* **C3. Quarter-turn capacity — proved, and extended to even side lengths.**
  `card_pattern_quarterTurn`: the number of quarter-turn invariant patterns on
  the `p × p` torus is `2 ^ ((p² + 2t + t²) / 4)` with `t = twoTorsionCard p`.
  For odd `p` this is the conjectured `2 ^ ((p² + 3) / 4)`; for even `p` it is
  `2 ^ ((p² + 8) / 4)`, because the quarter turn then fixes two diagonal cells
  and the half turn four.  Numeric instances: `8` (3×3), `128` (5×5), `8` (2×2),
  `64` (4×4).
* **C4. Which point groups descend to a rectangular torus — proved.**
  `signedDiag_mapsTo_torusLattice` (diagonal sign changes always preserve
  `pℤ × qℤ`) together with `signedSwap_mapsTo_torusLattice_iff` (a signed
  coordinate swap preserves it iff `p = q`) determines the subgroup of the
  order-eight point group `D₄` descending to the `p × q` torus: the order-four
  diagonal subgroup when `p ≠ q`, all of `D₄` when `p = q`.
* **C5. Entropy deficit as a measure of stylistic constraint — proved.**
  `entropyBits_orbitBernoulli`: the orbit-Bernoulli distribution (switch each of
  the `m` orbits on independently with probability `θ`) has entropy exactly
  `m · H₂(θ)` bits, so by `entropyDeficit_orbitBernoulli` the deficit is
  `m · (1 - H₂(θ))` — a fixed cost per orbit — nonnegative
  (`entropyDeficit_nonneg`) and zero exactly at `θ = 1/2`
  (`entropyDeficit_eq_zero_iff`).

## New conjectures

Each is stated so that a single Lean counterexample refutes it.

### N1. Capacity of a rectangular torus under its full descended point group

By C4 the point group descending to the `p × q` torus with `p ≠ q` is the Klein
four-group `{diag(±1, ±1)}`.  Conjecture: the number of patterns invariant under
all four of its elements is

    2 ^ ( (p + t(p)) * (q + t(q)) / 4 ),   t(n) = twoTorsionCard n = gcd(2, n),

since Burnside adds `p*q`, `q*t(p)`, `p*t(q)` and `t(p)*t(q)` fixed cells.
*Refutation:* a pair `(p, q)` where a brute-force count differs — equivalently a
cell fixed by a coordinate sign change that the parity bookkeeping misses.
This is the rectangular counterpart of the proved `card_pattern_quarterTurn`, and
would complete the capacity table for every planar point group that descends.

### N2. Capacity under the full dihedral group of a square torus

For `p` odd let `D₄` act on `ZMod p × ZMod p` by the four rotations of
`QuarterTurns` together with the four reflections `(t,n) ↦ (n,t)`,
`(t,n) ↦ (-n,-t)`, `(t,n) ↦ (-t,n)`, `(t,n) ↦ (t,-n)`.  Each reflection should
fix exactly `p` cells, so Burnside predicts `(p + 1)(p + 3) / 8` orbits and

    capacity = 2 ^ ((p + 1) * (p + 3) / 8).

*Refutation:* an odd `p` (say `p = 7`, predicted `2 ^ 10`) where the count
differs.  Note the prediction agrees with the proved rotation-only value at
`p = 3` (both give `8`) but is strictly smaller from `p = 5` on, so the two
statements are independent.

### N3. Realizability for a non-free action

`symmetryGroup_subgroupPattern` realizes every subgroup for a *free* translation
action.  Conjecture: realizability survives the loss of freeness for the
quarter-turn action — for every `p ≥ 3` and every subgroup `H ≤ QuarterTurns`
there is a pattern `f : ZMod p × ZMod p → Bool` with
`symmetryGroup QuarterTurns f = H`.  *Refutation:* a `p ≥ 3` and a subgroup
(necessarily one of `⊥`, the half-turn subgroup, `⊤`) realized by no pattern.
Failure at `p = 1` is immediate — the single cell forces `⊤` — so the bound
`p ≥ 3` is part of the claim.

### N4. Capacity of the toroidal "pg" group

`card_pattern_glide` counts the patterns invariant under a single glide
reflection `γ(t, n) = (t + p/2, -n)` on the `p × q` torus with `p` even: there
are `2 ^ (p q / 2)`, since `γ` is fixed-point free
(`fixedBy_glide_eq_empty`).  Conjecture: for the larger group generated by `γ`
together with *every* time shift — the toroidal analogue of the wallpaper group
`pg` — the orbits are exactly the pitch pairs `{n, -n}`, so the capacity is

    2 ^ ((q + t(q)) / 2),   t(n) = gcd(2, n),

independently of `p`.  *Refutation:* an even `p` and a `q` where a brute-force
count differs, i.e. where the glide and the shifts fail to merge two cells with
the same pitch class.  For `q = 3` the prediction is `4` patterns for every even
`p`.

### N5. Maximum entropy at fixed onset density

The orbit-Bernoulli model is the natural biased model, but is it the *only*
extremal one?  Conjecture: among all probability distributions `P` on
`GroupInvariantPattern G α` whose expected number of "on" orbits is `m θ`, the
entropy `entropyBits P` is maximized precisely by `orbitBernoulli θ`, with value
`m · H₂(θ)`.  *Refutation:* a group action, a `θ` and a distribution with the
same expected onset density and strictly larger entropy.  Together with the
proved deficit law this would make `m · (1 - H₂(θ))` the exact information cost
of a stylistic onset density, rather than merely the cost of one particular
model.

# Future Directions

Derived from the results proved in `Catalog/Novelty/ArithmetizedQFTReflection.lean`,
`Catalog/Novelty/ConsistencyTransferSharpness.lean`,
`Catalog/Novelty/HeightSpectrumTransfer.lean`,
`Catalog/Novelty/TransferPreorderRealization.lean` and
`Catalog/Novelty/PhysicalCountermodelCompleteness.lean`.  Each conjecture is
stated so that a single verified Lean object refutes it.

## 1. Exact reflection strength of the interpretation axiom

The explicit arithmetic `PAsys pa qft` proves `Con(QFT₀) → Con(PA)` from the single
interpretation axiom `□_pa ⊥ → □_qft ⊥`.

**Conjecture.**  Over the GL calculus `Thm pa Ax`, the reflection sentence
`Con(qft) → Con(pa)` is derivable from an axiom set `Ax` consisting of *boxed-falsum
implications only* if and only if `Ax` already contains (or derives) the transfer
implication `□_pa ⊥ → □_qft ⊥`.

*Falsified by* an axiom set of that shape, plus a derivation of the reflection
sentence, together with a GL model validating `Ax` in which `□_pa ⊥ → □_qft ⊥` fails.

## 2. Depth-graded failure of reflection

`capSysN n` is consistent, minimally sound, and refutes the uniform reflection rule
exactly at iteration depth `n`: it proves `□^{n+1}⊥` and refutes `□^n ⊥`.

**Conjecture (depth-graded reflection hierarchy).**  For every `n ≥ 1` the *restricted*
reflection rule "`⊢ □ φ` implies `⊢ φ` for all `φ` of box-depth `< n`" holds in
`capSysN n`, while it fails at depth `n`.  Hence 1-consistency stratifies into a
strictly increasing chain of conditions, each strictly stronger than the minimal
soundness condition `⊬ □⊥` that is *equivalent* to the negative independence half.

*Falsified by* a formula of box-depth `< n` provably boxed but unprovable in
`capSysN n`, or by a proof that the depth-`n` rule holds.

## 3. Beyond the resolved one-sided transfer question

*Status: the previous conjecture of this section is now a theorem.*  In
`Catalog/Novelty/ConsistencyTransferSharpness.lean` the tag-sensitive Kripke
semantics `satC` yields an explicit consistent GL theory `sepSys u` with tags `u ≠ t`
proving `Con u → Con t` in which `Con t` is independent while `Con u` is refuted
(`one_sided_transfer_insufficient`, `mutual_transfer_not_weakenable`).  The exact
repair is also proved: one-sided transfer *plus* minimal soundness at the source tag
restores independence (`one_sided_transfer_with_min_soundness`), and minimal soundness
cannot be dropped (`min_soundness_hypothesis_necessary`).

*Status: the height-spectrum conjecture previously listed here is now settled — and it
was **false**.*  `Catalog/Novelty/HeightSpectrumTransfer.lean` computes the spectrum
exactly:

* `capC_Con_independent_iff` : `Independent (capC c N) (Con i) ↔ 1 ≤ c i ∧ 1 ≤ N`,
  so the conjectured upper constraint `c i ≤ N` is spurious
  (`height_spectrum_conjecture_false`);
* `capC_transfer_iff` : `Provable (capC c N) (imp (Con i) (Con j)) ↔ min N (c i) ≤ c j`,
  so the conjectured description `c i ≤ c j ∨ c i = 0` is too narrow
  (`transfer_spectrum_conjecture_false`).

The correct invariant is the *truncated* height `min N (c i)`: mutual transfer holds
iff `min N (c i) = min N (c j)` (`capC_mutual_transfer_iff`), which by
`capC_mutual_transfer_forces_simultaneous_independence` gives an explicit non-vacuous
family of instances of `independence_transfer`.  That invariant is moreover
**complete** — `provable_capC_congr_of_min_eq`: height functions with the same
truncation `min N ∘ c` generate the very same theory — and the transfer relation
`i ≼ j :↔ Provable (capC c N) (Con i → Con j)` is always a total preorder
(`capC_transfer_total_preorder`).

*Status: the realization conjecture previously listed here is now a theorem — and it
was **true**.*  `Catalog/Novelty/TransferPreorderRealization.lean` proves the exact
characterization of the realizable consistency-strength preorders:

* `transfer_preorder_characterization` : a relation `R` on tags is the provable-transfer
  relation `TransferRel c N` of some height function `c` **iff** `R` is transitive,
  total, and has no strict chain of length `N + 1` (`HasChainTo R (N+1) i`);
* `totalPreorder_iff_rank_representation` : equivalently, `R i j ↔ h i ≤ h j` for some
  `h` bounded by `N` — the rank function `rank R N` (the longest strict chain ending at
  a tag) is such an `h`, so the realizing theory is the explicit `capC (rank R N) N`
  (`transfer_preorder_summary`, which also records that it is consistent and GL);
* `transfer_pigeonhole` : among any `N + 2` tags two are transfer-equivalent, so at most
  `N + 1` strengths are separated, and `transfer_linear_order_realized` shows the bound
  is attained.

Section §6 of the same file explains the invariant: the truncated height is exactly the
*depth of provable inconsistency*, `Provable (capC c N) (□_i^k ⊥) ↔ 1 ≤ k ∧ min N (c i) < k`
(`capC_provable_boxPow_bot_iff`), and the transfer spectrum for all iterated boxed falsa
is computed in `capC_boxPow_transfer_iff`.

Two further facts about the *depth vector* `d c N i := min N (c i)` are proved there:
it is a complete invariant in the strong sense that different depth vectors give
different theories (`capC_ne_of_min_ne`, converse of `provable_capC_congr_of_min_eq`),
but the inclusion order between these theories is **not** the pointwise order on depth
vectors — `theory_inclusion_not_pointwise` exhibits `N = 1`, `d = (0, 1, 1, …) ≤
d' = (1, 1, …)` with `□_0 ⊥ → □_1 ⊥` provable for `d'` and refuted for `d`.

**Conjecture (order-preservation criterion for inclusion).**  For truncated depth
vectors `d = min N ∘ c` and `d' = min N ∘ c'`, the inclusion
`Provable (capC c' N) a → Provable (capC c N) a` holds for **every** formula `a` iff

1. `d i ≤ d' i` for every tag `i`  (depths may only increase), *and*
2. `d' i ≤ d' j → d i ≤ d j` for all tags `i, j`  (the relative order of the depths is
   not disturbed).

Condition 1 alone is provably insufficient (`theory_inclusion_not_pointwise`, in which
condition 2 fails); condition 1 alone is necessary because
`capC_provable_boxPow_bot_iff` reads the depths off the iterated boxed falsa.

*Falsified by* a pair `(c, c')` satisfying 1 and 2 together with a formula provable for
`c'` but not for `c`, or by a pair violating 1 or 2 whose theories are nevertheless
included.

## 4. Realizability gap for finitely presented operational semantics

The two-state switch is nonempty, finite, fully sound, and refutes
"consistent ⟹ realizable" with the finite constraint set `{on, off}`.

**Conjecture (no finite completeness).**  Every finitely presented operational
semantics (finite world type, decidable satisfaction) whose language contains at
least two mutually exclusive observation constraints is incomplete for the
assumption-plus-ex-falso proof system: some finite consistent constraint set has no
realization.

*Falsified by* a finite, decidable semantics with mutually exclusive observables in
which every consistent finite constraint set is realizable.

## 5. Sharpness of the completeness boundary

`consistency_equivalence_iff` characterizes the coincidence of mathematical and
physical consistency as `FalsumSound ∧ Complete`, and
`equivalence_without_full_soundness` shows full soundness is *not* implied by the
boundary.

**Conjecture (boundary rigidity).**  There is no semantic condition `C` strictly
between falsum-soundness and full soundness such that `C ∧ Complete` is *equivalent*
to the consistency biconditional for every proof system: any such `C` must already be
implied by falsum-soundness on complete semantics.

*Falsified by* a condition `C`, a complete falsum-sound semantics violating `C`
(showing `C` is strictly stronger), together with a proof that `C ∧ Complete` is
still equivalent to the biconditional.

# Future Directions

Derived from the analysis and adversarial review of cycles 1–9
(`Catalog/Computation/FourierFunctor/`), where we proved: `pontryagin : FinAb ≌
FinAbᵒᵖ`, `fourierNatIso` (Fourier inversion as a natural isomorphism of
functors `FinAb ⥤ ModuleCat ℂ`), `donoho_stark` with its **complete** equality
case (`donoho_stark_equality_iff`), the convolution theorem, Plancherel, the
fourth-power identity, exactness of duality with the character extension
theorem, annihilator counting, Poisson summation, the quadratic Gauss sum
evaluation `‖∑_x ψ(x²)‖² = N`, and — new in this cycle — the **kernel-level
uncertainty principle** (`abstract_uncertainty`, `AbstractUncertainty.lean`) and
**Pontryagin duality as a self-adjunction whose hom-set bijection is the
bicharacter swap** (`SelfDuality.lean`).

Each conjecture below is falsifiable and stated so that a single Lean file could
settle it.

---

## Closed since the previous cycle

* **C1 (the uncertainty principle is not about `𝓕`) — now a theorem.**
  `abstract_uncertainty` proves: if `T` is the transform with kernel
  `k : G → H → ℂ`, all entries of modulus `≤ μ`, and `f` can be reconstructed
  from `T f` by a kernel `l : H → G → ℂ` with entries of modulus `≤ ν`, then
  every non-zero `f` satisfies `1 ≤ μ · ν · |supp f| · |supp (T f)|`.  Three
  instantiations are proved: `donoho_stark_of_abstract` (Fourier, `μ = 1`,
  `ν = |G|⁻¹`, recovering the Donoho–Stark constant `|G|`),
  `matrix_uncertainty` (the Elad–Bruckstein coherence bound `1 ≤ μ² ·
  |supp f| · |supp (Uᵀ f)|` for any matrix with orthonormal rows) and
  `unbiased_uncertainty` (the normalised complex-Hadamard / mutually-unbiased
  form `n ≤ |supp f| · |supp (Uᵀ f)|`), with `hadamard2_uncertainty` as an
  explicit non-Fourier witness.  Sharpness is also formalised:
  `support_kernelTransform_delta` and `flat_kernel_card_bound` show that for a
  flat kernel Dirac masses attain the bound, so the constant `(μν)⁻¹` is
  optimal.  The unexpected structural conclusion is that the relevant invariant
  is the **coherence `μν`**, not the group order: `|G|` only ever enters through
  the normalisation of the inversion kernel.
* **C3 (self-adjointness of duality; Fourier as unit) — now a theorem.**
  `SelfDuality.lean` builds `dualSelfAdjunction : dualFunctor.rightOp ⊣
  dualFunctor` with `dualSelfAdjunction_unit_app` identifying its unit with
  `doubleDualNatIso`, and — the substantive half —
  `toAdjunction_homEquiv_eq_swapHom` shows that the abstract hom-set bijection
  is exactly the bicharacter swap `swapEquiv : (G →+ Ĥ) ≃ (H →+ Ĝ)`,
  `(swapHom f) h g = f g h`.  The identity of `Ĝ` is sent to evaluation
  (`swapHom_id_eq_doubleDualEmb`), and the Fourier kernel consists of its values
  (`fourier_apply_eq_swap_id`), which is the precise sense in which "the Fourier
  transform is the unit of self-duality".  A by-product is the counting identity
  `card_hom_dual_swap`.
* **C2 (equality case of Donoho–Stark)** and **C4 (ii) (Gauss-sum evaluation)**
  were closed in the previous cycle (`Rigidity.lean`, `GaussSum.lean`).

---

## C2′. Stability: almost-extremal functions are almost coset indicators

**Conjecture.** There is an absolute constant `C` such that for every finite
abelian `G` and every non-zero `f` with
`|supp f|·|supp 𝓕f| ≤ (1 + ε)·|G|`, there exist `K, a, χ, c` with

`‖f − c·χ·1_{a+K}‖₂ ≤ C·√ε·‖f‖₂`.

*The key insight is* that the proof of `donoho_stark_rigidity` is a chain of
three inequalities (triangle inequality for `𝓕f ψ`, `ℓ¹`-inversion at the
maximiser, and `‖f g‖ ≤ M`), each of which has a quantitative defect version;
`Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le` becomes "the number of terms with a defect `> δ`
is `< ε/δ`", so the rigid conclusion `f g = c·ψ g` degrades to an `ℓ²` estimate.

*Why now?*  With the exact equality case closed, every step of the argument is
written down explicitly in Lean, and the defect version replaces each equality
lemma by a bound with the same proof skeleton.

**Falsification route.** A family `f_n` on `ℤ/n` with
`|supp f_n|·|supp 𝓕f_n|/|ℤ/n| → 1` whose `ℓ²`-distance to every modulated coset
indicator stays bounded below.

---

## C4. Flat functions and the quadratic reciprocity route

**Conjecture.** Call `f : G → ℂ` *bi-unimodular* if `|f|` is constant and `|𝓕f|`
is constant.  Then (i) the bi-unimodular functions on `ZMod N`, `N` odd, are
exactly the modulated quadratic phases `x ↦ c·ψ(a x² + b x)` with `a` a unit —
the dual statement to `donoho_stark_equality_iff`; and (ii) the sign of the
Gauss sum (not just its modulus, which is `quadratic_gauss_sum_normSq`) can be
computed from the `4`-periodicity of `𝓕⁴ = |G|²·id` proved in
`Convolution.lean`, yielding a Fourier-analytic proof of quadratic reciprocity
for `ZMod p`.

*The key insight is* that our two extremal families now bracket the whole range
of the uncertainty product — coset indicators realise the minimum `|G|`
(`donoho_stark_equality_iff`) and quadratic phases the maximum `|G|²`
(`quadPhase_support_product`) — so a classification of the maximisers is the
exact mirror of the classification of the minimisers, and the same completing-
the-square computation drives both.

*Why now?*  `shifted_gauss_sum_normSq` already performs the completion of the
square in Lean, and `fourier_fourier` supplies the eigenvalue structure of `𝓕`
that pins down the sign.

**Falsification route.** A bi-unimodular function on some `ZMod N` (odd `N`)
that is not a modulated quadratic phase, or a Gauss sum whose sign disagrees
with the `𝓕⁴` prediction.

---

## C5. Extension to compact and to profinite groups

**Conjecture.** `FinAb` embeds in a category `ProAb` of profinite abelian groups
in which `dualFunctor` (now `Hom(−, ℚ/ℤ)`) is still an equivalence onto the
opposite of discrete torsion abelian groups, and the *uncertainty principle
degenerates*: for infinite profinite `G` the inequality
`|G| ≤ |supp f|·|supp 𝓕f|` becomes the statement that a locally constant `f` with
finite support has transform of infinite support.

*The key insight is* that our proof of exactness used the quotient `H ⧸ range f`
as a test object and nothing else; that argument survives verbatim in any
category of abelian groups closed under quotients and subobjects, whereas the
uncertainty argument uses `|G| < ∞` twice (once for the sup-norm maximiser, once
for the inversion normalisation).  The conjecture predicts exactly which of our
theorems survive.

*Why now?*  Mathlib has `PontryaginDual` for topological groups but no
categorical duality; the `InducedCategory` pattern used for `FinAb` transfers
directly, so the infrastructure cost is small and the payoff is a genuinely
infinite-dimensional test of the framework.

**Falsification route.** Exhibit a profinite abelian group whose double dual map
fails to be an isomorphism, or a finitely supported locally constant function on
`ℤ_p` whose transform has finite support.

---

## C6. Rigidity for arbitrary flat kernels (the Hadamard equality case)

**Conjecture.** Let `U : G → H → ℂ` have orthonormal rows and all entries of
modulus exactly `1/√n`, `n = |G| = |H|`.  Then equality
`|supp f| · |supp (Uᵀ f)| = n` for some non-zero `f` forces `U` to be, after
permuting and rescaling rows and columns, a **tensor product of a character
table of a subgroup with an arbitrary flat block**; in particular for `n` prime
equality can occur only if `U` is (equivalent to) the Fourier matrix of `ZMod n`.

*The key insight is* that `donoho_stark_rigidity` never used the group law
directly: it used that the maximiser of `|f|` forces equality in the complex
triangle inequality, which for a flat kernel says that the *ratios* of kernel
entries along `supp f` are constant.  That is a statement about the matrix, not
about `G`, so the group structure produced in the Fourier case must be
recoverable as a *consequence* of equality — this predicts a rigidity theorem
for complex Hadamard matrices.

*Why now?*  `abstract_uncertainty` and `flat_kernel_card_bound` isolate exactly
the two inequalities whose equality cases are needed, and the equality case of
the complex triangle inequality is already proved in `Rigidity.lean`.

**Falsification route.** A `6 × 6` (or larger) complex Hadamard matrix, e.g. in
the Björck–Fröberg or Tao family, together with a non-zero `f` attaining
`|supp f| · |supp (Uᵀ f)| = 6` that is not supported on a coset of a subgroup of
any group structure compatible with `U`.

---

## C7. An uncertainty principle for families of mutually unbiased bases

**Conjecture.** Let `U₁, …, U_m` be pairwise mutually unbiased bases of `ℂⁿ`
(all pairwise coherences equal to `1/√n`, as in `unbiased_uncertainty`).  Then
for every non-zero `f`

`∑_{i=1}^{m} |supp (U_i f)| ≥ m · n^{1/2}` and, more strongly,
`∏_{i=1}^{m} |supp (U_i f)| ≥ n^{m/2}`,

with equality for `m = 2` exactly in the Donoho–Stark extremal family.

*The key insight is* that the two-kernel proof of `abstract_uncertainty` only
ever compares a maximiser of `|f|` with the `ℓ¹` mass of one transform; running
it around a *cycle* `U₁ → U₂ → ⋯ → U_m → U₁` of unbiased bases multiplies the
defects, so the pairwise bound should self-improve to a product bound over the
whole family.

*Why now?*  `unbiased_uncertainty` supplies the base case `m = 2` in exactly the
form needed, and the composition `U_i U_j⁻¹` of two mutually unbiased bases is
again flat, so the induction step is another instance of the same theorem.

**Falsification route.** A complete set of `n + 1` mutually unbiased bases in
dimension `n = 4` and a vector whose support profile violates the product bound.

# Future directions

Concrete, falsifiable conjectures suggested by the formalization in
`Catalog/Logic/ConstructiveAnalysis/` (files `BishopReals.lean`,
`ConstructiveIVT.lean`, `BrouwerianCounterexamples.lean`, `ComputableReals.lean`,
`ConstructiveOrder.lean`, `ConstructiveSup.lean`, `Sharpness.lean`, `RootLocation.lean`).  Each is stated
so that a single Lean proof (or a single counterexample) settles it.

Five earlier conjectures of this list have since been settled inside the project;
they are recorded, with the theorem that settles them, in the last section.

## C6. `k` oracle calls per step cannot beat the ratio `1/(k+1)`

`Bishop.one_query_contraction_gt_half` and
`Bishop.exists_one_query_contraction_lt_half_add` show that the optimal contraction
ratio of a *one-query* located search is the infimum `1/2`, never attained.  The
natural generalization queries the locatedness oracle `k` times per step, at the
pairs `(p + α_i (q−p), p + β_i (q−p))` with `α_1 < β_1 ≤ α_2 < β_2 ≤ … < β_k`, keeping
on the answers the smallest enclosure they certify.

> **Conjecture.** The worst-case contraction factor of any such `k`-query scheme is
> `> 1/(k+1)`, and for every `η > 0` some `k`-query scheme achieves a factor
> `< 1/(k+1) + η`.  In particular the per-oracle-call efficiency
> `(contraction)^(1/k)` tends to `0` as `k → ∞`, i.e. batching queries strictly pays.

Falsifiable: a `k`-query scheme (for a concrete `k`, e.g. `k = 2`) that provably
preserves `Bishop.Enclosing` and contracts by a factor `≤ 1/(k+1)` refutes the first
half; a proof that no `2`-query scheme beats, say, `2/5` refutes the second.

## C7. The cotransitivity threshold of `lt_cotrans` is exactly `6`

`Bishop.Reg.lt_cotrans` decides `x < z` or `z < y` at any index `m` with
`1/(m+1) ≤ gapAt x y n / 8`; the arithmetic of the proof only needs
`1/(m+1) < gapAt x y n / 6`.

> **Conjecture.** `6` is optimal: the hypothesis `1/(m+1) ≤ gapAt x y n / κ` with
> `κ < 6` is insufficient — there are `x, y, z` and indices `n, m` satisfying it for
> which the midpoint test at `m` decides neither `x < z` nor `z < y` — while the
> conclusion of `lt_cotrans` does hold under `1/(m+1) < gapAt x y n / 6`.

Falsifiable: a Lean proof of `lt_cotrans` with a constant `κ < 6` refutes the first
half; an explicit triple defeating the constant `6` refutes the second.

## C8. The canonical bound in `Reg.mul` can be lowered to `⌈|x₀|⌉ + 1`

`Bishop.Reg.bound x = ⌈|x.approx 0|⌉ + 2` is used to choose the index shift in the
definition of multiplication.  Since `|x_n − x_0| ≤ 1/(n+1) + 1 ≤ 2`, with strict
inequality for `n ≥ 1`, only `n = 0` is at issue.

> **Conjecture.** Replacing `bound` by `⌈|x.approx 0|⌉ + 1` still yields a regular
> sequence in `Reg.mul`, and `toReal_mul` continues to hold; the constant `1` is then
> optimal, i.e. `⌈|x.approx 0|⌉` alone fails for some pair of Bishop reals.

Falsifiable: a pair `x, y` for which the sequence defined with `⌈|x.approx 0|⌉ + 1`
violates the regularity inequality refutes the first half; a proof of regularity with
`⌈|x.approx 0|⌉` refutes the second.

## C9. Local non-constancy with modulus `ν` gives root location only through brackets

`Bishop.exists_grid_near_root` locates a genuine root within one mesh, using only the
*sign change* of `f` across a grid cell, and `Bishop.local_nonconstancy_insufficient`
shows a bound on `|f x|` alone cannot locate a root even under local non-constancy.
What remains open is the intermediate, quantitative statement.

> **Conjecture.** If `f` has modulus `ω` on `[a,b]`, `f a ≤ 0 ≤ f b`, and satisfies
> local non-constancy with modulus `ν`, then *every* root of `f` in `[a,b]` is within
> `2 (b−a)/N` of a grid point `k` of the sign-change search of `Bishop.
> exists_grid_near_root`, provided the mesh satisfies `(b−a)/N ≤ ω (ν δ)`; and the
> number of roots of `f` in `[a,b]` is at most `⌈(b−a)/δ⌉` whenever `ν δ > 0`.

Falsifiable: a function with modulus `ω` and local non-constancy modulus `ν` having
two roots closer than `δ` with `ν δ > 0` refutes the second half; a root far from
every bracketing grid point refutes the first.

## Settled inside the project

* **C1 (root modulus `ε/c` is sharp) — proved.**  `Bishop.root_modulus_attained`
  exhibits, for every `c, ε > 0` with `ε/c ≤ 1`, a function with modulus of uniform
  continuity and slope bound `c` having an `ε`-approximate root at distance *exactly*
  `ε/c` from the exact root; `Bishop.no_root_modulus_below_one` shows no constant
  `κ < 1` can replace the factor `1`.
* **C2 (the diagonal shift is necessary) — proved.**
  `Bishop.Reg.unshifted_diagonal_not_regular` exhibits a regular sequence of Bishop
  reals (`Bishop.Reg.diagWitness`, denoting `1/(k+1)` with `k`-alternating error
  signs) whose unshifted diagonal violates regularity already at `m = 0, n = 1`
  (difference `2` against the allowed `3/2`).  For the same family the shifted
  diagonal converges to the correct limit `0`
  (`Bishop.Reg.diagWitness_limit_toReal`).
* **C3 (the ratio `2/3` is optimal for one-query located searches) — refuted.**  The
  general one-query scheme is formalized as `Bishop.searchGen`; it preserves the
  enclosure invariant (`Bishop.searchGen_enclosing`) and contracts by
  `max β (1−α)` (`Bishop.searchGen_width_le`).  `Bishop.trisection_not_optimal`
  instantiates `α = 2/5, β = 1/2`, contracting by `3/5 < 2/3`.  The corrected sharp
  statement is `Bishop.one_query_contraction_gt_half` (every one-query ratio exceeds
  `1/2`) together with `Bishop.exists_one_query_contraction_lt_half_add` (ratios
  arbitrarily close to `1/2` occur), so `1/2` is the unattained infimum.
* **C5 (every shelf root selector oscillates by at least `1` at `0`) — proved.**
  `Bishop.shelf_selector_oscillation_ge_one` shows that for *every* function `r`
  choosing a root of `shelf t` for each `t ∈ [-1,1]` and every `η > 0`, the difference
  `sSup (r '' {|t| ≤ η}) - sInf (r '' {|t| ≤ η})` is at least `1`; the roots are `1`
  for `t > 0` (`Bishop.shelf_root_of_pos`) and `2` for `t < 0`
  (`Bishop.shelf_root_of_neg`), and every root lies in `[1,2]`
  (`Bishop.shelf_root_mem_Icc`).  Selectors do exist classically
  (`Bishop.exists_shelf_root_selector`), so the statement is not vacuous.
* **C4 (Bishop's local non-constancy suffices, with an explicit modulus) — refuted in
  the "small value ⟹ small distance" reading.**
  `Bishop.local_nonconstancy_insufficient` exhibits, for every `δ ∈ (0,2)`, a
  `1`-Lipschitz function on `[0,4]` with a unique root, satisfying local
  non-constancy with the explicit modulus `ν h = h/8`, and a point at distance `2`
  from the root where `|f| ≤ ν δ / 2`.  What does survive without any non-degeneracy
  hypothesis is the bracketing statement `Bishop.exists_grid_near_root`: the
  sign-change grid search returns a grid point within one mesh `(b−a)/N` of a genuine
  root.

# Future Directions — Fitness Landscapes of Mathematical Theories (cycle 1)

The cycle-1 development (`Catalog/Pythagorean/TheoryFitness/`) fixes a
reproducible cost model — a finite corpus, a source-length function, and a
transitive dependency closure charged exactly once — and settles, inside that
model, the finite maximum principle, the dependency-adjusted champion, the exact
composition threshold, the adapter valley, the style-centre theorem, and the
non-existence of a normalisation-free global maximum.  What survived sharpened
the open questions rather than closing them; the five conjectures below are the
ones the proofs single out.

## 1. Canonicity gap conjecture (route-choice hardness)

*In the fixed-route model the champion is the canonical closure
(`canonicalLibrary_is_global_champion`).  Conjecture: with `r ≥ 2` alternative
proof routes per statement, deciding whether a corpus admits a covering library
of dependency-adjusted cost `≤ B` is NP-complete, and the gap between the
canonical-closure heuristic and the true optimum is `Θ(log |corpus|)` in the
worst case.*

**The key insight is** that `two_routes_no_canonical_champion` already exhibits
the exact obstruction: two cost-equal covering closures with empty intersection,
so the covering problem loses its least element the moment routes branch, and
what remains is a weighted set-cover instance in disguise.
Existence itself is not at risk — `min_cost_cover_is_champion` proves a
minimum-cost covering library is still attained with alternative routes — so the
open content is exactly the complexity of finding it.
**Why now?** The fixed-route case is fully proved, so the remaining content is
precisely the combinatorics of route choice — a finite, measurable object that
can be extracted mechanically from any real library's proof terms.

## 2. Sharp reuse threshold for realistic cost models

*The threshold `adapter ≶ shared mass` (`compose_gain_iff_density`) assumes an
additive adapter charge.  Conjecture: for any subadditive adapter cost
`A(s) ≤ c · s^θ` with `θ < 1`, composition of `k` libraries of shared density
`ρ` increases fitness for all `k ≥ k₀(ρ, θ)` with `k₀ = O(ρ^{-1/(1-θ)})`, and
this exponent is optimal.*

**The key insight is** that the exact identity
`cost(library) + k · core = Σ cost(specialist) + core` makes the saving grow
linearly in `k` while a subadditive adapter grows sublinearly, so the crossing
point is determined by a single exponent rather than by the library's contents.
**Why now?** Both sides of the inequality are already formalised and exactly
computable (`cost_library_add_card_core`), so the conjecture reduces to fitting
`θ` on measured interface-adapter sizes.

## 3. Quantitative adapter valleys are universal, not hypothetical

*`adapter_valley` derives a relative overshoot `(α − β)/(1 + β)` from an assumed
adapter law.  Conjecture: in any real corpus, the adapter law holds with
`α ≥ 1/4` and endpoint efficiency `β ≤ 1/10`, so every semantics-preserving
migration across an interface boundary has intermediate source-length overhead
of at least `15%` of the smaller endpoint.*

**The key insight is** that the combinatorial half of the statement is now
unconditional — `exists_boundary_crossing` shows a crossing step always exists —
so the entire empirical burden is the single constant `α` measured on
cross-interface transitions.
**Why now?** The theorem reduces measurement from all intermediate states of all
paths to one class of transitions, and the computed instance shows the bound is
attained, so any measured `α` immediately yields a falsifiable numeric floor.

## 4. Metastability requires only bounded style leakage

*The style-centre theorem needs either closed neighbourhoods or strictly worse
cross-style neighbours (`strictLocalMax_of_quarantine`).  Conjecture: there is a
leakage constant `λ > 0` such that any migration graph in which at most a
`λ`-fraction of each vertex's neighbourhood crosses styles still contains at
least three strict local maxima, one per style, after quotienting by renaming;
and `λ` can be taken independent of corpus size.*

**The key insight is** that quarantine is a purely local condition, and
`strictLocalMax_of_renaming` shows the whole notion is stable under
semantics-preserving renaming, so the quotient step costs nothing and only the
leakage fraction remains to be bounded.
**Why now?** The two hypotheses are now provably independent, so each can be
measured separately on a finite corpus without re-deriving the other.

## 5. Normalisation dichotomy is exhaustive

*`normalization_dichotomy` shows maxima always exist on finite classes and never
on the unrestricted class.  Conjecture: for a comparison class `C` closed under
the inflation operator, a global fitness maximum exists **iff** `C` bounds the
theorem-to-content ratio; i.e. resource normalisation is not merely sufficient
but necessary, and "bounded content-adjusted redundancy" is the unique minimal
hypothesis making the champion question well posed.*

**The key insight is** that the divergent family produced by
`unbounded_witnesses_are_semantically_inert` is semantically constant, so the
only quantity distinguishing it from genuine progress is redundancy relative to
semantic content — which suggests redundancy, not size, is the correct
normaliser.
**Why now?** The two halves of the dichotomy are proved, so the remaining task is
exactly to show no weaker hypothesis suffices — a single, sharp, falsifiable
statement.

## Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. **Submodular closure cost.** The map `s ↦ cost(closure of s)` is modular on
   dependency-closed sets (proved: `cost_merge_add_cost_inter`) but is
   conjectured *strictly submodular* on arbitrary generating sets; if so, greedy
   library construction is a `(1 − 1/e)`-approximation of the champion.
2. **Candidate-count phase transition.** Between the exponential `2^n`
   (independent) and linear `n + 1` (chain) baselines, the number of usable
   sub-libraries of a random dependency DAG with edge density `p` is conjectured
   to be `exp(Θ(n / (1 + pn)))`, with the crossover at `p ≍ 1/n`.
3. **Fitness-preserving refactoring is a groupoid.** The renaming equivariance
   `strictLocalMax_of_renaming` should extend to a groupoid action whose orbits
   are exactly the fitness level sets; if so, the migration graph descends to a
   finite quotient on which "distinct strict local maxima" is decidable.

# Future Directions — Hadwiger's Conjecture (cycle v19c, continuation pass)

What is now formalised (all statements below are `sorry`-free theorems in
`Catalog/Probability/Hadwiger*.lean`):

* transitivity of the minor relation (`isMinor_trans`), the law the catalog's
  `MinorModel.lean` left open;
* Hadwiger's conjecture for `k ≤ 2`, for finite graphs and — with no finiteness
  hypothesis at all — for arbitrary vertex types (`hadwiger_gen_two`);
* the excluded-minor characterisation of forests
  (`completeMinor_three_iff_not_isAcyclic`), i.e. forests = K₃-minor-free
  graphs;
* antitonicity in `k` (`hadwiger_monotone`), the reduction to connected graphs
  (`hadwigerProperty_of_connected`), and the reduction of the infinite case to
  the finite case by de Bruijn–Erdős compactness
  (`hadwigerPropertyGen_of_hadwigerProperty`);
* the Wagner reformulation `HadwigerProperty 4 ↔ every K₅-minor-free finite
  graph is 4-colourable`, with the deep inputs (Wagner's structure theorem, the
  Four Colour Theorem) carried as explicit named hypotheses, never assumed;
* failure of the converse (`chromaticNumber_not_minorMonotone`, witness `C₆`);
* the sharp extremal bound for the excluded minor `K₃` (`|E| ≤ |V| − 1`, edge
  density `< 1`) and its contrapositive "`|V| ≤ |E|` forces a `K₃` minor";
* a Bonferroni inequality for the catalog `G(n,p)` model and the bound
  `2p³ − p⁶ ≤ P(K₃ ≼ G(n,p))` for `n ≥ 6`.

Added in the continuation pass (`HadwigerCritical.lean`, `HadwigerCardTwo.lean`,
`HadwigerCriticalEquiv.lean`), again all `sorry`-free:

* **colour-critical subgraphs have large minimum degree**
  (`exists_subset_minDegree_of_not_colorable`): every finite graph that is not
  `k`-colourable contains a vertex subset in which *every* vertex has at least
  `k` neighbours — proved by a greedy re-colouring of a minimal
  non-`k`-colourable subset;
* the resulting **minimum-degree reduction**
  (`hadwigerProperty_of_minDegree_forces`): the statement "minimum degree `k`
  forces a `K_{k+1}` minor" implies `HadwigerProperty k`.  Instantiated at
  `k = 2` (`completeMinor_three_of_two_le_degree`, proved from the sharp
  `K₃`-density bound plus the handshake lemma) it gives an independent proof
  `hadwiger_two_via_min_degree`; at `k = 3` it isolates Dirac's theorem as the
  single remaining input (`hadwiger_three_of_dirac`);
* the classical **edge bound for `(k+1)`-chromatic graphs**
  (`mul_succ_le_two_mul_card_edgeFinset_of_not_colorable`): `|E| ≥ k(k+1)/2`,
  sharp on `K_{k+1}`;
* **Hadwiger's conjecture for all graphs with at most `k + 2` vertices**
  (`hadwiger_of_card_le_add_two`), for every `k` including the open range
  `k ≥ 5`.  One vertex past the previously known `k + 1` bound the graph need no
  longer be complete; the proof shows instead that all non-edges pass through a
  single vertex (`exists_clique_of_not_colorable_card_add_two`);
* the **minimum-degree equivalence** (`hadwigerProperty_iff_minDegree`): adding
  non-`k`-colourability to the minimum-degree hypothesis turns the reduction
  above into a genuine equivalence — the conjecture need only be checked on
  non-`k`-colourable graphs of minimum degree at least `k`;
* the **vertex-critical reduction** (`hadwigerProperty_iff_critical`):
  `HadwigerProperty k` holds iff it holds for graphs that are not
  `k`-colourable but become so after deleting any single vertex.  This is the
  vertex-critical half of what was Conjecture 4 below, now a theorem.

The following five conjectures are the concrete, falsifiable next steps.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Dirac's case, `k = 3`): min-degree 3 forces a `K₄` minor

**Statement.** `HadwigerProperty 3` : every finite graph that is not
3-colourable has a `K₄` minor. Equivalently (and this is the shape to
formalise): every finite graph with minimum degree at least 3 contains a `K₄`
minor, and every 4-chromatic graph has a subgraph of minimum degree 3.

**Status after this pass.** The reduction half is *done*: `HadwigerProperty 3`
now follows formally from the single hypothesis "every finite graph of minimum
degree at least `3` has a `K₄` minor" (`hadwiger_three_of_dirac`), because every
4-chromatic graph provably has a subgraph of minimum degree `3`
(`exists_subset_minDegree_of_not_colorable`).  What remains is exactly Dirac's
1963 theorem.

**The key insight is** that the remaining statement is *purely local*: no
colouring occurs in it any more, only a minimum-degree hypothesis, so it can be
attacked by the branch-set construction directly (a longest path, its endpoint's
three neighbours, and the three path segments they cut out) rather than through
a colouring induction.

**Why now?** The `k = 2` analogue is already a theorem here
(`completeMinor_three_of_two_le_degree`) and was proved by exactly this
route — extremal bound plus handshake — so the pattern to imitate at `k = 3` is
the `K₄` density bound of Conjecture 2. Exhaustive computation
(`ComputationalEvidence.md`) confirms no counterexample on ≤ 5 vertices.

**Falsifiable by:** a finite graph with χ ≥ 4 and no `K₄` minor.

---

## Conjecture 2: `K_{k+1}`-minor-free graphs are `O(k √(log k))`-degenerate

**Statement.** There is an absolute constant `C` such that every finite graph
with no `K_{k+1}` minor has a vertex of degree at most `C k √(log k)`; hence
such graphs are `C k √(log k)`-colourable. (Kostochka–Thomason.) A first,
fully self-contained target is the weaker but unconditional bound: a graph with
no `K_{k+1}` minor has at most `2^{k-1}(|V| - 1)` edges, hence a vertex of degree
< `2^k`, hence is `2^k`-colourable.

**The key insight is** that minor-freeness is an *edge-density* statement, and
density bounds are proved by contracting a shortest edge — a move for which the
branch-set model of `MinorModel.lean` plus `isMinor_trans` is precisely the
right formal interface.

The case `k = 2` of this programme is now a theorem here:
`card_edgeSet_add_one_le_of_no_K3_minor` gives the sharp bound `|E| ≤ |V| − 1`
for `K₃`-minor-free graphs, with the contrapositive
`completeMinor_three_of_card_le_card_edgeSet` ("`|V| ≤ |E|` forces a `K₃`
minor"). The first open target is the `K₄` analogue `|E| ≤ 2|V| − 3`; together
with the new lower bound `|E| ≥ k(k+1)/2` for `(k+1)`-chromatic graphs
(`mul_succ_le_two_mul_card_edgeFinset_of_not_colorable`) this would pin the
`k = 3` case between two explicit edge counts.

**Why now?** With `isMinor_trans` and `minorFree_minorClosed` proved, an
induction that contracts one edge at a time stays inside the formal framework,
which was the missing piece; nothing deeper than counting is required for the
exponential version.

**Falsifiable by:** a `K_{k+1}`-minor-free graph with more than `2^{k-1}(n-1)`
edges.

---

## Conjecture 3: the `K₃`-minor threshold in `G(n,p)` is `p = 1/n`

**Statement.** For `p = c/n` with `c < 1` fixed, `P(K₃ ≼ G(n,p))` stays bounded
away from `1`; for `c > 1` it tends to `1`. Formally, the proved event identity
`hasK3Minor = hasCycle` reduces this to the classical cycle threshold, and the
second-moment machinery of `ErdosRenyiMoments.lean` should deliver the upper
half.

**The key insight is** that the topological event "`K₃` is a minor" is *not* an
approximation of the combinatorial event "contains a triangle" — it is exactly
the cycle event, so its threshold is `1/n`, not `n^{-1}` in the subgraph sense
(`n^{-1}` for triangles as subgraphs happens to coincide, but the constants and
the limit laws differ, and only the minor version has a sharp `0/1` law at
`c = 1`).

**Why now?** `bonferroni_two` gives second-order lower bounds in the catalog
model for the first time, and `two_triangle_bound` shows how disjoint
structures combine; extending from two triangles to `⌊n/3⌋` disjoint triangles
gives `1 − (1 − p³)^{n/3}` and already crosses the `1/n` regime.

**Falsifiable by:** a proof that `P(K₃ ≼ G(n, c/n)) → 1` for some `c < 1`.

---

## Conjecture 4: Hadwiger's conjecture holds for all graphs with `|V| ≤ k + 3`

**Statement.** Every finite graph `G` with at most `k + 3` vertices that is not
`k`-colourable contains `K_{k+1}` as a minor — one vertex beyond the theorem
`hadwiger_of_card_le_add_two` proved in this pass.

**The key insight is** that on `k + 2` vertices non-`k`-colourability forces the
complement to be a *star* (no independent triple, no two disjoint non-edges), so
deleting one vertex leaves a clique; on `k + 3` vertices the complement instead
has no `K₄`, no disjoint triangle-plus-edge and no perfect `3`-matching, and the
Gallai–Edmonds structure of graphs with matching number `≤ 2` should again leave
a `K_{k+1}` minor after contracting two complement-independent edges of `G`.

**Why now?** The `k + 2` case is now formal, and its proof is exactly the
matching-number-`≤ 1` instance of the same analysis; the branch sets needed for
`k + 3` are of size at most two, so `completeMinor_of_branches` applies verbatim.

**Falsifiable by:** a graph on `k + 3` vertices with χ ≥ k+1 and no `K_{k+1}`
minor.  (Any such graph would also refute Hadwiger's conjecture itself.)

**Beyond the vertex-critical reduction.** The original Conjecture 4 of this
thread — that Hadwiger's conjecture may be checked on critical graphs only — is
now a theorem in its vertex-critical form (`hadwigerProperty_iff_critical`).
The remaining, strictly stronger version asks for the same equivalence with
*contraction-critical* graphs (every proper **minor** is `k`-colourable), for
which one needs a well-founded order on minors rather than on vertex subsets.

---

## Conjecture 5: the odd-minor strengthening for `k = 2`

**Statement.** Every graph that is not 2-colourable contains `K₃` as an *odd*
minor (branch sets with a 2-colouring under which all branch-set-internal edges
are bichromatic and all connecting edges monochromatic). More generally
(Gerards–Seymour), `χ(G) ≥ k+1` implies `K_{k+1}` is an odd minor of `G`.

**The key insight is** that our `k = 2` proof already produces the branch sets
from an *odd* cycle (a non-2-colourable graph has one), so the odd-minor
refinement should come out of the same construction with a parity bookkeeping
layer, giving the first formalised case of a conjecture strictly stronger than
Hadwiger's.

**Why now?** Mathlib's `IsAcyclic.isBipartite` and the odd-cycle
characterisation of non-bipartite graphs are available, and our contraction
lemma `completeMinor_three_of_triple` takes arbitrary branch sets, so the parity
data can be threaded through without redoing the construction.

**Falsifiable by:** a non-bipartite graph with no odd `K₃` minor.
