# Future Directions (cycle 1 of thread th_2130c620)

The five conjectures inherited from cycle 0 have now been formalised and proved in a precise
model (see `Catalog/Novelty/MultiwaySortingRadix.lean`, `SortingDirectSum.lean`,
`SortingFluctuationPenalty.lean`, `PriorSensitiveSorting.lean`).  What follows are the
*next* conjectures, each derived from a gap that only became visible after those proofs.

## 1. Semantic realisability of transcript profiles (the comparison-availability gap)

**Conjecture.** Let `A(n, q)` be the set of transcript maps realisable by *adaptive
comparison* algorithms, where the `k`-th query is a function of the previous answers and is
one of the `q`-outcome order queries on `n` items.  Then `A(n, q)` is strictly smaller than
the set of injective maps `Perm (Fin n) → Fin d → Fin q` for every `q ≥ 3` and every
`d < ⌈log_q (n!)⌉ + c` with an absolute constant `c ≥ 1`, and the exact minimal adaptive
depth exceeds the counting bound `⌈log_q (n!)⌉` for infinitely many `(n, q)`.

The key insight is that our proved lower bound `Sorter.clog_le_depth` uses only injectivity,
whereas realisable transcripts must additionally be *consistent*: the fibre of any prefix of
a transcript is an order ideal cut out by the queries asked so far, and multiway order
queries cannot split a permutation class into `q` arbitrary pieces. **Why now?** The counting
bound is proved and its achievability (`exists_sorter_clog_depth`) is proved to hold in the
*abstract* transcript model, so the gap between the two models is now a sharply posed,
finitely testable question for small `(n, q)`.

## 2. Uncomputation quantifies the equality case of the direct-sum theorem

**Conjecture.** For block sorting, define the *garbage index* of a reversible protocol as
`|Aux| / (m!·n!)`.  Then the minimal number of elementary uncomputation steps needed to
bring a protocol to the garbage-free case is `Θ(log (garbage index))`, and the class of
protocols with garbage index `1` is exactly the class characterised by
`block_history_equality_iff_no_garbage` — i.e. bijectivity of the history map is not only
necessary and sufficient but *quantitatively stable*: a protocol within a factor `1 + ε` of
the minimum has history map surjective on a `(1 − ε)`-fraction of `Aux`.

The key insight is that our equality theorem is an all-or-nothing pigeonhole statement, while
`block_history_strict_of_garbage` shows the failure mode is a cardinality defect that should
carry a metric, not just a boolean. **Why now?** Both endpoints (equality iff bijective, and
strictness under non-surjectivity) are proved, so the interpolating stability statement is
the only missing piece and is falsifiable on `(m, n) = (3, 2)` by exhaustive search.

## 3. A fluctuation–depth uncertainty relation

**Conjecture.** For a finite-time sorting protocol executing `d` binary comparisons with
per-comparison relaxation time `τ`, the dissipation identity
`⟨W⟩ − F = kT · D(p ‖ p^R)` (proved, `dissipated_work_eq_relEntropy`) is bounded below by
`kT · Var(W) / (2 (kT)² + C d τ⁻¹)`, so that the *product* of the excess work and the total
protocol time `dτ` is bounded below by an absolute multiple of `Var(W)`.

The key insight is that our proof extracts the excess from the strict `log x ≤ x − 1` defect
at each trajectory; second-order expansion of that defect converts the divergence into a
variance, which is the quantity a finite-time protocol cannot suppress. **Why now?** The
exact divergence identity removes all ambiguity about the equilibrium term, so any
speed-versus-dissipation trade-off must live entirely in the second-order remainder, which is
already isolated in the proof.

## 4. Prior-sensitive history is incompressible below the entropy, even with side information

**Conjecture.** Let `p` be a prior on orderings and let the sorter be allowed a free
side-information register correlated with the input (a "catalyst" that must be returned
unchanged).  Then the expected retained history is still at least `H(p)` bits, and equality
holds iff the prior is dyadic; in particular catalysts cannot beat
`PriorSorter.entropy_le_expectedComparisons`, and the one-comparison slack of
`exists_priorSorter_within_one_comparison` is unavoidable for non-dyadic priors.

The key insight is that a returned-unchanged catalyst cannot change the Kraft budget of the
transcript code, so the Shannon bound should survive verbatim, while the sharp equality case
(dyadic priors) is the equality case already isolated in the catalog's
`expected_length_eq_entropy_iff`. **Why now?** The prior-sensitive floor and its
one-comparison achievability are both proved, so the only remaining question is whether
auxiliary correlated resources move the floor — a clean yes/no with a concrete dyadic
boundary.

## 5. Radix-mixing and the optimal query alphabet

**Conjecture.** Allow the `k`-th query to have its own radix `q_k`.  Then the minimal
"mixed-radix depth vector" for sorting `n` items satisfies `∏_k q_k ≥ n!`, the ideal work
`kT ∑_k log q_k` is minimised exactly when `∏_k q_k` is the smallest product of the allowed
radices exceeding `n!`, and the resulting minimum work exceeds `kT log (n!)` by strictly less
than `kT log (max_k q_k)` — a strict improvement over the fixed-radix sandwich
`optimal_radix_work_sandwich` whenever `n!` is not a power of a single allowed radix.

The key insight is that the fixed-radix sandwich loses up to one full query register because
`⌈log_q n!⌉` overshoots; mixing radices makes the overshoot a number-theoretic approximation
problem for `n!` by products from a fixed multiplicative set. **Why now?** The fixed-radix
theorem gives the exact baseline and the exact loss term, so the mixed-radix optimum is a
well-posed integer-programming question that can be solved exactly for `n ≤ 8`.

# Future directions

The formalisation in `Catalog/Algebra/PosetFlow/` develops the combinatorial core of
*the chain replacement of a poset flow*: the refinement poset `ChainFrom x y` of
strictly increasing chains, its cone structure, the concatenation (flow composition)
law, the behaviour under order-reflecting inclusions, and the Euler-characteristic
invariants (Philip Hall's theorem, the Möbius function as reduced Euler
characteristic of an open interval).

The following conjectures are the concrete next steps suggested by what the
formalisation established — and by what it could *not* yet reach.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Nerve contractibility upgrade)

*For every finite poset `R` with a cone point, the simplicial nerve of `R`
(`CategoryTheory.nerve` of `R` viewed as a category) is a contractible simplicial
set; consequently, for `x ≤ y` in a finite poset, the nerve of `ChainFrom x y` is
contractible and the chain replacement of a poset flow is a genuine q-cofibrant
replacement.*

The key insight is that the involution `C ↦ C △ {z}` that proves the vanishing of
the alternating face sum (`alternatingSum_orderComplex_eq_zero_of_conePoint`) is the
shadow of an explicit simplicial homotopy `Δ¹ × N(R) → N(R)` contracting `N(R)` onto
the cone point, so the numerical statement already proved is the Euler
characteristic of a homotopy that can be written down face by face.

Why now? Mathlib now has `SSet`, `nerve`, and simplicial homotopies, so the
contracting homotopy can be defined directly and its two ends identified; the
combinatorial bookkeeping — precisely the chain manipulations proved here — is the
part that usually blocks such a formalisation, and it is now available.

Falsifiable: exhibiting a finite poset with a cone point whose nerve has a
nontrivial homotopy group would refute it.

---

## Conjecture 2 (Fibrewise product formula for the trace)

*Let `f : P ↪o Q` be order-reflecting and `x y : P`. For every `D : ChainFrom x y`
the fibre `{E : ChainFrom (f x) (f y) // trace f E = D}` is isomorphic, as a poset,
to the product over the covering pairs `(u, v)` of `D` of the posets of chains from
`f u` to `f v` whose interior misses the image of `P`.*

The key insight is that the Galois coinsertion `chainGaloisCoinsertion` already
splits the chain poset of `Q` into a lower set (the image of `P`) and its
complement, and the two-step version of the splitting is exactly the order
isomorphism `chainSplitOrderIso`; the general statement should follow by induction
on the cardinality of `D` using that isomorphism at each cut point.

Why now? Both halves of the induction are formalised and sorry-free, so the only
missing ingredient is an indexing scheme for covering pairs of a finite chain —
routine but currently absent.

Falsifiable: a finite order-reflecting inclusion and a chain `D` where the fibre has
a cardinality different from the product would refute it.

---

## Conjecture 3 (Möbius vanishing from local cones is not exhaustive)

*The vanishing criterion `mu_eq_zero_of_conePoint_openInterval` is strictly weaker
than the vanishing of `μ`: there exist finite posets with `μ(x, y) = 0` where the
open interval `(x, y)` has no cone point, but every such interval has a
"contractible-but-not-conical" order complex; equivalently, for finite posets the
implication "`μ(x,y) = 0` ⟹ `Δ(x,y)` is `ℤ`-acyclic" is **false**.*

The key insight is that `μ(x, y)` sees only the Euler characteristic, so any interval
whose order complex has cancelling homology in different degrees (the smallest
candidates come from triangulations of the dunce hat or from the poset of a
non-shellable complex) will have `μ = 0` without being acyclic.

Why now? The bridge `alternatingSum_openInterval_eq_neg_mu` between `μ` and the
order complex is now formal, so the search for a separating example is a finite,
decidable computation over small posets that can be run inside Lean.

Falsifiable by construction: exhibit and verify one explicit finite poset.

---

## Conjecture 4 (Homotopy-invariance of the Galois coinsertion)

*If `l : A → B` and `u : B → A` form a Galois (co)insertion between finite posets,
then the induced maps of order complexes are homotopy inverse; in particular the
alternating face sums of `A` and `B` agree.*

The key insight is the classical fact that adjoint monotone maps are homotopic to
each other through the unit/counit, so `l` and `u` induce mutually inverse maps up
to homotopy; the Euler-characteristic consequence is a purely combinatorial identity
that should be provable by the same involution technique used in this development.

Why now? `chainGaloisCoinsertion` supplies a large and natural family of examples
(one for each order-reflecting inclusion of finite posets and each pair of points),
so the statement can be stress-tested computationally before being proved.

Falsifiable: two finite posets in Galois coinsertion with different alternating face
sums.

---

## Conjecture 5 (Ordered-Bell asymptotics of the chain replacement)

*For the Boolean lattice `Bₙ`, the number of elements of `ChainFrom ⊥ ⊤` is the
ordered Bell number `aₙ` (OEIS A000670), and more generally for any finite poset `P`
the total number of chains is `∑_{x ≤ y} |ChainFrom x y| = ∑_{k} c_k`, whose
alternating version is `-∑_{x ≤ y} μ(x, y)`; hence the "size" of the chain
replacement of a poset flow is controlled by the Möbius invariant of the poset.*

The key insight is that Hall's theorem, now formal, converts every counting
statement about chains into a statement about the incidence algebra, where
multiplicative structure (products of posets, `mu_prod_mu`) is available.

Why now? The evidence file already exhibits the values `1, 3, 13` for `n = 1, 2, 3`,
matching A000670, and Mathlib's incidence algebra provides the product formulas
needed for an inductive proof.

Falsifiable: a value of `|ChainFrom ⊥ ⊤|` for some `Bₙ` differing from `aₙ`.

# Future Directions (thread th_ffe6cbbf)

State of the thread after the present cycle.  Every statement marked "**settled**"
is a sorry-free Lean 4 theorem in `Catalog/Probability/`, checked against the
project's Mathlib pin; the main theorems depend only on `propext`,
`Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

## What is settled

* **Quantitative Copycat stability.** The exact modulus is *geometric*, not linear:
  `|⟦φ⟧_M s − ⟦φ⟧_N (f s)| ≤ 1 − (1−ε)^{depth φ}` (`PModalStructure.transport_le`),
  attained by an explicit two-state leaking family (`Sharp.transport_eq`).  The
  conjectured linear bound `d·ε` follows but is never attained for `d ≥ 2`
  (`linear_bound_not_attained`), while being sharp to first order in `ε`
  (`linear_bound_first_order_sharp`).
* **Groupoid structure.** Approximate analogies compose with additive total variation
  defect (`ApproxAnalogy.refl/symm/comp`, `overlapDefect_eq_half_l1`), with a
  semantic holonomy bound for two-step loops (`holonomy_bound`).
* **Networks.** Along a chain of analogies with local defects `ε_i` the defects add
  and the transport modulus is `1 − (1 − Σ_{i<k} ε_i)^d`
  (`Network.network_transport_le`); for a cycle this bounds the semantic holonomy
  (`Network.loop_holonomy_bound`), exact cycles have trivial holonomy
  (`Network.loop_holonomy_trivial`), and any meaning factoring through the modal
  theory of a world is globally coherent around an exact cycle
  (`Network.meaning_invariant_of_trivial_holonomy`).
* **Approximate Hennessy–Milner.** For nominal structures the naming bijection is
  forced (`Resolution.nominal_analogy_eq`); `η`-agreement on the depth-one fragment
  yields an `(nη/2)`-approximate analogy (`Resolution.nominalApproxAnalogy`) and
  hence the modulus `1 − (1 − nη/2)^d` (`Resolution.nominal_approx_transport`), with
  the dimension factor `n/2` optimal (`Resolution.HMSharp.hm_sharp`).
* **Resolution gap.** Two 2-world systems are modally identical but admit no analogy
  of defect `< 1` (`Resolution.resolution_gap`).

### Settled this cycle

* **The analogy distance is an attained metric** (`Catalog/Probability/AnalogyMetric.lean`).
  `analogyDist M N` — the least defect of an approximate structural analogy — is
  realized as a minimum over the finitely many atom-preserving renamings
  (`optimalAnalogy`), so `∃ ApproxAnalogy M N ε ↔ analogyDist M N ≤ ε`
  (`analogyDist_le_iff`).  It satisfies the metric axioms (`analogyDist_self`,
  `analogyDist_comm`, `analogyDist_triangle`, all read off from the groupoid
  operations), lies in `[0,1]` (`analogyDist_mem_Icc`), and its zero set is exactly
  isomorphism (`analogyDist_eq_zero_iff`), so it is a genuine metric on isomorphism
  classes.  Depth-`d` truth probabilities are `1 − (1 − d(M,N))^d`-continuous with
  the optimal renaming (`optimal_transport_le`), and the constant is exact:
  `Sharp.dist_eq` computes `d(exactSys, leakySys ε) = ε` for the extremal family,
  which attains the modulus.  This closes Conjecture 3 of the previous cycle.
* **Graded modalities do not close the resolution gap** — a *refutation*
  (`Catalog/Probability/GradedResolution.lean`).  With the counting semantics
  `gsat` ("at least `k` successors of positive probability satisfy `φ`"), graded
  truth is invariant under exact analogies (`gsat_transport`), but it is *blind on
  deterministic systems*: any two deterministic constant-atom systems, on arbitrary
  finite world sets and with arbitrary successor functions, satisfy exactly the same
  graded formulas at every pair of worlds (`det_graded_iff`).  Hence "two self-loops"
  and "one 2-cycle" are graded-equivalent yet non-isomorphic (`gap_persists`): a
  finite language of graded modalities does **not** classify finite pointed models up
  to isomorphism, refuting Conjecture 1 of the root direction and the `k = 1`
  separation claim of Conjecture 4.  What does separate the pair is the
  self-reference observation `0 < step s s` (`loopObs`), which is itself invariant
  under exact analogies (`loopObs_transport`, `loop_separates`) — the missing
  resolution is a fixed-point phenomenon, not a multiplicity phenomenon.

## Next falsifiable steps

### 1. Fixed-point rank is the right resolution dial

**Conjecture.** Extend the graded language by the observations `loop_m` = "the
`m`-step return probability at the current world is positive", `m ≥ 1`.  Then for
deterministic finite systems the resulting language classifies pointed systems up to
isomorphism, the level `m` is needed exactly for systems whose reachable cycle has
length `m`, and the resulting hierarchy is strict at every level.

The key insight is that `det_graded_iff` shows counting successors carries no
information in the deterministic world, while `loop_separates` shows a single
self-reference observation already splits the smallest confused pair; the invariant
that survives is the cycle type of the successor function.

**Why now?** Both endpoints are theorems: blindness of grading at every level and
separation by the `m = 1` loop observation, so only the uniform construction and the
strictness examples remain.

### 2. `analogyDist` is a *geodesic* metric, and the modulus is exactly its arc length

**Conjecture.** On finite probabilistic systems with a fixed world set and fixed
valuation, `analogyDist` is a geodesic metric: for every pair `M, N` and every
`θ ∈ [0,1]` there is `K` with `d(M,K) = θ·d(M,N)` and `d(K,N) = (1−θ)·d(M,N)`;
moreover the transport modulus `1 − (1−ε)^d` is exactly the arc length of the induced
path in the space of depth-`d` observation vectors.

The key insight is that `analogyDist` is a max over worlds of total variation
distances, and total variation interpolates linearly along kernel segments
`(1−θ)·step_M + θ·step_N`, so the optimal renaming can be kept fixed along the whole
segment.

**Why now?** `analogyDist_le_iff` makes the distance a minimum over a finite set, so
candidate geodesics can be exhibited concretely, and `analogyDist_triangle` supplies
the inequality that a geodesic must saturate.

### 3. The distance is computable, and the optimal renaming is not always unique

**Conjecture.** `analogyDist` is computable in time `O(n! · n²)` and no better in
general: deciding `analogyDist M N ≤ ε` is as hard as graph isomorphism for the
`0/1`-valued kernels, while for kernels with pairwise distinct row profiles the
optimal renaming is unique and computable in `O(n² log n)`.

The key insight is that `analogyDist_eq_zero_iff` identifies the zero set with
isomorphism, so any subexponential algorithm would give a subexponential
isomorphism test for the corresponding digraphs; conversely distinct row profiles pin
the renaming exactly as the nominal atoms do in `Resolution.nominal_analogy_eq`.

**Why now?** The distance is now a finite minimum with a proven characterization of
its zero set, which is precisely the reduction interface needed.

### 4. Networks: the sharp per-cycle constant is sub-additive

**Conjecture.** For a cycle of analogies with local defects `ε_e`, the sharp holonomy
constant is strictly below `1 − (1 − Σ_e ε_e)^d` whenever two consecutive defects are
supported on overlapping world pairs, and equals it exactly when the supports are
pairwise disjoint; `analogyDist` of the composite is then the correct sharp constant.

The key insight is that `Network.chainAnalogy` adds total variation defects, which is
tight only for disjointly supported defects, and `analogyDist` now provides the
*exact* composite defect against which additivity can be measured.

**Why now?** With `analogyDist` available, the conjecture becomes the concrete
statement `analogyDist M K ≤ analogyDist M N + analogyDist N K` with an explicit
description of the equality case — a finite, checkable condition.

### 5. Quantitative graded transport

**Conjecture.** Graded truth is *not* stable: for every `ε > 0` there are systems at
analogy distance `ε` whose graded theories differ already at grade `1` and depth `1`;
but the *ε-relaxed* graded modality "at least `k` successors of probability `> ε`
satisfy `φ`" is transported along ε-approximate analogies with no error at all.

The key insight is that positivity of a transition is a discontinuous functional of
the kernel, so exact grading cannot be stable, while thresholding at the defect level
restores invariance because a defect of `ε` can move at most `ε` of mass.

**Why now?** `gsat_transport` proves the exact (`ε = 0`) case, and the total variation
identity `overlapDefect_eq_half_l1` gives the precise mass-movement budget needed for
the thresholded version.

# Future directions — adjacency-degree algebras and moment rigidity

The formal development lives in `Catalog/Physics/AdjacencyDegree/` (13 files, all compiling,
no `sorry`, axioms `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only).  What is *proved* there:

* the cyclic module `M_G = 𝓐(G)𝟏` sits inside the orbit module `U_G`, and equals the span of
  `𝟏` exactly for regular graphs (`Basic.lean`);
* word moments `𝟏ᵀ w(A,D) 𝟏` are isomorphism invariants and are degree-decorated caterpillar
  homomorphism counts (`Moments.lean`, `Caterpillar.lean`);
* moment equality forces equality of the degree distribution, of the joint degree
  distribution, and — the general form — of **every** degree-decorated walk count
  (`DegreeRecovery.lean`, `EdgeStatistics.lean`, `WalkStatistics.lean`);
* conversely those walk counts recover all the moments, so the two invariants have exactly the
  same strength (`CaterpillarRigidity.lean`);
* moments only see the colour-refinement quotient (`Equitable.lean`, `Quotient.lean`), hence
  fail on regular graphs (`RegularFailure.lean`) and already on a connected non-regular
  six-vertex pair (`SixVertexWitness.lean`);
* `M_G = U_G` for stars and for degree-transitive graphs (`OrbitEquality.lean`), and the
  `J`-ideal moments factorise (`Synthesis.lean`).

The following conjectures are the natural next targets.  Each is falsifiable: a single
counterexample refutes it, and each is stated so that a Lean formalisation can be attempted
directly against the definitions already in the catalog.

---

## Conjecture 1 (McKay's principal form). Moments determine every tree.

If `T₁`, `T₂` are trees with `wordMoment T₁ w = wordMoment T₂ w` for all words `w` in `{A, D}`,
then `T₁ ≃g T₂`.

*Status.* Proved here for stars (`starGraph_iso_of_moments`); verified by exhaustive
enumeration for all trees on at most 9 vertices (`ComputationalEvidence.md`, exploratory).

*The key insight is* that by `CaterpillarRigidity.wordMoment_eq_iff_degWalkCount_eq` the moment
invariant is exactly the family of degree-decorated caterpillar counts, so the statement is a
purely combinatorial reconstruction problem: rebuild a tree from the number of walks realising
each prescribed degree pattern, peeling leaves by their decorated pattern multiplicities.

*Why now?* The reduction from linear algebra to walk counts is now a theorem rather than a
heuristic, and the leaf-peeling induction needs no new analytic input — only the counts that
are already proved to be invariants.

---

## Conjecture 2 (Forest module identity). `M_G = U_G` for every forest.

For every forest `F`, the cyclic module `cyclicModule F` coincides with the orbit module
`orbitModule F`.

*Status.* Proved here for stars and for degree-transitive graphs; the general forest case is
open in this development.

*The key insight is* that in a forest the iterated degree refinement (`Equitable.lean`) already
stabilises at the automorphism-orbit partition, so the inclusion `M_G ≤ U_G` proved in
`cyclicModule_le_orbitModule` should be reversible by exhibiting, for each orbit, an explicit
polynomial in `A` and `D` whose value on `𝟏` is the orbit indicator — a construction that
`degIndicator_mem_cyclicModule` already carries out one degree class at a time.

*Why now?* The inclusion and the degree-class indicators are formalised, so only the
refinement-stabilises-at-orbits step is missing, and it is exactly the acyclicity input.

---

## Conjecture 3 (Exact characterisation). Moment equality ⇔ common colour-refinement quotient.

Two graphs on the same number of vertices have equal adjacency-degree word moments **iff** their
colour-refinement (1-WL) quotients, weighted by class sizes, are isomorphic.

*Status.* The "if" direction is proved (`Quotient.wordMoment_eq_of_quot_eq`); the "only if"
direction is open.

*The key insight is* that the moments are linear functionals of the quotient data, and the
quotient matrix has full-rank Krylov structure on the class-size vector, so recovering the
quotient from the moments should be a finite-dimensional moment problem for a nonnegative
matrix pencil rather than a graph-theoretic argument.

*Why now?* Both sides of the equivalence are already definable in the catalog
(`quotAdj`, `quotDeg`, `classSize`), so the conjecture is a statement about existing objects
and any counterexample is a finite, checkable pair.

---

## Conjecture 4 (Minimal order of failure). Six is the exact threshold.

Every pair of non-isomorphic connected graphs on at most five vertices is separated by the
adjacency-degree moments, and six is therefore the minimal order at which the invariant fails
for connected graphs (a witness on six vertices is proved here).

*Status.* The six-vertex failure is proved in Lean (`moment_failure_connected_nonregular`); the
`n ≤ 5` separation is exploratory only.

*The key insight is* that on at most five vertices the colour-refinement quotient of a
connected graph already has as many classes as the automorphism orbits, so by Conjecture 3's
proved direction the invariant is complete there; the statement is a finite verification that
can be discharged by `decide` over a suitable encoding.

*Why now?* The infrastructure to state and check it — `quotAdj`, `degWalkCount`, decidable
six-vertex graphs — is in place, and the finiteness makes it a genuine test of the
decidability route rather than of the theory.

---

## Conjecture 5 (Quotient algebra is a full matrix algebra). Tree orbit quotients.

For a tree `T` with orbit quotient of size `k`, the algebra induced by `𝓐(T)` on the orbit
quotient is the full matrix algebra `M_k(ℝ)`, and consequently the ideal `𝓐(T) J 𝓐(T)` acts on
`M_T` as its full endomorphism algebra.

*Status.* The scalar shadow of this — the factorisation
`moment (X * J * Y) = moment X * moment Y` (`Synthesis.moment_mul_J_mul`) — is proved; the
algebra statement is open.

*The key insight is* that the quotient of a tree carries a distance-graded filtration with
one-dimensional graded pieces, so the images of `A` and `D` generate a matrix algebra by a
Jacobson-density argument, with the `J`-ideal supplying the rank-one elements.

*Why now?* `moment_mul_J_mul` already isolates the rank-one behaviour of `J` at the level of
moments, which is exactly the input a density argument needs, and the quotient objects are
formalised.

# Future directions: bold, testable conjectures from the symmetry dichotomy

The cycle established, in
`Catalog/MachineLearning/TransformerUniversality/PermutationDichotomy.lean` (0 sorries):

* `group_uniform_universal` — for **any** finite group `Γ` of token symmetries, the
  `Γ`-invariant part of the attention algebra is uniformly dense in the `Γ`-invariant continuous
  functionals on compact saturated domains (specializations: `symmetric_uniform_universal` for
  the full symmetric group, `shift_uniform_universal` for cyclic/relative symmetry);
* `equivariant_uniform_universal` — the exact converse in the sequence-to-sequence setting:
  symmetric attention, queried through the marked-token encoding, is a universal approximator of
  the continuous `Γ`-equivariant maps, and the constructed heads are exactly equivariant;
* `equivariant_iff_exists_marked_invariant` — a representation theorem: continuous equivariant
  sequence-to-sequence maps are *exactly* the marked-token evaluations of continuous invariant
  functionals;
* `orbit_barrier_lower` / `orbit_barrier_attained` / `symmetry_barrier_position_read` — the
  obstruction is *sharp*: the optimal invariant error on an orbit equals exactly half the orbit
  oscillation, and reading an absolute position costs at least `1/2`;
* `positional_restores_universality` / `positional_seq2seq_universality` — one-hot positional
  encodings remove the obstruction completely, via an explicit invariant continuous decoder.

Below are the follow-up conjectures, ranked by expected impact.

## C1. Head-count law: the symmetric approximant needs only orbit-many heads, not `|Γ|`-many

**Conjecture.** For every `Γ`-invariant `g ∈ C(K, ℝ)` and `ε > 0`, there is a `Γ`-invariant
element of `attentionAlgebra` that `ε`-approximates `g` and is a sum of at most
`poly(dim, 1/ε)` products of readouts — in particular independent of `|Γ| = n!`, which is what
the averaging proof of `group_uniform_universal` currently spends.

*The key insight is* that averaging over `Γ` is a *projection*, not a construction: the invariant
subalgebra is already generated by the multisymmetric power sums `x ↦ ∑_i ∏_a (x_i a)^{e_a}`,
each of which is a **single** product of readouts, so the group sum can be eliminated in favour
of a generating set of size polynomial in the feature dimension and the degree.

*Why now?* The stability lemma `attentionAlgebra_compPerm_mem` plus the sharp barrier give both
halves needed to measure such a bound: any candidate generating set can be tested against the
`1/2` barrier of `symmetry_barrier_position_read`, so the conjecture is falsifiable by an
explicit finite computation at small `|ι|`.

## C2. Softmax realizability: every element of the attention algebra is a limit of genuine
softmax transformer blocks

**Conjecture.** The uniform closure on compacta of finite compositions of *softmax* attention
layers with residual connections and coordinatewise multiplicative gating contains
`attentionAlgebra`, with an explicit inverse-temperature schedule `β(ε) = O(log(1/ε))`.

*The key insight is* that `softmaxHeadRead_zero_scores` already realizes a linear readout as a
zero-score softmax head, and the exponential concentration bound of `SoftmaxLookup.lean`
(`sum_weight_erase_le`) controls the deviation of a finite-`β` head from a hard selection, so
products of readouts should be reachable by stacking two layers with logarithmically scaled
scores.

*Why now?* Both ingredients are already formalized in this catalog; the missing step is a single
composition estimate, so the conjecture can be attacked directly and refuted by an explicit
two-token counterexample if the residual structure is insufficient.

## C3. Symmetry-group determination: the invariance group of a trained architecture is
recoverable from finitely many queries

**Conjecture.** For a model `p` in `attentionAlgebra ι κ`, the subgroup
`{σ : p ∘ permAct σ = p}` is determined by the values of `p` on the orbit of a single generic
sequence, and equals the stabilizer of the positional encoding in the sense of
`PositionalSymmetry.posStab`.

*The key insight is* that `orbit_barrier_lower` converts symmetry detection into an
approximation-error measurement: a non-symmetry of `p` shows up as a nonzero orbit oscillation,
which is exactly the quantity the sharp barrier measures.

*Why now?* The barrier is now known to be an equality, not just an inequality, so orbit
oscillation is a *complete* invariant rather than a one-sided test.

## C4. Quantized-domain phase transition between exact and approximate universality

**Conjecture.** On the `N`-quantized cube of sequences, the minimal number of heads of an exact
symmetric model interpolating an invariant target grows like `Θ(N^{|ι|·|κ|}/|Γ|)`, while the
number needed for `ε`-approximation of a Lipschitz target grows like `Θ((L/ε)^{|ι||κ|}/|Γ|)`;
in particular exact interpolation and uniform approximation have the *same* exponent but differ
by the symmetry factor `|Γ|`.

*The key insight is* that the group-averaging step divides the effective domain by the orbit
size, so both counting problems descend to the orbit space, where the finite lookup theorem of
`TransformerArchitecture.lean` and the separation lower bound of `FiniteLookupSeparation.lean`
apply verbatim.

*Why now?* The orbit-space picture only became available with `SaturatedUnder` and the averaging
argument proved this cycle; the statement is a finite counting claim, hence decidable at small
parameters.

## C5. Beyond finite groups: compact symmetry groups and continuous positional encodings

**Conjecture.** `group_uniform_universal` remains true when the finite group `Γ` is replaced by a
compact group acting continuously on the position space (e.g. rotations of a circular position
encoding), with Haar averaging in place of the finite sum, and the barrier becomes half the
oscillation over the (now compact) orbit.

*The key insight is* that the only property of `Γ` used in the proof is that averaging is a
bounded projection onto the invariants that preserves the subalgebra — a property Haar measure
supplies for compact groups.

*Why now?* The proof of `symmetrize_error` isolates exactly this projection property, so
replacing `∑_{g ∈ Γ} / |Γ|` by `∫ dμ` is a localized change; a counterexample would have to come
from failure of subalgebra stability, which is testable on the rotation group of a 4-token ring.

# Future directions (thread `th_576aa37a`, cycle 1)

This cycle closed four of the six targets left by cycle 0 — the CSS dictionary
(`Catalog/Geometry/CSSDictionary.lean`), CSS distance
(`Catalog/Geometry/CSSDistance.lean`), the actual hypercube incidence complex
(`Catalog/Geometry/HypercubeIncidence.lean`, with the bridge theorem now
instantiated unconditionally), the graph/complex separation
(`Catalog/Geometry/GraphRepresentability.lean`), and the Singleton comparison at
the correct block length `N = n·2ⁿ⁻¹`.  The Steane code
(`Catalog/Geometry/SteaneCode.lean`) certifies the framework end to end:
`[[7,1,3]]`.

Two facts drive everything below.  (i) The hypercube homological code has
**distance 1** although its graph has girth 4: a graph code has no `Z`-checks,
so its primal distance is the least weight of a *non-cut*, which is 1 whenever
the graph is bridgeless.  (ii) A graph incidence matrix always satisfies the
all-ones relation, so `rank < #V`; independence of the `X`-checks is an absolute
obstruction to a graph model.

## Conjecture 1 (bridgeless ⟺ distance one, for all graph codes)

For a finite graph `G` with incidence matrix `∂₁` over `𝔽₂` and no `Z`-checks,
`cssDistance = 1` **iff** `G` has no bridge, and `cssDistance = 2` iff `G` has a
bridge but no two parallel bridges (with the convention that isolated vertices
are discarded).

*The key insight is* that in a graph code the primal distance is not a systole
at all but a **co-systole of the cut matroid**: `dX` is the minimum size of a
non-cut, i.e. the girth of the *bond matroid*, which equals `1` exactly when no
single edge is a bond.  *Why now?*  `HypercubeDistanceOne.lean` proves the
hypercube instance by exhibiting a square through a chosen edge; the only input
was "the edge lies on a cycle", which is precisely bridgelessness, so the
general statement is within reach of the same argument.

## Conjecture 2 (weight profile characterises representability)

A binary matrix `M` is the incidence matrix of a `k`-dimensional simplicial
boundary map iff every column has weight exactly `k+1` **and** the "all-ones on
each `(k−1)`-face" relations hold; for `k = 1` this reduces to: `M` is a graph
incidence matrix iff every column has weight `2`.  Consequently a binary CSS
complex is graph-representable iff `H_X` admits a column-weight-two form, and
the rank bound `rank H_X + 1 ≤ #rows` is necessary but **not** sufficient.

*The key insight is* that the parity obstruction proved in
`GraphRepresentability.lean` is only the degree-`0` shadow of a whole family of
weight constraints, one per skeleton dimension.  *Why now?*  We already have the
necessary direction and two counterexamples (`steaneH`, the `1×1` identity); the
missing content is a normal-form algorithm turning a column-weight-two matrix
into an explicit graph.

## Conjecture 3 (no expander-free distance growth)

For every family of graph codes (`d₂ = 0`) the distance is bounded by a
constant, while `k` grows linearly in `N`; hence **no** one-dimensional complex
achieves `k·d² = Ω(N)`.  Growing distance forces genuine `2`-cells: for a
cellulated closed surface the `min(systole, cosystole)` theorem gives
`d = Θ(√N)` only when both the systole and the cosystole grow.

*The key insight is* that `dX ≤ 1 + (minimum bond size)` collapses the primal
sector of any bridgeless `1`-complex, so the entire burden of distance falls on
the cosystole, which the girth alone cannot carry.  *Why now?*  With
`cssDistance` and `min(systole, cosystole)` formalised, both sectors are finally
expressible in Lean, and the toric-code files already in the catalog supply the
`2`-cell comparison case.

## Conjecture 4 (Singleton slack of homological codes)

For every graph code on a bridgeless graph, the quantum Singleton defect
`N − k − 2(d−1) = N − k − 2` equals `rank ∂₁ − 2 = #V − β₀ − 2`; in particular
the defect is exactly the number of independent vertex checks minus two, and it
is `0` only for the `4`-cycle-like degenerate cases.

*The key insight is* that for graph codes the Singleton defect is a purely
topological quantity — the rank of the boundary map — rather than a code-design
parameter.  *Why now?*  `hyperComplex_singleton_slack` already proves the
hypercube case (`N − k = 2ⁿ − 1`), and the general identity follows from
`graph_numLogical_add` once Conjecture 1 pins `d = 1`.

## Conjecture 5 (four hypercubes, four homologies)

Of the four candidate meanings of "hypercube complex" — the cube graph `Qₙ`, the
filled cubical `n`-ball, its boundary sphere `Sⁿ⁻¹`, and the periodic cubical
torus `(S¹)ⁿ` — **only the torus** can produce a one-logical-qubit CSS code, and
it does so only for `n = 2` with an `M × N` grid of size `1`; the ball has
`k = 0`, the sphere `k = 0` in middle degree, and the graph `k = 2ⁿ⁻¹(n−2)+1`.

*The key insight is* that the "one logical qubit" folklore is a statement about
`H₁` of a *torus*, and it was silently transported to `H₁` of a graph, where the
first Betti number is the circuit rank instead.  *Why now?*  Three of the four
objects are now formalised or nearly so (the graph here, the torus in
`Catalog/Geometry/ToricCode/`), so the comparison needs only the two cubical
models.

# Future Directions

Derived from the verified results in

* `Catalog/Novelty/CollatzSpectralNormalized.lean` — limit law, modulus formula,
  resonance classification, `3n+1` vs `5n+1` vs `7n+1` discriminator, `L²` mean;
* `Catalog/Novelty/CollatzSpectralUniform.lean` — explicit `O((1+|ω| log N)/N)`
  error bound, uniform convergence on compact frequency sets, and the
  density-zero blindness no-go;
* `Catalog/Novelty/CollatzSpectralResonance.lean` — arithmetic of the resonance
  sets and pairwise separation of the three classical multipliers.

What this cycle settled. The one-step phase `T(n)/n` splits into a constant even
branch `1/2` and an odd branch `a + 1/n`; the odd perturbation `1/n` is summable
after Cesàro averaging, so `F_N(ω)/N → (e(ω/2)+e(aω))/2` with modulus
`|cos(π(a−½)ω)|`.  Every question about "cancellation for the `an+1` map at a
fixed frequency" is therefore *completely answered* at the level of the one-step
sum, and the answer contains no dynamical information whatsoever
(`spectral_blind_to_finite_modification`).  The following conjectures push into
the regimes where information can survive.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Second-order spectral law: the `log N` term is a genuine invariant)

For every `a ≥ 1` and every `ω ≠ 0`,
`F a ω N − N · limitAmp a ω − c(a,ω) · log N` converges as `N → ∞`, with
`c(a,ω) = π i ω e(aω)` (the coefficient produced by the odd-branch expansion
`e(ω/n) = 1 + 2πiω/n + O(ω²/n²)` summed against the odd harmonic series).
Equivalently, `(F a ω N − N·limitAmp a ω)/log N → c(a,ω)`.

**The key insight is** that the first-order term erases the multiplier's
arithmetic (it depends only on `e(aω)` through a modulus that is a single
cosine), while the *second*-order term is an honest half-harmonic sum whose
coefficient is linear in `ω` and carries the branch phase `e(aω)` undamped —
so the subleading spectrum sees strictly more than the leading one.

**Why now?** `norm_F_div_sub_limitAmp_le` already isolates the deviation sum
`Σ dseq` and bounds it by `2π|ω|(1+log N)`; the conjecture asserts that this
bound is attained with an explicit constant.  The Lean infrastructure
(`dseq_eq`, `sum_one_div_le_one_add_log`) needs only a matching *lower* bound
plus `Real.log` asymptotics for the odd harmonic sum, both of which are in reach
of the existing `harmonic` API.

---

## Conjecture 2 (Iterated transforms are not blind)

Define the `m`-step transform `F^{(m)} a ω N = Σ_{n≤N} e(ω · T_a^m(n)/n)`.
Then for each fixed `m`, `F^{(m)} a ω N / N` converges to an explicit finite
combination `Σ_{j} 2^{−m} · (multiplicity) · e(ω · r_j)`, where `r_j` ranges over
the finitely many limiting `m`-step ratios `a^{k} / 2^{m−k}` (`k` = number of odd
steps), weighted by the density of residue classes mod `2^m` following that
parity pattern.  Moreover, for `m ≥ 2` the resonance set of `F^{(m)}` is **not**
a coset of a lattice, and its zero set determines `a` uniquely.

**The key insight is** that one step gives two branches and hence a cosine, i.e.
one Diophantine condition; `m` steps give `2^m` branches with ratios
`a^k/2^{m−k}`, so the limiting amplitude becomes an exponential polynomial in
`ω` whose zero set is an intersection of many conditions — rigid enough to
recover `a`, and no longer invariant under sparse modification of the map.

**Why now?** The proof template is exactly the one verified here: split by the
parity pattern of the first `m` steps (a residue class mod `2^m` of known
density), show the ratio converges on each class, and Cesàro-average.
`summand_eq` + `dseq_eq` + `Filter.Tendsto.cesaro_smul` generalize verbatim.

---

## Conjecture 3 (A density-zero blindness threshold)

`spectral_blind_to_density_zero` is sharp in the following strong sense: for
every function `h : ℕ → ℝ` with `h N / N → 0` and `h N → ∞` there exist a
multiplier `a` and a modification of `ratio a` supported on a set `S` with
`#(S ∩ [1,N]) ≍ h N` such that the modified transform still satisfies
`F̃/N → limitAmp a ω` for all `ω`, yet the modified map has an orbit structure
(e.g. an extra cycle of length `≍ h N` at scale `N`) that differs from the
original.  Conversely, any modification on a set of positive upper density
changes the limit for a set of frequencies of positive measure.

**The key insight is** that "invisible to the normalized spectrum" is exactly
"supported on a density-zero set", so the spectral method has a precise
information-theoretic ceiling: it can only ever certify statements that are
themselves invariant under density-zero surgery — and cycle existence is not.

**Why now?** The forward half is already proved (`norm_Fgen_sub_le` gives the
`2·#S/N` bound, which is the whole content).  The converse needs a lower bound
on `‖Σ_{k ∈ S} (e(ω r₁) − e(ω r₂))‖` after averaging in `ω`, i.e. a Plancherel
argument on `[0,2]` for which `meanSquare_limitAmp` is the model computation.

---

## Conjecture 4 (Resonance sets classify the multiplier, and pairwise
intersections are governed by `gcd(2a−1, 2b−1)`)

For all `a, b ≥ 1`, the common resonance set
`R a ∩ R b = {ω : (2a−1)ω and (2b−1)ω are both odd integers}` equals
`{ω = (2m+1)·g / ((2a−1)(2b−1)/g') ...}` — precisely, writing
`d = gcd(2a−1, 2b−1)`, `R a ∩ R b = (d / ((2a−1)(2b−1))) · (2ℤ+1) ∩ R a`, and in
particular `R a ∩ R b ⊆ 2ℤ+1` exactly when `d = 1`.  Hence `R a = R b` iff
`a = b`, and the map `a ↦ R a` is a complete invariant of the multiplier.

**The key insight is** that the resonance sets are cosets of the lattices
`(1/(2a−1))(2ℤ+1)`, so their intersection theory is pure elementary number
theory of the odd numbers `2a−1` — an arithmetic invariant hiding inside a
purely analytic (Fourier) statistic.

**Why now?** The three instances `d = gcd(5,9) = gcd(5,13) = gcd(9,13) = 1` are
already proved in `common_resonance_three_five`, `common_resonance_three_seven`,
`common_resonance_five_seven`, each via a two-line `omega` certificate.  The
general statement is the same argument with `d` carried symbolically, and
`limitAmp_eq_zero_iff` reduces it entirely to `ℤ`.

---

## Conjecture 5 (Orbit transforms: a genuine spectral–dynamical bridge)

Let `σ(n)` be the stopping time of `n` under `T_3` and define the *orbit
transform* `G ω N = Σ_{n≤N} e(ω σ(n)/log n)`.  Then `G ω N / N` converges for
every `ω` to the characteristic function of the limiting distribution of
`σ(n)/log n`, and the Collatz conjecture restricted to `[1,N]` is *equivalent*
to `σ` being everywhere finite, i.e. to `G` being well defined — whereas no
statement about `F a ω N` has this property (by Conjecture 3 / the proved
blindness theorem).

**The key insight is** that spectral information about a dynamical system can
only be dynamical if the *phase itself* is an orbit functional; replacing the
one-step ratio `T(n)/n` by the normalized stopping time turns the transform into
the characteristic function of the (conjecturally log-normal) stopping-time
distribution, where cancellation genuinely encodes orbit behaviour.

**Why now?** The present cycle proves the negative half rigorously — the
one-step transform is provably blind — which is precisely the justification for
moving the phase from one step to the whole orbit.  The positive half is a
Lévy-continuity statement, and Mathlib now has the characteristic-function and
weak-convergence API needed to state it.

# Future directions (Cycle 2, thread th_3b515382)

Cycle 2 delivered, with complete Lean proofs and no `sorry`:

* explicit periodic left/right shifts, translation equivariance of every elementary
  rule, and the Rule 110 singleton theorem as a corollary of a general
  right-transitivity criterion;
* the rule-number bijection `Fin 256 ≃ LocalRule` and a census showing that exactly
  `16` rules provably have a unique fixed configuration on every cyclic lattice;
* `MvPolynomial` models: `eval s (rulePoly g i) = step g s i`, polynomial-level shift
  equivariance, and the fixed-point ideal (update equations plus the Boolean relations
  `X i ^ 2 - X i`) whose `GF(2)`-points are exactly the fixed configurations;
* exact fixed-point counts as arithmetic functions: `#V(150,n) = 4` for `n` even and
  `2` for `n` odd; `#V(90,n) = 4` when `3 ∣ n` and `1` otherwise, via a periodic
  descent principle that reduces an infinite family to one finite check;
* simulation embeddings `Config d ↪ Config n` for `d ∣ n` preserving exact orbit
  lengths, the existence of a periodic orbit for every rule, and an exact 2-cycle of
  Rule 110 on every lattice with `4 ∣ n`;
* the Klein four-group of reflection/complementation symmetries realised as
  *conjugacies of the dynamics*, hence invariance of both the fixed-point count and
  the exact orbit spectrum, which enlarges the certified census from `16` to `48`
  rules (rules `124`, `137`, `193` inherit the Rule 110 singleton theorem);
* a companion criterion (zeros travel left, ones travel right) certifying that the
  four rules `176, 178, 184, 186` — including the traffic rule `184` — have exactly
  the two constant configurations as fixed points, on every lattice.

The following conjectures are the sharpest open questions those results raise.  Each
is falsifiable by a finite computation or by a single counterexample.

## C1. The singleton criterion is *characterised* by an eventual-orbit condition

**Conjecture.**  For an elementary rule `g` the following are equivalent: (i)
`#V(g,n) = 1` for every `n ≥ 1`; (ii) `#V(g,n) = 1` for `n = 1,2,3,4,5,6,7`; (iii) the
only bi-infinite `g`-fixed word is the all-zero word.  In particular the set of rules
with `#V ≡ 1` has exactly `78` elements; `48` of them are already certified by the
symmetry-closed criterion, so the conjecture predicts exactly `30` further rules whose
unit count needs a non-local argument.

*The key insight is* that `#V(g,n)` counts closed walks of length `n` in the de Bruijn
graph of `g` restricted to the "fixed" edges `g a b c = b`; a count that stays `1`
forever means that this subgraph has a unique cycle, which is decidable from a graph
with `4` vertices — hence a finite test must exist, and the only question is how small
it can be.

*Why now?*  The census machinery (`ruleEquiv`, `singletonRules`,
`mem_singletonRules_fixedPoints_ncard`) already exists, and the transfer-matrix
statement below would turn (i) ⇔ (ii) into a linear-algebra computation over `ℕ`.

## C2. Transfer-matrix trace formula for every rule and every size

**Conjecture.**  Let `T g : Matrix (Cell × Cell) (Cell × Cell) ℕ` have entry
`T[(a,b),(b',c)] = 1` iff `b = b'` and `g a b c = b`, and `0` otherwise.  Then for all
`n ≥ 1`,
`#V(g,n) = trace (T g ^ n)`.
Consequently `n ↦ #V(g,n)` satisfies a linear recurrence of order at most `4` with
integer coefficients, and is a sum of `n`-th powers of the eigenvalues of a `4×4`
`0/1`-matrix.  In particular the sequences `1,1,4,1,1,4,…` (rule 90), `2,4,2,4,…`
(rule 150) and `1,3,1,3,…` (rule 30), each now proved individually, would become
instances of one eigenvalue phenomenon rather than three separate arguments.

*The key insight is* that a fixed configuration on `ZMod n` is precisely a closed walk
of length `n` in the fixed-edge de Bruijn graph, so counting is a trace, and the
arithmetic periodicity observed for rules 90, 150 and 30 comes from roots of unity in
the spectrum.

*Why now?*  The descent theorem `ncard_fixed_eq_of_periodic` already proves the
special case where the graph is a disjoint union of cycles; the general case only
needs the "matrix power counts walks" lemma, which is the missing infrastructure.

## C3. Rule 110 has a non-fixed periodic configuration exactly when `4 ∣ n`

**Conjecture.**  For `n ≥ 1`, rule 110 has a configuration of minimal period `> 1` on
`ZMod n` if and only if `4 ∣ n`.  The "if" direction is proved
(`rule110_exists_minimalPeriod_two`); the "only if" direction is verified for
`n ≤ 8` computationally.

*The key insight is* that the smallest rule-110 glider has spatial period `4`, so all
short orbits should be pullbacks along `ZMod n → ZMod 4`, and the conjecture says that
the entire short-orbit structure of the universal rule on a torus is generated by a
single four-cell pattern.

*Why now?*  The simulation-embedding theorem `minimalPeriod_pull` gives one direction
for free, and it also says what a proof of the converse must produce: a retraction of
the periodic part of the dynamics onto the four-site lattice.

## C4. The fixed-point coordinate ring is `0`-dimensional but its length separates rules

**Conjecture.**  For every rule `g` and every `n ≥ 1` the quotient
`MvPolynomial (ZMod n) (ZMod 2) / fixedIdeal g n` is a finite-dimensional
`GF(2)`-algebra — hence of Krull dimension `0` — and its `GF(2)`-dimension equals
`#V(g,n)`.  Thus Krull dimension is a *useless* invariant here, while the length of
the coordinate ring recovers exactly the point count.

*The key insight is* that the Boolean relations `X i ^ 2 - X i` force the quotient to
be a product of copies of `GF(2)`, one per `GF(2)`-point, so all the information sits
in length, not dimension — which explains why the "dimension tracks complexity"
heuristic of cycle 0 had to fail.

*Why now?*  `fixedIdeal` and `mem_zeroLocus_iff_isFixed` are in place; what is missing
is the Chinese-remainder decomposition of a Boolean quotient ring, a self-contained
piece of commutative algebra.

## C5. A sheaf on the lattice site, specified before use

**Specification (to be formalised, then tested).**  Site: the category whose objects
are the arcs `[i, i+ℓ]` of the cyclic lattice `ZMod n` and whose morphisms are
inclusions, with the Grothendieck topology generated by finite covers by overlapping
arcs.  Presheaf: `F(U) = { partial configurations on U that satisfy the update
equation at every site whose full neighbourhood lies in U }`, with restriction the
obvious truncation.

**Conjecture.**  `F` is a sheaf, and `Γ(ZMod n, F) ≅ V(g,n)`; moreover `F` is flasque
if and only if `g` is right-transitive in the sense of
`CAShiftsPolynomialsOrbits.RightTransitive`, so the `16` census rules are exactly the
ones with vanishing higher cohomology on the cyclic site.

*The key insight is* that gluing partial fixed configurations across overlapping arcs
is exactly the propagation argument used in
`fixedPoints_eq_singleton_zero_of_right_transitive`, so the obstruction to gluing is
the failure of that local criterion.

*Why now?*  The propagation lemma is already isolated and proved; the sheaf language
would turn it from an ad-hoc induction into a cohomological statement, and gives a
concrete falsifiable prediction (flasqueness ⇔ right transitivity) rather than a vague
analogy.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Algorithmic Immune Systems

Derived from the verified results in `Catalog/Shared/Immune*.lean` (Parts I–IX:
parasite calculus and attestation, semantics, the diagonal parasite, quarantine
and the conservation law, the reflexive oracle barrier, the algebra of mutations
and the immune uncertainty principle, ensembles and the arms race, bounded
universes, monitoring frequency).

Each conjecture below is stated so that it can be *falsified* by a single Lean
counterexample.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Immune capacity law: rigidity × memory is exactly exponential)

For every monitor `S ⊆ PAst` and every size bound `N`, let `mem(S) = |S|` and let
`rig(S, N)` be the number of behaviourally trivial programs of size `≤ N` that
`S` rejects.  Then there are absolute constants `c₁, c₂ > 0` with

`c₁ · 2^{N/3} ≤ mem(S) + rig(S, N) ≤ c₂ · 2^{N/3} · poly(N)` for every *optimal*
monitor, and the lower bound is attained only by the bounded whitelist of
Part VIII.

*Status.* The lower bound `2^n ≤ |S| + |padFamily n \ S|` is **proved**
(`immune_uncertainty`); the matching upper bound and the uniqueness of the
optimum are open.

**The key insight is** that `pad` realises an *injective encoding of bit strings
into a single semantic equivalence class*, so the immune system is forced to pay
one bit of memory per bit of dead code it wishes to tolerate — attestation is a
lossless code for a class on which behaviour is constant.

**Why now?** Both sides are finitary and decidable for fixed `N`: the upper bound
is a counting argument over `astUniverse N L`, which is already constructed and
proved to contain the bounded universe (`mem_astUniverse`).

---

## Conjecture 2 (Reflexive oracle hierarchy)

Stratify programs by *reflexion depth*: `ask`-free programs have depth `0`, and a
program has depth `≤ d+1` if every oracle query it makes is answered by an oracle
that is correct on all programs of depth `≤ d`.  Then for every `d` there is an
oracle `O_d` correct on all programs of depth `≤ d`, no oracle is correct at
depth `d+1` for all `d` simultaneously, and the hierarchy is strict.

*Status.* Depth `0` is **proved** (`oracle_correct_on_askFree`), and the global
impossibility is **proved** (`no_correct_reflexive_oracle`).  The strictness of
the intermediate levels is open.

**The key insight is** that oracle-independence of `ask`-free behaviour
(`askFree_effect_oracle_indep`) is the base case of an induction on reflexion
depth: each level fixes the semantics of the level below, exactly as a Tarskian
truth hierarchy escapes the liar by stratification.

**Why now?** The oracle-parameterised semantics `evalO`/`effectO` is already in
place, so a depth predicate is a routine inductive definition on `OAst`, and the
level-`d` oracle can be defined by the same classical comprehension used for
`canonicalOracle`.

---

## Conjecture 3 (No probabilistic escape from the diagonal)

Let `μ` be any finitely supported probability distribution over harmless
detectors, and let `err(μ) = inf_p Pr_{d ~ μ}[d classifies p correctly]`.  Then
`err(μ) = 0`: there is a single program on which *every* detector in the support
errs, so randomisation does not buy even an `ε` advantage.

*Status.* The support-wise version is **proved** for sound detectors
(`ensemble_common_escape`, `ensemble_vote_zero`: the vote count for the escaping
parasite is exactly `0`).  The general case, where members may be unsound, is
open and is the interesting one.

**The key insight is** that the disjunctive ensemble `ensembleOr` is itself a
program of the calculus, so the diagonal construction applies to the *ensemble*,
not to its members; randomisation over a finite support is subsumed by a single
deterministic program.

**Why now?** `ensembleOr` with `flags_ensembleOr_iff` already reduces any monotone
combination rule to a single detector; the remaining work is to handle non-monotone
rules (majority with unsound members) by a counting argument over the support.

---

## Conjecture 4 (Latency–damage law for sampled monitoring)

For monitoring period `k` and any horizon `T`, the maximal number of compromised
steps that an adversary can force is exactly `T - ⌊T/k⌋`, and this is attained by
the constant `attack` adversary; moreover no rollback policy weaker than
per-step verification changes this count.

*Status.* Both extremes are **proved**: `periodic_healing` (clean at every
checkpoint) and `attack_window` (compromised at every non-checkpoint), which
already pin the count for the constant adversary.  The optimality over *all*
policies is open.

**The key insight is** that quarantine is an idempotent retraction
(`quarantine_idem`), so the guarded dynamics is completely determined by the
checkpoint pattern; the damage count is therefore a purely combinatorial function
of the sampling set, independent of the adversary's cleverness.

**Why now?** `traceK` generalises verbatim to an arbitrary checkpoint set
`C ⊆ ℕ`, turning the conjecture into a statement about `|[0,T] \ C|` that should
follow from the same case analysis used in `attack_window`.

---

## Conjecture 5 (Semantic quotient collapse)

Let `PAst/≈` be the quotient by semantic equivalence (`semSetoid`).  Then no
finite monitor on the quotient can exist at all: every `≈`-class that contains a
malicious program contains programs of unbounded size, and any monitor that is
`≈`-invariant, sound and computable must accuse either nothing or everything —
the categorical shadow of `no_perfect_detector`.

*Status.* Open.  The ingredients are proved: classes are exponentially large
(`semClass_card_exp`), finite whitelists are never `≈`-closed
(`finite_whitelist_not_semantically_closed`), and the internal/external gap is
isolated (`internal_external_gap`).

**The key insight is** that `≈`-invariance is precisely the hypothesis Rice's
theorem needs, while attestation deliberately violates it; the immune system's
power comes entirely from *not* being a semantic invariant.

**Why now?** `semSetoid` is already available as a `Setoid`, so the quotient type
and the induced monitor are one definition away, and the two horns of the
dichotomy can be assembled from `sound_detector_misses` and
`complete_detector_false_alarms`.

---

## Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. **(C1a)** `|astUniverse N L| ≤ (L + 2)^{2^{O(N)}}` is far too weak; the true
   count of programs of size `≤ N` with literals `< L` satisfies a Catalan-type
   recurrence.  Formalise the recurrence and derive a *matching* upper bound for
   Conjecture 1.
2. **(C2a)** Define reflexion depth on `OAst` and prove level `1`: there is an
   oracle correct on all programs whose `ask` arguments are themselves
   `ask`-free.
3. **(C4a)** Replace `traceK` by checkpoints indexed by an arbitrary set `C` and
   prove `damage(C, T) = |[1,T] \ C|` for the constant `attack` adversary.

# Future Directions — Diophantine–Lattice: Spectral Bounds on Non-Homogeneous Quadratic Forms

All conjectures below are falsifiable statements about the objects formalised in
`Catalog/Applications/DiophantineLatticeSpectral.lean` (`QF`, `HasSpectralBounds`,
`inhomEval`, `sqDistLattice`, `inhomMin`, `theta`).  They arose from the four
verification cycles recorded in that file and from the numerical experiments in
`ComputationalEvidence.md`.

## What is already settled (so the conjectures are not restatements)

* Spectral gap: `m·d(t,ℤⁿ)² ≤ Q(x − t)` for all `x ∈ ℤⁿ` (`spectral_gap_lower`),
  strict positivity off the lattice, and the resulting non-solvability
  (`no_integer_solution_below_gap`).
* Sandwich for the inhomogeneous minimum: `m·d(t,ℤⁿ)² ≤ μ(Q,t) ≤ M·n/4`
  (`inhomMin_sandwich`).
* Effective rational gap `m/q²` (`Cycle2.gap_rational_shift`).
* Two-sided counting `(2√(R/(Mn)) − 1)ⁿ ≤ N(R) ≤ (2√(R/m) + 1)ⁿ`
  (`Cycle3.counting_two_sided`).
* Theta series: convergence, factorisation over diagonal forms, decay at the gap
  rate, and `Θ(s) → 0` (`summable_theta`, `Cycle2.theta_diagonal`,
  `theta_decay`, `Cycle2.theta_tendsto_zero`).
* Exact extremal set for the half-shifted sum of squares: the `2ⁿ` vertices of
  the unit cube (`Cycle4.half_shift_minimizer_count`).

---

## C1. Sharp covering constant: the inhomogeneous minimum is controlled by the *trace*, not by `n·λ_max`

**Conjecture.** For every symmetric positive definite `A` with spectral bounds
`m, M` and every shift `t`,
`μ(Q, t) ≤ (1/4)·tr(A)`, and this is attained iff `A` is diagonal and `t` is a
half-integral shift.  In particular `μ(Q,t) ≤ M·n/4` (the proved bound) is never
sharp unless all eigenvalues coincide.

*The key insight is* that the rounding point `x = round(t)` used in
`exists_le_covering` wastes information: it bounds `Q(x − t)` by
`λ_max·‖x − t‖²`, whereas rounding *coordinatewise* gives
`Q(x − t) = ∑ᵢⱼ Aᵢⱼ (xᵢ−tᵢ)(xⱼ−tⱼ)` whose expectation over a random half-integral
displacement is exactly `tr(A)/4`, the off-diagonal terms cancelling in mean.

*Why now?* The averaging argument only needs the finite probability space
`{±1/2}ⁿ`, which is directly expressible with the existing `Finset` machinery in
the file; no measure theory is required, so it is a self-contained next step that
would upgrade every corollary depending on `M·n/4`.

## C2. Gap–theta duality: the decay rate of `Θ` *equals* the inhomogeneous minimum

**Conjecture.** For a spectrally sandwiched form with `m > 0`,
`lim_{s→∞} −(1/s)·log Θ(s) = μ(Q, t)`, and moreover
`Θ(s)·exp(s·μ(Q,t)) → r(μ)`, the number of integer points attaining the minimum
(finite by `card_solutions_le`).

*The key insight is* that `theta_decay` proves one inequality
(`≥ m·d(t,ℤⁿ)²` for the rate) purely from the term bound, while the matching
upper bound must come from isolating the minimising terms and dominating the rest
by the counting estimate `N(R) ≤ (2√(R/m)+1)ⁿ` — i.e. the *counting* theorem and
the *decay* theorem are two halves of one Laplace-type asymptotic.

*Why now?* Both halves are already formalised; the missing step is a dominated
tail estimate `∑_{Q(x−t) ≥ μ+δ} exp(−sQ) ≤ C·exp(−s(μ+δ))`, which follows from
polynomial coefficient growth by a summation-by-parts argument on `ℤⁿ` — a
finite-combinatorial lemma, not new analysis.

## C3. Rational shifts are extremal: a Diophantine dichotomy for the gap

**Conjecture.** For `m > 0` fixed, the gap function `t ↦ m·d(t,ℤⁿ)²` restricted
to shifts with denominator dividing `q` attains its minimum *exactly* at shifts
with a coordinate of exact denominator `q`, with value `m/q²`
(`Cycle2.gap_rational_shift` is the inequality); and for irrational `t` the
sequence of best rational approximations `p_k/q_k` of a coordinate produces gaps
`≍ m/q_k²`, so that `liminf q² · gap` over the convergents is positive iff the
coordinate is badly approximable.

*The key insight is* that `distZ_rat_ge` is the Diophantine statement
`‖a/q‖_ℤ ≥ 1/q` in disguise, so the spectral gap of a shifted lattice form is a
*continued-fraction invariant* of the shift, not merely a metric quantity.

*Why now?* Mathlib has continued fractions and the Hurwitz/Dirichlet
approximation theorems; combining them with `distZ_rat_ge` turns the qualitative
"off-lattice ⇒ positive gap" theorem into a quantitative badly-approximable
dichotomy with no new lattice theory required.

## C4. Reduction stability: the gap is invariant, the covering bound is not

**Conjecture.** For every `U ∈ GLₙ(ℤ)`, the transformed form `Q_U(y) = Q(Uy)`
with shift `U⁻¹t` has the *same* inhomogeneous minimum `μ(Q_U, U⁻¹t) = μ(Q, t)`
and the same solution counting function, but its spectral bounds `m_U, M_U` can
differ arbitrarily; consequently the LLL-reduced representative minimises the
ratio `M_U·n/4 : m_U·d(U⁻¹t,ℤⁿ)²` and the sandwich `inhomMin_sandwich` becomes
asymptotically tight after reduction.

*The key insight is* that `inhomMin` is a `GLₙ(ℤ)`-invariant of the pair
`(form, shift)`, whereas both ends of the proved sandwich are not — so lattice
reduction is precisely the act of choosing coordinates in which the two
*non-invariant* bounds pinch the *invariant* quantity.

*Why now?* The invariance half is a short bijection argument on `ℤⁿ` (the map
`x ↦ U⁻¹x` is a `Finset`-preserving equivalence), so the conjecture can be split
immediately into a provable invariance lemma and a genuinely open optimisation
statement about reduced bases.

## C5. Theta factorisation obstructs off-diagonality (a converse to `theta_diagonal`)

**Conjecture.** If for some shift `t` with all coordinates irrational the theta
series of `A` factorises as a product of `n` one-dimensional shifted Gaussian
sums for all `s > 0`, then `A` is diagonal.  Equivalently: the failure of
multiplicativity of `Θ` is a faithful invariant detecting off-diagonal mass.

*The key insight is* that `Cycle2.theta_diagonal` proves factorisation from
diagonality by Fubini on `ℤⁿ`, and the reverse direction should follow by
comparing the `s → ∞` expansions: the first two exponents of `Θ` recover the two
smallest values of `Q(x − t)`, and matching all of them across the product
forces the Gram matrix to split.

*Why now?* The proved ingredients (`tsum_pi_prod`, `summable_theta`, and the
counting bound that makes coefficientwise comparison legitimate) already give
uniqueness of Dirichlet-type expansions in this setting; the remaining work is
combinatorial bookkeeping of exponents, not new convergence theory.

# Future Directions (cycle 1, thread th_ed2afa00)

Derived from the verified results in `Catalog/Logic/GEBGradedLawvere.lean`:
graded (partial) universality, the obstruction spectrum
(`representable ⟺ pointwise fixed points`), the refutation of the
monoid-closure conjecture, the vacuity of full universality, the counting law
`n^n - (n-1)^n` with density `1 - e⁻¹`, and the explicit pitch-class triad.

## 1. A relative obstruction spectrum for *iterated* self-application

Extend `RepresentsDiagonal` to depth `k`: a table represents the composite
`f ∘ (x ↦ eval x (eval x x))` and its higher analogues.  Conjecture: depth-`k`
representability of `F` holds iff every `f ∈ F` has a point of period dividing
`k` under some auxiliary transformation, so the spectrum stratifies into a
strictly increasing chain whose `k`-th level over `Fin n` has cardinality
`n^n - #{f : f has no point of period dividing k}`, and the chain is strict for
every `n ≥ 3`.

*The key insight is* that the depth-1 argument consumes the semantic
endomorphism exactly once, which is precisely why pointwise fixed points — and
not the generated monoid — control representability; increasing the depth
should trade fixed points for periodic points in a controlled way.

*Why now?* The depth-1 spectrum is now a proved equivalence with an exact
finite count, so any deviation at depth `k` is immediately measurable against
`n^n - (n-1)^n`, and the `Fin 3` monoid counterexample supplies the smallest
domain where strictness can be tested exhaustively.

## 2. Density laws as an invariant of the semantic category

The representable density over `Fin n` tends to `1 - e⁻¹`.  Conjecture: for the
category of finite semantic domains with a fixed extra structure (monoid
actions, partial orders, metric quantisations), the representable density
converges to a structure-dependent constant, and this constant is a complete
invariant separating the structures: e.g. monotone endomorphisms of a finite
chain have density `1` (every monotone self-map of a finite chain has a fixed
point) while permutations have density `1 - e⁻¹ + o(1)` in the derangement
sense.

*The key insight is* that the obstruction is quantitative: `e⁻¹` of all
semantic dynamics is permanently outside self-applicative syntax, and this
proportion is computed from the fixed-point predicate alone, so it should vary
predictably when the ambient class of endomorphisms is restricted.

*Why now?* `card_maximal_representable_family` and
`representable_density_tendsto` give the unrestricted baseline in closed form,
so restricted classes can be compared to a proved reference value.

## 3. Coherence hierarchy for weak simulations

The current file proves: equivalences transport diagonal codes and values,
coherent retractions lift codes, embeddings preserve values but not code-hood
(explicit `Unit ↪ Bool` counterexample), bisimulations preserve only
observational equality (explicit parity counterexample).  Conjecture: these are
the only four levels — i.e. there is a four-element lattice of coherence laws
such that each strictly weaker law admits a two-element counterexample and each
law is necessary and sufficient for the corresponding transport statement.

*The key insight is* that transport uses preservation of the evaluation table
in both arguments simultaneously; dropping preservation in the second argument
kills code-hood while preserving values, and dropping equality to a congruence
kills values while preserving observations.

*Why now?* Each level already has a proved positive statement and, where it
fails, a minimal finite counterexample, so the remaining work is exactly the
completeness of the lattice.

## 4. Uniqueness from guardedness in ordered and metric domains

`contraction_code_independence` shows that uniqueness of semantic fixed points
makes all diagonal codes agree across unrelated presentations.  Conjecture: the
same conclusion holds for guarded endomorphisms of ultrametric or
domain-theoretic semantics (Banach fixed points in complete ultrametric spaces,
or unique fixed points of guarded recursive definitions), and moreover the
resulting canonical value is computable as the limit of the diagonal iterates
of *any* code.

*The key insight is* that presentation transport is canonical while code choice
is not; uniqueness is the exact hypothesis that collapses the second source of
ambiguity, and guardedness is its syntactic shadow.

*Why now?* The Lipschitz case is proved with no isomorphism hypothesis
whatsoever, so the statement is already in the strongest possible "unrelated
codes" form and can be ported verbatim to any uniqueness principle.

## 5. Maximal *graded* triads with genuine domain morphisms

The explicit triad over `ZMod 12` uses evaluation-preserving equivalences of
three three-constructor syntaxes.  Conjecture: for the free graded model on a
family `F`, the group of evaluation-preserving automorphisms is isomorphic to
the group of permutations of `F` fixing the chosen fixed-point assignment,
times the stabiliser of the literals; consequently two graded triads over the
same `F` are equivalent iff their fixed-point assignments agree, and the number
of inequivalent triads over `Fin n` with `|F| = m` is computable in closed form.

*The key insight is* that the free graded model is determined by nothing but a
choice function selecting one fixed point per endomorphism, so classification
of triads reduces to classification of such choice functions.

*Why now?* `exists_table_of_fixed_points` builds the free model explicitly and
`geb_triad_second_value` shows that different choices give genuinely different
diagonal witnesses (`0` versus `3`), so the moduli problem is nonempty and
finite.

# Future Directions

Conjectures distilled from the formalization of *Various Bialgebras of
Representative Functions on Free Monoids* carried out in `Catalog/Novelty/`
(`FreeMonoidShuffle`, `FreeMonoidUnshuffle`, `FreeMonoidCharacters`,
`RepresentativeFunctions`, `DeconcatenationShuffle`,
`ShuffleCharacterNotRational`, `ShuffleOfSeries`).

Each conjecture below is stated so that it can be turned directly into a Lean
statement over the existing definitions, and each is falsifiable by an explicit
finite computation or by exhibiting a single counterexample.

---

## C1. The antipode of the shuffle Hopf algebra is the signed reversal

**Statement.** Over the definitions `shuf` (shuffle) and `deconc`
(deconcatenation coproduct) of `Catalog/Novelty/`, for every nonempty word `w`
and every field `K ⊇ ℚ`,
`Σ_{(u,v) ∈ deconc w} (-1)^{|u|} · (count z (shuf (reverse u) v)) = 0` for all
`z`, i.e. `S(w) = (-1)^{|w|} · reverse w` is the antipode of the graded Hopf
algebra `(K⟨X⟩, ⧢, Δ_deconc)`.

*The key insight is* that the already-proved bialgebra axiom
`deconc_bind_shuf` upgrades to a Hopf structure precisely because the
deconcatenation coproduct is connected and graded, so the antipode is forced by
Takeuchi's recursion — and the closed form must then be a *signed multiset
identity between shuffles of reversals*, which is a purely combinatorial claim
amenable to the counting machinery (`count_shuf_eq_count_unsh`,
`count_deconc`) already developed here.

*Why now?* All of the counting infrastructure for `shuf`, `unsh` and `deconc`
now exists and is verified; the antipode is the last missing structure map, and
it is exactly the input needed to state Sweedler duality intrinsically.

---

## C2. Rational series form a shuffle-subalgebra that is *not* closed under
the antipode-twisted inverse

**Statement.** `isRepresentative_shuffleSeries` shows rationality is preserved by
`⧢`. Conjecture: the shuffle-invertible rational series (those `f` with
`f [] ≠ 0`) do **not** form a group inside the rational series: there is a
rational `f` with `f [] = 1` whose shuffle inverse `g` (which exists uniquely as
a series) has infinite Hankel rank.

*The key insight is* that the separation already proved in
`ShuffleCharacterNotRational` — `expPlane` is a shuffle character but has
infinite Hankel rank because `det[1/(i+j)!] ≠ 0` — should be reachable from a
*rational* input by shuffle inversion, since the shuffle inverse of `1 - x` type
series is an exponential-like series with factorial denominators.

*Why now?* `factorial_relation_vanishes` gives a working, Archimedean method for
proving infinite Hankel rank; the same method should apply verbatim to the
coefficients of a shuffle inverse.

---

## C3. φ-deformations interpolate between concatenation and shuffle without
changing the rational locus

**Statement.** For a parameter `q : K`, define the `q`-shuffle on words by the
recursion `au ⧢_q bv = a(u ⧢_q bv) + b(au ⧢_q v) + q · [a=b] · ⟨ab⟩(u ⧢_q v)`.
Conjecture: for every `q`, `(K⟨X⟩, ⧢_q)` is associative and commutative, and
the set of representative functions is closed under `⧢_q` for every `q`, i.e.
the rational locus is a *deformation invariant*.

*The key insight is* that the proof of `isRepresentative_shuffleSeries` uses
only the bialgebra axiom `unsh_append` for the dual coproduct, never the precise
combinatorics of the shuffle; so any deformation whose dual coproduct is still
multiplicative for concatenation must preserve rationality.

*Why now?* The proof in `ShuffleOfSeries.lean` is already written in exactly this
"axiom-only" style, so the deformed case should require only a new
`unsh_q_append` lemma and nothing else.

---

## C4. A Ree-type criterion: rational shuffle characters are exactly the
exponentials of rational planes — and there are none but the counit

**Statement.** If `f` is a shuffle character (`f(u)f(v) = Σ_{w ∈ u ⧢ v} f(w)`)
and `f` is representative, then `f = counit` whenever the alphabet is nonempty
and `K` has characteristic 0.

*The key insight is* that `isConcatCharacter_iff_planeStar` and
`isConcatInfChar_iff_isPlane` say a character is determined by a single plane,
and the plane's exponential has factorial coefficients — the very coefficients
proved non-rational in `ShuffleCharacterNotRational`. The partial results
`planeStar_isShuffleCharacter_imp_zero` and `not_isRepresentative_expPlane`
already close the two extreme cases.

*Why now?* Only the "every shuffle character is the exponential of its
infinitesimal part" step (a Ree-type theorem over ℚ) is missing; the rest is
verified.

---

## C5. Sweedler duality is an isomorphism onto the representative functions

**Statement.** The map sending a linear representation `(λ, μ, γ)` to the series
`w ↦ λ μ(w) γ` induces a bijection between the finite-dimensional comodule
structures on `K⟨X⟩` (for `Δ_conc`) and the space of representative functions,
and it is an algebra isomorphism for both the Hadamard and the shuffle products.

*The key insight is* that `representative_tfae` already identifies "finite
dimensional space of left translates" with "has a linear representation"; adding
the shuffle multiplicativity `isRepresentative_shuffleSeries` upgrades this
bijection from a linear isomorphism to a bialgebra isomorphism — the Sweedler
dual statement of the paper.

*Why now?* Both halves (Kleene–Schützenberger and shuffle closure) are now
formalized and sorry-free; only the naturality of the correspondence remains.
