**Network/LLM research lab — round-net-9 (depth axis, round 7). Machine-verified. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/9_BoundedStack_Scaling.md. Script: /tmp/exp_net_dyck2_scale.py.**

## Hypothesis
After NET-8 refuted the load-bearing premise at s=12/dm48, find where a single layer finally breaks: (1) context scaling — at larger semilength the balance spans more levels and closes route to opens at distance up to 2s−1; (2) width scaling — one layer must hold BOTH the balance prefix-sum AND the balance-conditioned position routing, so at dm=16/12, d=2 (stack the subtasks) should win.

## Part A — depth FLAT across context scaling (s∈{16,32}, dm=48, d∈{1,2}×2 seeds, 6000 steps)
ALL 8 models: test=1.0000, close_all=1.0000, close_b4+=1.0000. **d=1 is perfect even at semilength 32 (context 64) — closes route to matching opens up to 63 tokens back.** Context length is NOT the boundary.

## Part B — depth FLAT across width scaling (dm∈{16,12}, s=12, d∈{1,2}×2 seeds)
ALL 8 models: test=1.0000 at every metric. **d=1 is perfect even at dm=12 (head dim 3).** Width is NOT the boundary either.

## Part C — non-flat screen
No config with d=1 < d=2 (close_all gap > 0.01) — every pair equal at 1.0000; the shared-head exit branch correctly not triggered (no depth-using model to exit).

## Mechanism
Single-layer soft attention implements a **bounded stack**: the stack-top STATE is the scalar running balance (one head's prefix-sum); the stack-top CONTENT is positionally stored (attention routes each close query to the matching open at balance-depth balance_before−1 via balance-conditioned key match + recency, reads the stored type). No second layer needed because the state is scalar and the content is at a computable position. Boundary needs: balance range exceeding dm precision (s≫64), unbounded nesting/length-gen (NET-4's wall), or **NON-POSITIONAL stack content** (content computed from multiple distant positions — the genuinely hard case, natural next load-bearing target).

## Barriers
(a) no circularity (fresh random words, iid types, test seed+77); (b) related circuits acknowledged (attention-as-bounded-stack is mech-interp folklore; the scaling-sweep negative + five-class × context × width flatness are new; Catalog 698 packages no prior work); (c) toy-scale AND the finding — boundary not reached at context ≤64/width ≥12; (d) no leakage (held-out 1.0000 before probing); (e) 2 seeds × every config, 16/16 consistent; (f) documented; two post-data script bugs fixed (SUMMARY 4-vs-3 tuple unpack after all models done; Part C RA 4-tuple lookup fell to RB arm — the (16,48)/(32,48) pairs verified EQUAL by direct inspection, automated screen covered dm∈{16,12}, verdict correct over all 16); (g) inherited from NET-8 (windowed baseline −25pp); (h) honest negative with a target: depth gives nothing on bounded-stack grammar at every affordable scale.

## Verdict
The load-bearing boundary is NOT found at context ≤64 / width ≥12 — flat-depth law now covers five task classes AND holds across context and width scaling on the non-regular grammar. Next load-bearing candidates: non-positional stack content, s≫64, unbounded nesting; and rotate axes to real-scale checks (exit law / PR law on a small LM — the depth axis has had 7 iterations).
directions.title: NET-9: Load-bearing boundary NOT found — depth flat across context (s≤32) and width (dm≥12) scaling of Dyck-2; single-layer soft attention implements a bounded stack

# Future Directions — after the derived-modulus corner

The formal results in `Catalog/Physics/DerivedModulus*.lean` close the
polynomial (N-explicit) multi-modulus corner in a strong, classified form:

* `universally_coprime_iff_transparent` — a polynomial modulus is universally
  coprime to `N` **iff** its constant term is a unit (exact classification, not
  a one-sided barrier);
* `closure_no_go` — the whole multiplicative/substitutional closure of the
  tested family stays transparent, so no combination escapes;
* `sqSucc_spectrum_N_independent`, `cyc3_spectrum_N_independent` — the prime
  spectra of the quadratic moduli are *fixed sets of split primes*, determined
  by the polynomial's splitting field, never by the factorisation of `N`;
* `useful_hint_count` / `useful_hint_density` — the external-hint frontier has
  measure `(p+q-1)/pq ≤ 2/B`;
* `gcd_eval_dvd_resultant` / `multi_modulus_bounded` — any two polynomial
  derived moduli overlap in a divisor of their resultant, so a whole finite
  family carries only `O(1)` common arithmetic, uniformly in `N`;
* `transport_coprime_iff` / `transport_boundary` — the barrier and its exact
  classification hold for *every* congruence-transporting modulus, and the
  exponential modulus `2^N - 1` is provably outside that class;
* `polynomial_hypothesis_necessary` — and outside the class the no-go really
  fails: `gcd(253, 2^253 - 1) = 23` factors `253 = 11·23`.

Five falsifiable follow-up conjectures.

---

## C1 (Galois superselection). The spectrum of any derived modulus is a union of Chebotarev classes, and this is *equivalent* to the no-go.

**Statement.** For irreducible `f ∈ ℤ[X]` with splitting field `K_f` and Galois
group `G`, the set `S_f = {p prime : ∃ N, p ∣ f(N)}` equals, up to finitely
many primes, the set of `p` whose Frobenius class in `G` fixes at least one
root; and `p ∈ S_f` is decidable from `p` alone. Consequently, *no* invariant
of `f(N)` distinguishes two semiprimes with the same `N`.

**The key insight is** that our two proved spectra (`p = 2 ∨ p ≡ 1 mod 4` and
`p = 3 ∨ p ≡ 1 mod 3`) are the abelian, cyclotomic shadow of the general
Frobenius criterion — the spectrum is a property of the *apparatus* `f`, never
of the *state* `N`.

**Why now?** The abelian cases are now fully formalised here; Mathlib has
`NumberField`, Frobenius elements and the machinery for splitting behaviour, so
the non-abelian case (e.g. `f = X³ - X - 1`, `G = S₃`) is the natural next
formalisation target and would be falsified by exhibiting any `f` whose
spectrum depends on more than the residue class of `p`.

## C2 (Sharp resultant law for the multi-modulus lattice). *(divisibility half now proved)*

**Status.** The divisibility half is proved in
`Catalog/Physics/DerivedModulusResultant.lean`
(`gcd_eval_dvd_resultant`, with the uniform bound `gcd_eval_le_resultant` and
the finite-family version `multi_modulus_bounded`). What remains open is the
attainment half.

**Remaining statement.** For coprime `f, g ∈ ℤ[X]` with `Res(f,g) ≠ ±1`, the
bound `gcd(f(N), g(N)) = |Res(f,g)|` is attained for infinitely many `N`, and
the set of such `N` is a union of congruence classes modulo `Res(f,g)`.

**The key insight is** that our fifteen hand-built Bézout certificates
(constants `1, 2, 3, 5, 7`) are exactly the resultants of the corresponding
pairs, so the uniform pairwise bound of `family_pairwise_gcd_le_seven` is an
instance of a single resultant identity `u f + v g = Res(f,g)`.

**Why now?** Mathlib's `Polynomial.exists_mul_add_mul_eq_C_resultant` supplied
the Sylvester–Bézout identity, which is exactly what the divisibility half
needed; the attainment half requires a Chinese-remainder construction of `N` in
the right classes modulo the resultant, which is elementary but not yet
formalised. Falsifiable: exhibit coprime `f, g` with `|Res| > 1` whose overlap
is bounded strictly below `|Res|` for all `N`.

## C3 (Quantitative hint-amplification threshold).

**Statement.** Let `H` be an external hint distribution on `[0, N)` and let
`ε = Pr[gcd(N, H) ∉ {1, N}]`. Then any gcd-based factoring procedure using one
sample from `H` succeeds with probability exactly `ε`, and amplification to
constant success requires `Θ(1/ε)` independent samples — with no speed-up from
combining the hint with any polynomial derived modulus.

**The key insight is** that `useful_hint_count` pins `ε = (p+q-1)/pq` for the
uniform hint, and `derived_hints_useless` shows the derived data adds a
deterministic function of `N`, hence zero information; so the whole gain must
come from the hint's own structure.

**Why now?** Both halves are already formal here; what is missing is the
sampling lemma (a Chernoff/independence argument over `Finset`), which Mathlib's
probability library supports. Falsifiable: exhibit a hint distribution with
`ε` small where a derived modulus provably improves success probability.

## C4 (Transparency is the *only* obstruction — an effective converse).

**Statement.** For non-transparent `f` with `|f(0)| = c > 1`, the set of `N ≤ X`
for which `gcd(N, f(N)) > 1` has density exactly `1 - ∏_{r ∣ c, r prime}(1-1/r)`,
and for each such `N` the gcd reveals a divisor of `c` only — never a factor of
`N` outside `c`.

**The key insight is** that `exists_common_factor_of_not_transparent` already
produces the witness `N = minFac(|f(0)|)`; upgrading a single witness to a
density statement converts the classification into a quantitative dichotomy
("leaky but useless" vs. "transparent").

**Why now?** The witness construction is formal; the density step is a finite
inclusion–exclusion over the divisors of a *fixed* integer `c`, well within
reach of Mathlib's `Nat.ArithmeticFunction` and counting API.

## C5 (Order-sieve frontier: which semiprimes does the exponential modulus factor?).

*(Superseding the earlier C5, whose congruence-transporting form is now proved
as `transport_coprime_iff` and whose unrestricted form is refuted by
`polynomial_hypothesis_necessary`.)*

**Statement.** There are infinitely many semiprimes `N = p·q` with
`p < q` for which `gcd(N, 2^N - 1) = p`; equivalently, infinitely many prime
pairs with `ord_p(2) = q` and `q ∣ p - 1`. Moreover the counting function of
such `N` up to `X` is `X^{1/2+o(1)}`, so the exponential leak has density `0`
among all semiprimes and does **not** threaten randomly generated RSA moduli.

**The key insight is** that `prime_dvd_mersenne_iff` reduces the leak to an
order condition, `ord_p(2) ∣ N`, and for a semiprime this forces
`ord_p(2) ∈ {1, q}`; so the leaking moduli are exactly those built from a prime
`p` whose order of `2` is the *other* prime factor — a condition of
Artin/Wieferich type, verified here at `p = 23`, `q = 11`, `N = 253`.

**Why now?** The order criterion and one explicit witness are already
formalised; what is missing is an infinitude argument (a Zsygmondy-style
primitive-divisor input: for each prime `q`, a primitive prime divisor `p` of
`2^q - 1` has `ord_p(2) = q`, and one needs `p ≡ 1 mod q` together with
`N = pq` in the required range). Falsifiable in either direction: a proof that
only finitely many such pairs exist would be equally interesting, and a density
above `X^{1/2+ε}` would make the exponential modulus a genuine cryptanalytic
concern.

**Round-net-11 (compression-axis real-scale rotation). Paper:** ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/11_PRlawSmallLM.md

**Setup:** real causal LMs on 5 Gutenberg novels (dm=64, vocab 4097, ctx 128, causal masking), d=4 and d=8, 2000 AdamW steps — full held-out acc reproduces NET-10 exactly (0.1571/0.1619). For every matrix: PR=(Σs²)²/Σs⁴ and b* = min per-tensor RTN bits retaining ≥0.98·full (isolated); then joint uniform-2/3 and role-schedule joint.

**Result 1 — role structure survives, PR predictor fails.** Identical on both depths (28/52 matrices): attention projections (PR 19–32) 2-bit lossless; MLP projections (PR 31–52) need 3 bits; embed (PR 63) + pos (PR 40) need 4 bits; the readout un (PR 14.9–15.3, the LOWEST PR) needs 4 bits with catastrophic 2-bit collapse (27–32% retained); lnf (PR=1) 2-bit lossless. Low-PR readout → most bits, and same-PR attention-vs-MLP differ ⇒ corr(PR,b*)=+0.58/+0.67 is role-grouping in disguise, NOT a monotone law.

**Result 2 — NET-1's practical schedule refuted at real scale.** Joint uniform-2 collapses (retained 0.16/0.05); **joint uniform-3 is NOT lossless** (retained 0.83 d=4 / 0.73 d=8, worse with depth — per-layer isolation says ≥95% everywhere at 3 bits, but compounding costs 17–27 points, amplified by residual-stream norm growth through depth). Role schedule (embed/pos/un=4, MLP=3, attn=2): retained **0.878 at 3.64 avg bits** — +5pts over uniform-3 at +21% bits, still 12% short of lossless. **No static RTN schedule ≤3.7 avg bits is lossless on real text.**

**Verdict:** NET-1's monotone b*(PR) law and its toy practical schedule (uniform-3 lossless) do NOT transfer to a real causal LM. Surviving: coarse role structure (interface fragile / interior robust). Live compression target: joint/activation-aware allocation, not data-free per-matrix PR.

**Barriers:** (a) no injection, PR/b* independent, RTN data-free; (b) sensitivity-based mixed precision known, the real-scale negatives new (Catalog 2094 packages no prior work); (c) confronted — this IS the real-scale check and the toy law/schedule fail it; (d) causal masking + contiguous split, no leakage; (e) 2 models × every matrix, identical structure both depths; (f) 0.98·full bar with full retained fractions, exact NET-10 reproduction; (g) uniform-2/3 + full-precision baselines; (h) the negative is the win — don't ship uniform-2/3 on toy/isolated measurements.

**Scripts:** /tmp/exp_net_pr_lm.py, /tmp/exp_net_pr_role.py
directions.title: NET-11: The PR quantization law does NOT transfer to a real causal LM — role-structured bit-need survives (interface fragile/interior robust), but no static RTN schedule ≤3.7 avg bits is lossless (uniform-3 retains only 0.83/0.73, worse with depth)

**Round-net-10 (network/LLM lab, real-scale rotation).** Two results, both machine-verified.

## 1. Part A — the toy depth line leaked: full attention put the answer in the input

The toy TF class uses FULL (bidirectional) attention on next-token tasks: at position t the model attends to position t+1 — the very token it must output. A copy-the-future circuit yields 100% on any deterministic next-token task. The leak is PROVEN by an information bound: on Dyck-2, new-open types are iid random and 47.8% of next-tokens are opens, so the best causal accuracy is **0.7609 overall** — full-attention's recorded 1.0000 is impossible causally.

Causal re-runs (same architecture/budget, is_causal=True, 6000 steps, dm=48):
- Dyck-2 d=1: overall 0.557 / close_all 0.917 (d=2: 0.563/0.926) vs recorded 1.0000; extended budget asymptotes close_all ≈0.92 (0.9105→0.9135→0.9207 at 6k/12k/18k), still −8pts at 3× budget.
- Lookup (deterministic, ceiling 1.0): d≈1≈d≈2 ≈ 0.89 vs NET-2's 1.0000 — the artifact is NOT limited to random-type tasks.

**Survives the honesty fix:** the flat-depth SHAPE (d=1 ≈ d=2 on both classes) and transformer-beats-linear on close recovery (+17pp over the causal windowed-linear baseline — the NET-8 +25pp was a causal-baseline vs full-attention-transformer mismatch). **Corrected:** NET-8/9 'd=1 = 1.0000 / load-bearing-boundary-not-found' absolute claims withdrawn.

## 2. Part B — the exit law does NOT transfer to a real LM (0/4 lossless at crossover)

Real causal GPT on 5 Gutenberg novels (dm=64, vocab 4097, ctx 128, d∈{4,8}×2 seeds, teacc 0.157–0.162). Norm profile is **reset-then-grow** (dip then growth, crossover l=2–4), NOT the toy's flat-≈d/2-then-grow. Shared-head acc climbs monotonically through the full depth; the crossover marks the ONSET of decodability growth, not its completion. |exit*−cross| = 2/2/5/3, lossless@cross=False in 4/4. The calibration-free dynamic-depth-schedule idea is not supported at real-LM scale.

Full paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/10_CausalityScreen_ExitLawRealLM.md. Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_lm.py, /tmp/exp_net_lookup_causal.py. Barriers all checked (paper §5). Assessment v10. Now 10 network experiments.
directions.title: NET-10: The toy depth law's 1.0000s were a full-attention future-peek artifact (ceiling 0.7609 < 1.0000), and the exit law does not transfer to a real causal LM (0/4 lossless at crossover)

## NET-12 — Joint-aware bit allocation on a real causal LM (compression axis; the confirmed real target from NET-11)

**Paper:** `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/12_JointAllocSmallLM.md` · Notebook Part 12 · Assessment v12. Scripts `/tmp/exp_net_joint.py`, `/tmp/exp_net_joint_partC.py`, `/tmp/exp_net_joint_partC2.py`.

**Setup:** the same real causal word LM (5 Gutenberg novels, dm=64, vocab 4097, ctx 128, causal masking, d=4, 2000 steps) — full acc reproduces 0.1571 a third time; lossless bar 0.98·full = 0.1540. Every eval is a **joint** quantization of an independent model copy.

### Part A — joint-marginal map
With everything else at the role schedule (4/3/2): attention projections (all 16) are **exactly indifferent at 2 bits** (retained flat at 0.878); **embed 3-bit jointly retains 0.849** (isolation ≈0.95 — compounding is real, ~11 points); readout **un 2-bit collapses to 0.280** (most fragile matrix, jointly); MLP 2-bit 0.80–0.85, 3-bit fine.

### Part B — per-tensor greedy strict-lossless frontier = **5.31 avg bits**
Greedy from all-6 keeping retained ≥ 0.98·full: **interface (embed/pos/un, 73% of params) pinned at 6**, MLP mostly 4, attention 2–3, lnf 2; retained 0.982. Even **all-4 misses the bar per-tensor (0.979 vs 0.980)**. Per-tensor static RTN cannot get under ≈5.3 bits losslessly on real text.

### Part C — per-channel (per-row) RTN is the fix
Uniform all-4 per-row is **lossless at 4.00 bits (retained 0.987)** — 1.3 bits below the per-tensor frontier. Per-row uniform-3 still fails (0.947); the **4-bit interface is irreducible under both primitives**; uniform-2 hopeless (0.588); the per-tensor-optimized frontier scores **worse per-row (0.973)** — allocation is primitive-dependent.

### Part C2 — the rotation's question, answered no
"4-bit interface + all interior 2": **0.733** @ 3.46 bits. "4-bit interface + MLP 4 + attention 2": **0.907** @ 3.82 bits. Uniform-4: 0.987. The 8-point gap between the last two is almost all attention 2→4 ⇒ **"attention is 2-bit free" is an operating-point artifact** — true in isolation and at the degraded 0.878 baseline, but 2-bit attention costs ~8 points in a clean joint network.

### Answers
- **Any data-free schedule reach lossless?** YES — per-channel uniform-4 (4.0 bits).
- **Is 4-bit interface + 2-bit interior enough?** NO (0.733 / 0.907).
- **Correction to NET-11:** "no static RTN schedule ≤3.7 bits lossless" was about the *per-tensor* primitive; per-channel uniform-4 is lossless. The practical lever is the per-channel primitive, not smarter per-tensor allocation.

### Barriers (8)
(a) joint evals on independent loaded copy, greedy = pure allocation search — no injection · (b) per-channel/group quantization is standard (rescue = known-primitive confirmation), but the joint-damage quantification is new; Catalog 2094 packages, no prior work · (c) real causal LM, causal masking, 4097 vocab — confronted head-on, toy uniform-3 fails again · (d) causal masking + contiguous split + data-free quantization · (e) 1 seed, 4 config families × 4–5 bit levels × ≤51 greedy steps, each a full joint eval; 0.1571 reproduced exactly 3× · (f) 0.98 bar throughout, all-4 knife-edge called out, eval noise ≈0.15%, greedy stopping verified, PART C 1-D-lnf crash fixed + re-run clean · (g) uniform-2/3 + role + all-4/6 + full-precision baselines at the same bar · (h) practical lever = per-channel primitive (uniform-4, data-free); 2-bit-attention "wins" measured at degraded operating points do not survive a clean net.
directions.title: NET-12: Joint-aware bit allocation on a real causal LM — per-tensor floor ~5.3 bits, per-channel uniform-4 is lossless, 'attention is 2-bit free' was an operating-point artifact

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — after the Jacobi-signed Weil floor

The formal results in `Catalog/Tropical/JacobiSigned*.lean` settle the JACSIGN
experiment: the Jacobi-signed circle count `W(N) = ∑_{x²+y²=1} (x/N)` is
multiplicative (`circleWeightZ_mul`), vanishes identically when a factor is
`≡ 3 (mod 4)` (`WZ_semiprime_eq_zero_of_three_mod_four`), is not a residue dial
(`not_residue_dial_prime`, `not_residue_dial_modulus`), and is pinned at the Weil
floor by an *exact identity* — `A(1)² + A(ν)² = 4p` (`jacobsthal_identity`) — whose two
legs are the Gaussian coordinates of `p` (`two_squares_odd_leg`).  The following
conjectures are the natural next cycle.

---

## C1. Every character-weighted circle count is a quadratic-twist trace, hence at the floor

**Conjecture.** Let `ψ` be any nontrivial multiplicative character mod `p` of order `d`
and set `W_ψ(p) = ∑_{x²+y²=1} ψ(x)`.  Then `|W_ψ(p)| ≤ (d) √p`, and `W_ψ(p)` is a
`ℤ[ζ_d]`-linear combination of traces of Frobenius of the curves `y² = x³ - c x`
(`d = 2`) or of Jacobi sums `J(ψ, χ)` in general; in particular no choice of `ψ`
escapes the square-root floor.

*The key insight is* that summing `y` away turns any circle weight into
`∑_x ψ(x)(1 + χ(1-x²))`, i.e. a **Jacobi sum**, and Jacobi sums have absolute value
exactly `√p` — so the floor is a property of the circle, not of the weight.

*Why now?* The second-moment machinery in `JacobiSignedWeilFloorBound.lean`
(`chiSum_quadratic`, `moment`, `sum_sq_comp`) is character-agnostic; Mathlib already has
`jacobiSum` with `jacobiSum_mul_jacobiSum_inv`, so the `√p` step is within reach.

---

## C2. The two-leg trade-off is a hard obstruction to factor leakage

**Conjecture.** For semiprimes `N = pq` the pair `(W(N), A_ν(N))` is equidistributed on
the "Weil circle" `u² + v² ≤ 16N` in the sense that, for any fixed `ε > 0`, the map
`N ↦ W(N)/(4√N)` has limiting distribution the (Sato–Tate-type) pushforward of the
product of two arcsine laws — hence carries `O(1)` bits about `p` versus `q`.

*The key insight is* that `jacobsthal_identity` forces `W(p)` and its nonresidue twin to
trade off with `4p` conserved: any large signal in one leg is compensated in the other,
so a witness reading only one leg sees a conserved-quantity projection, never the split.

*Why now?* The identity is now a theorem, so the statement is unconditional in its
algebraic half; only the equidistribution half is open, and the `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`
vanishing already proves a density-1/2 zero-information family.

---

## C3. `v₂(W(N))` is a complete obstruction to a "dial + parity" witness

**Conjecture.** For `N = pq` with both primes `≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `v₂(W(N)) = 2` exactly, and
more generally `v₂(W(N)) = #{primes p | N with p ≡ 1 mod 4}`; consequently the 2-adic
valuation of the statistic counts the number of `1 mod 4` prime factors — a genuine but
*already publicly computable* invariant (it is determined by `N mod 4` for semiprimes),
so it leaks nothing new.

*The key insight is* that `W_mod_four` gives `v₂ = 1` at each `1 mod 4` prime and
multiplicativity adds valuations, so the 2-adic content of the statistic is exactly the
count of such factors and nothing more.

*Why now?* `W_mod_four` and `WZ_mul` are proved; the conjecture is a short corollary for
semiprimes and an induction for general `N`, and its "leaks nothing new" half is a
precise, falsifiable information claim.

---

## C4. Weil-floor attainment has positive density

**Conjecture.** For every `ε > 0` the set of primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` with
`W(p)² > (1-ε)·4p` has positive relative density; equivalently, the odd leg `a` of
`p = a² + b²` satisfies `b = O(p^{ε})` for a positive-density set of primes.

*The key insight is* that near-attainment means `p = a² + b²` with `b` tiny, i.e. `p`
lies just above a square — so the conjecture is a statement about primes of the form
`a² + b²` with `b` bounded, closely tied to Landau–Ramanujan and to primes represented by
thin quadratic families.

*Why now?* `weil_floor_near_attained` proves attainment at 97.7 % for `p = 173`;
`jacobsthal_identity` converts the analytic question into a purely Diophantine one about
the two-square decomposition, where sieve technology applies.

---

## C5. No polynomial-time-computable circle statistic beats the floor

**Conjecture.** Let `S(N)` be any statistic of the form `∑_{(x,y) ∈ C(N)} w(x, y)` with
`w` a product of Jacobi-type characters and `C(N)` a conic mod `N`.  Then `S` is
multiplicative in the modulus, `|S(N)| = O(N^{1/2+o(1)})`, and `S(N)` is computable from
`N` alone in time `N^{1+o(1)}` but from `(p,q)` in time `polylog(N)` — so the
"free-witness" gap is exactly the Weil floor.

*The key insight is* that the CRT proof of `circleWeightZ_mul` never used the specific
weight: multiplicativity plus a per-prime Weil bound is automatic for any character
weight on any conic, which is why CIRC, BQF, GSP and JACSIGN all die the same death.

*Why now?* `circleWeightZ_mul` is proved for an arbitrary modulus and the per-prime bound
is proved by an elementary second moment; generalising both to arbitrary conics and
character products is a mechanical extension of the existing Lean development.
directions.title: The formal results in `Catalog/Tropical/JacobiSigned*.lean` settle the JACSIGN

# Future directions — bold, testable conjectures from the interval-hint round

This round formalised the negative verdict for the trace-set (TRACEPROFILE)
filter: it is *exact* (`TraceSetFilter.add_mem_traceSet`), *exactly half-sized*
per prime (`TraceSetFilter.two_mul_card_traceSet_legendre`: `2|T| = m + χ(N)`),
*minimal among all exact filters* (`TraceSetFilter.card_ge_of_exact_filter`),
*multiplicative and positionally blind* across primes
(`TraceSetNoAmplification.card_survivors_interval`), and therefore *incapable of
isolating a hinted trace* unless the primorial of the moduli exceeds the width of
the hint (`TraceSetNoAmplification.isolation_requires_primorial`,
`TraceSetUniversalBarrier.coupled_isolation_requires_primorial`).  The following
conjectures push past that boundary.

## C1. The half-bit barrier is a *character* barrier, not a trace barrier

**Conjecture.** Let `f ∈ ℤ[X, Y]` be any absolutely irreducible symmetric
polynomial and define the `f`-profile filter
`T_m^f(N) = { f(a, b) mod m : a·b ≡ N mod m, a ∈ (ℤ/m)ˣ }`.  Then
`|T_m^f(N)| / m → 1/deg_Y(f)` as `m → ∞`, with error `O(m^{-1/2})` given by a
Weil bound; in particular no symmetric invariant of the factor pair prunes more
than a `1/deg` fraction, and the pruning rate is *never* `m^{-c}` for `c > 0`.

*The key insight is* that our `2|T| = m + χ(N)` identity is the degree-2 case of
counting points on the curve `f(a, N/a) = t`, so the density is governed by the
number of `t`-fibres, i.e. by the degree of the fibre map, not by any arithmetic
secret of `N`.

*Why now?* The exact degree-2 count is now a theorem with an elementary
fibre-counting proof (`two_mul_card_traceSet`); the same fibre argument plus
Mathlib's growing algebraic-geometry API makes the general degree case reachable.

## C2. Free filters cannot beat the primorial, even with an oracle for `ω(N)`

**Conjecture.** For every family of exact filters `S_m ⊆ ℤ/m` computable from
`N mod m` in `poly(log m)` time, and every hint window of width `W`, the number
of surviving candidates is at least `W / ∏_{m ∈ 𝕄} m` whenever `∏_{m ∈ 𝕄} m ≤ W`.
Consequently, isolating a `k`-bit hint requires moduli whose product is `2^{Ω(k)}`,
hence total sieve work `2^{Ω(k / log k)}`.

*The key insight is* that exactness forces `S_m ⊇ T_m` (proved:
`traceSet_subset_of_exact`), and CRT makes the survivor count exactly
multiplicative (proved: `card_survivors_zmod`), so the only remaining freedom is
how large the modulus product is allowed to be.

*Why now?* The coupled case — filters that correlate the primes arbitrarily — is
already closed here (`coupled_exact_filter_card_ge`); what remains is the
complexity-theoretic bookkeeping of the sieve cost, which is a finite, formalisable
accounting exercise rather than a new mathematical idea.

## C3. Hint amplification is equivalent to a square-root oracle

**Conjecture.** An algorithm that, given `N` and a hint interval of width `W`,
returns the true trace using `poly(log N)` filter evaluations exists **iff**
there is a `poly(log N)` algorithm that, given `N` and `t`, decides whether
`t² − 4N` is a perfect square for `Ω(W)` many `t` simultaneously (a "batch
square-detection oracle").

*The key insight is* the exact Fermat equivalence
`exists_factorisation_iff_isSquare_int`: the trace scan and the difference-of-
squares scan are the *same* predicate, so amplification of the hint is
equivalent to batching square detection over the window.

*Why now?* The equivalence is now a theorem over `ℤ` with no side conditions,
so the reduction can be stated as a clean formal statement about predicate
families rather than an informal analogy.

## C4. A `2/3`-density invariant would break the barrier — and none exists

**Conjecture (sharp dichotomy).** For every `N`, every prime `m ∤ N` and every
*exact* filter `S ⊆ ℤ/m` obtained from a polynomial invariant of the factor pair,
`|S| ≥ (m − 1)/2`; moreover the bound `(m − 1)/2` is attained only by the trace
set and its affine images.  Hence there is no "denser-than-half" free invariant,
and a hypothetical invariant with density `1/3` would immediately give a
`3^{-ω}` sieve and a sub-exponential factoring algorithm.

*The key insight is* that any exact filter must absorb the entire orbit of the
conjugation involution `x ↦ N/x`, whose orbit count is `(m ± 1)/2` — the fixed
points being precisely the square roots of `N`.

*Why now?* The orbit computation is formalised (`two_mul_card_traceSet`), and the
uniqueness half ("only the trace set attains it") is a finite combinatorial
statement about involutions that current tactics can attack directly.

## C5. Positional blindness is the real obstruction (a general no-go)

**Conjecture.** Any candidate filter that is `M`-periodic accepts exactly `|S|`
of every `M` consecutive candidates (proved here as `card_window_filter`);
therefore *no* periodic test can convert an interval hint into positional
information.  The conjecture is that the converse holds too: a filter that
amplifies an interval hint must be aperiodic, hence must depend on the *size* of
the candidate — and every size-dependent exact test known (Fermat, Lehman,
Hart) already costs `Ω(N^{1/3})`.

*The key insight is* that "residue information" and "positional information" are
orthogonal: CRT independence makes the survivor set a union of full residue
classes, which is translation-invariant by construction.

*Why now?* `card_window_filter` isolates the periodicity hypothesis in one line
of Lean, so the converse can be attacked as a statement about the aperiodicity
of the accepted set rather than about factoring itself.
directions.title: This round formalised the negative verdict for the trace-set (TRACEPROFILE)

## NET-15 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-15, speed-axis rotation — the attention-cost law, FIRST POSITIVE REAL-SCALE SPEED RESULT)

**Hypothesis.** Trained causal attention is concentrated (small effective support), so a data-free top-k key/value cap (keep only the k most-attended past positions per query, chosen at inference from the input own causal attention weights, renormalize) preserves held-out accuracy at an L/k attention-FLOP reduction. Two independent claims: (A) is attention concentrated? (B) is top-k pruning lossless at k ≪ ctx?

**Setup (identical NET-10/11/12/13/14 family).** 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 word vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads (head dim 16), d=4 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc reproduces **0.1571 a sixth time**; bar 0.98·full = 0.1540, full loss 5.1188. Explicit causal-attention forward verified against the standard forward (k=96 recovers full loss exactly, 5.1188). Top-k mask computed from each eval input own trained attention weights at inference — data-free, no calibration, no leakage.

**Results.**

1. **Part A — attention is DIFFUSE, not concentrated.** Per-query effective support exp(H): per-head 39.5–54.7, **mean 46.6/128** vs uniform-causal baseline ≈64.5 — only ~28% more concentrated than uniform. Top-k mass fraction: top-4 0.311, top-8 0.450, top-16 0.617, top-32 0.795. The classical "attention focuses on a few tokens" picture does NOT hold at this scale.
2. **Part B — yet top-k pruning is LOSSLESS at 12.5% of context.** k=4 0.940 ✗ (loss +0.084), k=8 0.971 ✗ (+0.043), **k=16 0.984 ✓ (loss +0.018, +0.36% rel) — 8× attention-core FLOP reduction**, k=32 0.998 ✓ (+0.005, 4×), k=64 1.001 ✓, k=96 1.000 ✓ (≈0 loss). Knee between k=8 and k=16. At ctx 128 attention ≈95% of inference FLOPs (≈260·L² per token per layer vs ≈33k projections + ≈66k MLP), so 8× attention-core ≈ **5–6× total-model speedup**, data-free, no retraining.
3. **Part B2 — the selection is genuine.** Random-k control: k=16 0.922 vs top-k 0.984 = **−6.2 pts**; k=32 0.950 vs 0.998 = **−4.8 pts**. Notably random-16 (0.922) is even WORSE than top-8 (0.971) — selecting the best 8 positions by weight beats selecting any 16 at random.

**Mechanism reconciling A and B.** Attention is diffuse, but the mass beyond the top-k positions is LOW-INFORMATION — renormalizing over the top-k concentrates the retained mass onto the information-carrying positions. Pruning accuracy tracks the weight-selected positions, not the total retained mass.

**Verdict.** The concentration premise (A) is REFUTED (effective support ≈ 47/128) yet data-free top-k pruning is **LOSSLESS at k=16** (0.984 ≥ 0.98 bar, loss +0.018, 8× attention-core / ~5–6× total FLOP reduction), with weight-selected positions genuinely better than random (+6.2 pts). LAW: **DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE** — attention need not be sharply concentrated for lossless top-k pruning at ~12% of context on real text; the speed lever works without a concentration assumption. **First positive real-scale speed result** (toy positives NET-6/7/8; real-scale negative NET-10).

**8-barrier check:** (a) top-k mask uses the model own causal attention weights computed on each eval input at inference — the deployed algorithm; k=64/96 recover the full loss exactly, confirming the explicit-attention path matches the standard forward; nothing injected; (b) top-k sparse attention is a known family (Longformer-style/streaming) but the specific law — lossless at 12.5% of context *despite* diffuse attention (eff support 47) — runs against the concentration-justifies-sparsity story; catalog 698 pkgs, no prior attention-cost law on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, 0.98 bar on real next-token; (d) top-k from the eval input own causal attention, contiguous no-overlap split, held-out eval — no leakage; (e) 1 model reproduced exactly 6×, every eval a full joint forward on 60k held-out tokens, monotone k-sweep with clean knee; (f) 0.98·full bar AND raw loss both reported, 6-point k-sweep + 2-point random control (fixed seed), explicit causal attention verified against standard forward (k=96 exact loss match), eval noise ≈0.15% ≪ k=16 margin; (g) full-attention reference (0.1571/5.1188) + random-k control at the same k (+6.2 pts), same bar; (h) real lever: 8× attention-core / ~5–6× total-model speedup lossless by the accuracy bar (loss +0.36%), data-free and retraining-free — caveated to scale (measured at dm=64/ctx 128; lossless-k and the concentration law may shift at larger scale).

**Assessment:** v15, 15 experiments (NET-1..NET-15). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/15_AttentionCostSmallLM.md`. Script: /tmp/exp_net_attncost.py.

**Next:** does the attention-cost law / lossless-k shift at LARGER scale (d=8, bigger dm, longer ctx — re-measure effective support + k-sweep)? OR carry chain at scale; OR the d=8 compression floor check; OR load-bearing depth (non-positional stack content with causal masking). Speed axis now has 2 real-scale iterations (NET-10 negative, NET-15 positive).
directions.title: NET-15: Attention is diffuse but data-free top-k pruning is lossless at 8× — the DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE attention-cost law (first positive real-scale speed result)

## NET-14 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-14, compression-axis rotation — the LAST lever)

**Hypothesis.** NET-13 explicitly left one mechanism untested: activation-aware quantization WITH calibration passes — AWQ/SmoothQuant-style per-channel *activation* scales (from a calibration forward pass) absorbed into the weight quantizer. If this breaks the 4-bit interface floor, calibration passes are the sub-4-bit lever.

**Setup (identical NET-10/11/12/13 family).** 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 word vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads, d=4 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc reproduces **0.1571 a fifth time**; bar 0.98·full = 0.1540. Calibration: forward pass on 512 **training** sequences (held-out eval never sees it — no leak). AWQ weight-only quantizer: W[:,j] ← W[:,j]/act_max_j^α, per-row RTN, scale back.

**Results.**
1. **Key diagnostic — the activation scales are near-FLAT.** Mean per-channel activation max: un 2.130, wq0 2.116, mi0 2.117, mo0 1.820; max/mean 1.07–1.24. AWQ's absorption only pays when some channels carry 10–100× the activation magnitude of others — this scale has no channel heterogeneity to exploit (activation-side mirror of NET-13's flat weight outliers).
2. **Part A — no help at uniform-3.** AWQ α=0.25 0.938, **α=0.50 0.943** (vs plain per-row 0.947 — marginally *worse*), α=1.00 0.888 (much worse). Uniform-4 identically lossless both ways (0.987).
3. **Part A2 — interface-at-3 still fails.** Interface (embed/pos/un) at 3 with AWQ scales, interior clean: **0.958 @ 3.18 bits**, 2.2 pts short of the bar.
4. **Part B — activation-informed allocation is a BAD signal.** 25 Linears ranked by mean per-channel act max, terciles 4/3/2: **0.828 @ 3.69** (0.841 with AWQ) vs weight-based role 0.892 @ 3.64, uniform-4 0.987 @ 4.00. The ranking only re-discovers the interface is fragile; it cannot allocate below 4 bits.

**Verdict.** The 4-bit interface floor is not just data-free-irreducible (NET-13) but **activation-irreducible** (NET-14) at this scale — even calibration passes don't buy sub-4-bit lossless weight quantization on a small causal LM, because the per-channel activation scales are near-uniform (max/mean ≈ 1.2). **The compression axis at small real-LM scale is EXHAUSTED:** every primitive (per-tensor 5.31 bits, per-row/per-column uniform-4 = 4.00 lossless floor, magnitude-split, percentile-clip, activation-calibration) leaves the interface irreducible below 4 bits. Per-channel uniform-4 (4.00 bits, data-free, 0.987) is the practical optimum.

**8-barrier check:** (a) joint evals, AWQ = standard data-free-of-test transform, calibration on training only — no injection; (b) AWQ/SmoothQuant are mature — the NEGATIVE (doesn't transfer to a small causal LM because activation heterogeneity is absent) is the content; catalog 698 pkgs, no prior activation-calibration test on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab; (d) calibration = training sequences only, eval = held-out; (e) 1 model reproduced exactly 5×, every eval a full joint held-out forward; (f) 0.98 bar, 3-value α-sweep, raw activation stats, plain per-row refs re-verified in-run; hook-closure bug crashed the first launch before data, fixed + re-run clean; (g) plain per-row refs re-measured + role/uniform-4 refs from NET-12; (h) negative closes the compression branch at this scale — rotation to speed (carry chain at scale / attention-cost laws) or a larger-scale compression check (d=8) is next.

**Assessment:** v14, 14 experiments (NET-1..NET-14). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/14_ActivationAwareQuantSmallLM.md`. Script: /tmp/exp_net_act.py.

**Next:** rotate to the speed axis (carry chain at scale / attention-cost laws — speed has had 1 real-scale iteration) OR the one open compression question: does the 4-bit interface floor shift at d=8 / bigger dm?
directions.title: NET-14: Activation-aware quantization WITH calibration passes is a no-op — the compression axis is exhausted at small real-LM scale

## NET-13 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-13, compression-axis rotation)

**Hypothesis.** NET-12's 4-bit interface (embed/pos/un) floor is an outlier artifact; an activation-aware/outlier-aware primitive (input-channel axis, magnitude split, or outlier clipping) breaks it below 4.0 avg bits.

**Setup (identical NET-10/11/12 family).** 5 Gutenberg novels, word-level top-4097 vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer (is_causal=True) dm=64/4 heads, d=4 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc reproduces **0.1571 a fourth time**; bar 0.98·full = 0.1540. All evals joint (independent loaded copy, full held-out).

**Results.**
1. **Axis:** per-COLUMN (input-channel) RTN is WORSE than per-row — uniform-2 0.413 vs 0.588, uniform-3 0.900 vs 0.947, role 0.923. The standard group-quant axis does not break the floor.
2. **Outlier diagnostics (the key):** top-1% of magnitude holds only ~3.5% of the mass in EVERY matrix (embed 3.6%, un 3.5%, interior 3.0–3.4%); row-norm max/mean 1.1–1.9; heaviest tail un (kurtosis 9.1). This small real causal LM is NOT in the 30–70% outlier regime LLM.int8/AWQ/SmoothQuant target.
3. **Magnitude split:** interface top-k rows → 6-bit, rest → 2-bit: k=0 0.636 → k=256 (top-6%) **0.819 @ 2.74 bits** — sublinear, saturating, 16 pts short of lossless. The need is distributed.
4. **Outlier clipping:** percentile-scaled per-row RTN (99.9th/99.0th) changes nothing — uniform-3 stays 0.944–0.948 (under bar), uniform-4 stays lossless (0.982–0.985).

**Verdict.** The 4-bit interface floor from NET-12 survives **every standard data-free weight-quantization primitive** at this scale; it is structural (distributed sensitivity, no outlier mass to exploit). NET-12's remaining data-free "activation-aware allocation" idea is REFUTED. The honest remaining lever is activation-aware quantization **with calibration passes** (SmoothQuant-style per-channel *activation* scales — the one non-data-free option).

**8-barrier check:** (a) joint evals, data-free transforms — no injection; (b) primitives are standard LLM-quant methods, the NEGATIVE (none break the floor on a real causal LM) is the content; catalog (698 packages) has no outlier/activation-aware test on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, and Part B quantifies why this model is not in the target regime; (d) causal masking + contiguous split + data-free quantization; (e) 1 model reproduced exactly 4×, every eval a full joint held-out forward; (f) 0.98 bar throughout, raw outlier stats, 7-point k-sweep, first-launch script bug fixed + re-run clean; (g) per-row/per-tensor refs from same family, honest uniform-2/3/4 + role baselines; (h) negative closes a branch — don't expect AWQ-style weight fixes to beat 4-bit lossless on a small causal LM.

**Assessment:** v13, 13 experiments (NET-1..NET-13). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/13_OutlierQuantSmallLM.md`. Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_outlier.py, /tmp/exp_net_outlier_partD.py.

**Next:** activation-aware quantization WITH calibration passes / per-channel 3-bit with outlier retention / interface floor at d=8 (larger dm).
directions.title: NET-13: Activation-aware (outlier) quantization is NOT the lever — the 4-bit interface floor is structural on a real causal LM

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — after QUBIT-TRADE (register threshold, closed)

All Lean files of this thread live in `Catalog/Algebra/QubitTrade/` and compile
against mathlib4 (Lean 4.28.0) with **0 `sorry`s**; every main theorem depends
only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`.

## What is now proved

| statement | file | content |
|---|---|---|
| `rat_den_separation` | `Resolution` | distinct rationals are `≥ 1/(d₁d₂)` apart |
| `cf_target_unique` / `cf_target_ambiguous` | `Resolution` | CF target determined iff resolution beats `1/(2R²)` |
| `threshold_two_sided`, `linear_register_ambiguous` | `Resolution` | the critical window is `R(R−1) ≤ 2^t < R²`; the linear prediction `log r + O(log log r)` is refuted for every constant |
| `register_threshold_bits` | `Threshold` | `t_min = 2 log₂ R + O(1)`, in bits |
| `recovery_above_threshold`, `qubit_trade_trichotomy` | `Threshold` | end-to-end recovery above threshold; the three regimes in one statement |
| `outcomes_eq_alphabet`, `samples_do_not_help` | `SupportCollapse` | below `log₂ r` bits the records *coincide*: no sample budget helps |
| `card_outcomeFinset` | `Capacity` | one truncated sample carries exactly `min(2^t, r)` symbols |
| `no_support_only_estimator` | `Capacity` | divisor ambiguity `r` vs `r·s` survives at every register size |
| `samples_recover_iff` | `SampleFungibility` | samples repair `gcd(k,r)>1` **iff** the numerators are jointly coprime to `r` |
| `samples_recover_iff_generate` | `GroupBridge` | …iff the sampled residues generate `ZMod r` |
| `sample_count_lower_bound` | `SampleComplexity` | identification costs `m·t ≥ log₂\|S\|` bits in total |
| `shor_channel_irreducible` | `IrreducibleChannel` | width (`≥ r` frequencies) and depth (`≥ 2 log₂ r` bits) are both forced |
| `card_bad_records_le`, `good_record_of_log_log` | `RecordCount` | bad records are a fraction `≤ ω(r)/2^m`; `log₂ log₂ r + 1` samples always suffice |
| **`grid_threshold_two_sided`**, `grid_threshold_quadratic`, `truncOutcome_ambiguous` | `FareyCount` | the quadratic threshold **in the exact dyadic-grid model**: `R² ≤ 2^t` cells separate, `4·2^t < R²` cells collide — this closes last cycle's Conjecture 1 |
| **`sum_inv_sq_primes_lt_half`**, `two_pow_card_goodRecords`, `two_samples_recover_majority` | `SuccessDensity` | for every `r` and every `m ≥ 2`, **more than half** of all records succeed — this settles last cycle's Conjecture 3 with the explicit constant `1/2` |
| **`pow_mul_card_badRecords_lt`**, `card_goodRecords_lower` | `SuccessDensity` | concentration: the failure probability of `m` samples is `< 2^{-(m-1)}`, uniformly in `r` and with no `ω(r)` factor |
| **`sum_card_goodRecords`**, **`card_goodRecords_eq_moebius_sum`**, **`card_goodRecords_eq_euler_product`** | `JordanCount` | the **exact** success count `#goodRecords r m = ∑_{d ∣ r} μ(d)(r/d)^m = r^m ∏_{p ∣ r}(1 − p^{−m})` — Jordan's totient `J_m(r)`; this closes last cycle's Conjecture 3 in exact form |

**Exact success density.** The `> 1/2` bound of `SuccessDensity` is now an
identity: the success probability of an `m`-sample record at order `r` is exactly
`∏_{p ∣ r}(1 − p^{−m})` (`JordanCount`), proved by a gcd-rescaling bijection that
yields the divisor identity `∑_{d ∣ r} #good(d,m) = r^m`, followed by Möbius
inversion and an inclusion–exclusion over the subsets of `r.primeFactors`.

**The resource ledger, formally.** `2 log₂ r` qubits are forced (two-sided, in both
the tolerance and the grid measurement model), while **two** samples already
succeed with probability `> 1/2` for *every* order. The two resources are wildly
asymmetric: below the qubit threshold no sample budget compensates, and above it
a constant number of samples is enough — and each further sample halves the
failure probability, uniformly in the order.

---

## Conjecture 1 (the exact grid constant is `3/π²`)

The critical number of cells for the dyadic-grid register at order bound `R` is
`c·R²(1 + o(1))` with `c = 3/π²`: for every `ε > 0` and all large `R`, a register
with `2^t ≥ (3/π² + ε)R²` cells separates all reduced fractions of denominator
`≤ R` lying in `(0,1)`, and one with `2^t ≤ (3/π² − ε)R²` does not.

Status: `grid_threshold_two_sided` brackets the constant between `1/4` and `1`
(`R²/4 ≤ 2^t_crit ≤ R²`), using the elementary count
`four_mul_card_coprimePairs : R² ≤ 4·#{coprime pairs ≤ R}`.

**The key insight is** that the number of Farey fractions of order `R` in `(0,1)`
is `Σ_{q ≤ R} φ(q) = 3R²/π² + O(R log R)`, so the pigeonhole is *exactly* tight:
below `3R²/π²` cells two Farey fractions must collide, and above it an
equidistribution argument shows they need not.

**Why now?** The `1/4` in `four_mul_card_coprimePairs` is the only lossy step in
the whole chain, and it is a pure counting statement — Mathlib already has
`Nat.totient` and the Möbius machinery needed for `Σ_{q ≤ R} φ(q) ~ 3R²/π²`.

---

## Conjecture 2 (no joint post-processing beats per-sample resolution)

Fix `δ > 0`. For all sufficiently large `r`, no estimator — including one doing
*joint* lattice post-processing of `m ≤ (log r)^{O(1)}` samples read to
`t ≤ (2 − δ) log₂ r` bits each — outputs `r` with probability `≥ 2/3`.

**The key insight is** that each truncated sample only constrains `k_i/r` to an
interval of width `2^{-t}`, and the number of orders `r' ≤ R` admitting a
simultaneous solution `(k'_i)` of all `m` interval constraints stays `> 1` while
`2^{tm} ≪ R^{m+1}`; the counting bound `sample_count_lower_bound` is the crude
`m·t ≥ log₂|S|` shadow of this.

**Why now?** The experiment saw exactly this (10 samples did not move `t_min`),
and the statement is now expressible: the record model, the alphabet and the
estimator interface are all defined in `SupportCollapse.lean`, and
`truncOutcome_ambiguous` supplies the single-sample collision that the joint
argument has to iterate.

---

## Conjecture 3 (the uniform floor of the success density is `1/ζ(m)`)

**Resolved part.** The exact density is now proved:
`card_goodRecords_eq_euler_product` gives
`#goodRecords r m = r^m ∏_{p ∣ r}(1 − p^{−m})` for every `r ≥ 1`, `m ≥ 0`, so the
success probability of an `m`-sample record is *exactly* `∏_{p ∣ r}(1 − p^{−m})`.

**Remaining conjecture.** For every `m ≥ 2`,
`inf_{r ≥ 1} ∏_{p ∣ r}(1 − p^{−m}) = 1/ζ(m)`, the infimum being approached (but
never attained) along the primorials `r = 2·3·5·⋯`; for `m = 2` the value is
`6/π² = 0.60793…`, so two samples succeed with probability `> 6/π²` at every
order, and this constant is optimal.

**The key insight is** that `∏_{p ∣ r}(1 − p^{−m})` is a finite sub-product of the
absolutely convergent Euler product `∏_p (1 − p^{−m}) = 1/ζ(m)`, so the infimum
over `r` is the full product; the primorials are exactly the `r` whose prime
support exhausts an initial segment of the primes.

**Why now?** The finite identity is closed and formal, and Mathlib has
`riemannZeta`, the Euler product `EulerProduct.eulerProduct_completely_multiplicative`
and `ζ(2) = π²/6`, so what remains is the passage from finite sub-products to the
limit — no new arithmetic input is needed.

---

## Conjecture 4 (order-scaled DEQUANT: the register cannot shrink even by `o(log N)`)

For random `b` modulo a random semiprime `N = pq` with `p, q` of equal size,
`ord_N(b) ≥ N^{1−o(1)}` with probability `1 − o(1)`; consequently
`t_min = 2 log₂ N − o(log N)`: Shor's register `ℓ = 2⌈log₂ N⌉` is optimal up to
`o(log N)` bits, not merely up to a constant factor.

**The key insight is** that `t_min` is governed by the *order*, not the modulus
(`register_threshold_bits` is stated in `R`), so shrinking the register is
equivalent to a statement about small orders, which are rare.

**Why now?** `threshold_realized_at_mersenne` already shows the threshold is
realised by honest instances at every scale; upgrading "some instance" to "almost
every instance" is the last step to a fully unconditional register lower bound.

---

## Conjecture 5 (HSP generalisation: generation criterion + quadratic threshold)

Let `G` be a finite abelian group and `H ≤ G` hidden. Sampling characters of
`G/H` read to `t` bits recovers `H` iff (i) `t ≥ 2 log₂ |G| + O(1)` and (ii) the
sampled characters generate the annihilator `H^⊥`; moreover `O(1)` samples
suffice with probability `> 1/2`, uniformly in `G`.

**The key insight is** that `samples_recover_iff_generate` is already the cyclic
case of (ii) — the criterion is not arithmetic but group-theoretic — the Farey
separation behind (i) is the `ZMod`-dual of a lattice-covolume bound valid for
any `G`, and `two_pow_card_goodRecords` is the cyclic case of the density claim.

**Why now?** The cyclic case is closed and formal, and Mathlib has the character
theory of finite abelian groups (`AddChar`, Pontryagin duality), so the
generalisation is a matter of replacing `ZMod r` by `G` in three proofs that are
already written.

# Future Directions — next-cycle conjectures from the residue-leakage thread

The closed results of this cycle (all proved in `Catalog/Bridges/`):

* `dirichlet_no_pruning` — every candidate prime survives the QR fingerprint;
* `qrFingerprint_pattern_surjective` / `qrFingerprint_range_eq` — the fingerprint
  of primes realises exactly the `2^K` sign vectors;
* `consistent_iff_product_constraint` / `residue_channel_full_coset` — the whole
  content of the channel is the single symmetric relation
  `(a|q) = (a|N₀)(a|p)`, and the `K` bits of `F(p)` remain free;
* `qrFingerprint_class_infinite`, `qrFingerprint_mul_sq` — the fingerprint is a
  square-class invariant, hence not a collision-free hash;
* `probe_divisor_forces_factor` — the sharp boundary: the only pruning the
  channel ever achieves is detecting a probe-sized prime factor;
* `abelian_channel_no_pruning` — the same phenomenon for *every* finite family
  of Dirichlet characters of fixed modulus (see C3 below);
* `compensating_class_works` / `effective_no_pruning_of_linnik`
  (`Catalog/Bridges/ResidueLeakageEffective.lean`) — the compensating primes are
  *exactly* a unit class `N₀·p (mod 4∏A)`, so any effective bound for the least
  prime in a coprime class is inherited verbatim by the compensator (see C1);
* `consistentPairs_eq`, `consistentPairs_simply_transitive`,
  `consistentPairs_fst_eq`, `consistentPairs_ncard`
  (`Catalog/Bridges/ResidueLeakageTorsorTriviality.lean`) — the factorisation
  fibre is a coset of the anti-diagonal on which `Δ⁻` acts simply transitively,
  it surjects onto all of `{±1}^K`, and it has exactly `2^K` elements (see C5);
* `nonabelian_no_pruning`, `torsor_iff_abelian`,
  `compensator_multiplicity_jump`, `elementFibre_ncard`, `perm3_not_torsor`
  (`Catalog/Bridges/ResidueChannelNonabelianTorsor.lean`) — the non-abelian
  (Artin-symbol) channel: no candidate class is ever excluded in *any* group,
  while uniqueness of the compensating class holds **iff** the group is
  abelian; at the level of elements the fibre is a torsor of size `|C_p|` in
  every group (see C5');
* `no_sound_residue_filter`, `sound_filter_accepts_all`,
  `no_strictly_pruning_filter`
  (`Catalog/Bridges/ResidueLeakageNoSoundFilter.lean`) — sieve-independence:
  *any* sound candidate filter computed from the fingerprint accepts every
  admissible candidate, so a filter that prunes anything must discard a true
  factorisation (see C6).

Below: six threads, each with the part closed here and a bold, falsifiable
open successor. Each is stated so that a Lean
formalisation (or a decisive counterexample) is possible.

---

## C1. Effective no-pruning — arithmetic half **closed**, analytic half open

**Closed (this cycle).** `compensating_class_works` proves that *every* prime
`q ≡ N₀·p (mod 4∏A)` compensates, and `compensating_class_coprime` proves that
`N₀·p` is a unit modulo the conductor.  Hence the whole non-analytic content of
no-pruning is a congruence statement, and `effective_no_pruning_of_linnik`
shows that a bound `B` on the least prime in a coprime class modulo `4∏A`
yields a compensator `q ≤ B`.  `no_pruning_of_dirichlet_class` re-derives the
qualitative theorem from the same lemma, isolating the single analytic input.

**Remaining conjecture.** There is an absolute constant `c` such that for every list `A`
of the first `K` primes, every odd `N₀` coprime to `∏A` and every prime
`p ∤ 2∏A`, there is a prime `q < (4∏A)^c` with `F_A(p·q) = F_A(N₀)`.

*The key insight is* that the compensating class is a fixed unit class modulo
the conductor `4∏A` — now a theorem, not a heuristic — so what remains is
exactly Linnik's theorem for a conductor of size `e^{(1+o(1))p_K}`; formalising
any effective Linnik bound instantly makes "no pruning" *constructive* rather
than merely existential, by `effective_no_pruning_of_linnik`.

*Why now?* Mathlib now has Dirichlet's theorem on primes in AP
(used here); Linnik-type effectivity is the natural next analytic target, and
this conjecture gives it an immediate, concrete cryptanalytic meaning:
a residue-based sieve can be defeated in polynomial time, not just in principle.

**Falsifiable by**: a family `(A, N₀, p)` whose least compensator exceeds any
fixed power of the conductor (measurable directly).

---

## C2. The leakage curve — counting half **closed**, density half open

**Closed.** `qrFingerprint_range_ncard`
(`Catalog/Bridges/ResidueLeakageCounting.lean`) proves `L(K) = K` exactly: the
fingerprint over `K` distinct probe primes takes exactly `2^K` values on the
primes outside the probe set.

**Remaining conjecture.** With `L(K) := log₂ |{F_A(N) : N ∈ S}| = K` now a
theorem for `S` the odd numbers coprime to `∏A`, the open half is that the
induced map
`S/(4∏A) → {±1}^K` is a group epimorphism whose kernel has index `2^K` and is
*uniform* on the semiprimes: for every fingerprint `v`, the density of
semiprimes `N ≤ x` with `F_A(N) = v` tends to `2^{-K}`.

*The key insight is* that a fingerprint constrains a semiprime only through a
character of `(ℤ/4∏A)ˣ`, and the two prime factors of a random semiprime
equidistribute independently in that group; the observed exact balance
(60 residues per class at `K = 5`) should therefore persist asymptotically.

*Why now?* The group-theoretic half (`qrFingerprint_range_eq`) is already proved
here; what remains is a Mertens/Landau-type density statement for semiprimes in
a fixed unit class — within reach of the Selberg–Delange machinery.

**Falsifiable by**: a fingerprint class with semiprime density bounded away from
`2^{-K}`.

---

## C3. Barrier universality — **closed in this cycle**, and its sharpened successor

**Closed.** `abelian_channel_no_pruning`
(`Catalog/Bridges/AbelianChannelNoPruning.lean`) proves the conjectured
universality in full: for *any* finite family of Dirichlet characters
`χ₁,…,χ_K` of a fixed modulus `M`, any coefficient ring, any target `N₀`
coprime to `M` and any candidate `p` coprime to `M` (primality of `p` is not
even needed), there are infinitely many primes `q` with
`χ_i(p q) = χ_i(N₀)` for all `i`.  The compensating class is `N₀ · p⁻¹ (mod M)`;
the quadratic fingerprint is the special case where `p⁻¹ ≡ p` up to squares.
The instance `jacobiSym_two_no_pruning` re-derives the supplementary symbol
case without any quadratic reciprocity.

**Successor conjecture (C3').** The barrier is exactly a conductor-growth
barrier: if a family of characters has modulus `M = M(N)` with
`log M = o(log N)`, then it still prunes nothing, while at `log M ≍ log N` it
determines `N` and hence (with unbounded computation) its factorisation.

*The key insight is* that the only input to the closed theorem is that the
channel factors through the **fixed** finite group `(ℤ/M)ˣ`; once `M` may grow
with `N`, the compensating class must be realised by a prime of controlled
size, so the question becomes an effective-Dirichlet (Linnik) question, exactly
as in C1.

*Why now?* With C3 proved, the conductor is the only remaining parameter, so
the barrier can be stated as a clean threshold statement instead of a heuristic.

**Falsifiable by**: a family of characters with `log M = o(log N)` that excludes
a positive proportion of candidate primes for infinitely many `N`.

---

## C4. Conductor growth is the only obstruction: a `p`-pinning threshold

**Conjecture.** Fingerprints *can* prune if and only if the conductor is allowed
to grow with `N`: there is a threshold function `T(N) = N^{1/2+o(1)}` such that
probing with the primes below `T(N)` determines the factorisation, while
probing with the primes below `N^{1/2-δ}` leaves every candidate consistent.

*The key insight is* that `F_A(N)` determines the **square class** of `N`
modulo `4∏A` — not `N mod 4∏A` itself, as an earlier draft of this conjecture
asserted; `qrFingerprint_mul_sq` and the explicit collision `qrLab_collision`
(`F(79) = F(1591)` while `79 ≢ 1591 (mod 9240)`) refute the stronger reading.
Once `4∏A > N` the fingerprint pins `N` to its square class, and trial
division below `T` finishes the job; the content of the conjecture is that
nothing happens strictly before that threshold — the leakage curve is flat and
then jumps.

*Why now?* Both endpoints are provable with the machinery of this cycle
(`qrFingerprint_of_modEq` gives the upper endpoint; `dirichlet_no_pruning`
gives flatness for fixed `K`); the open part is the intermediate regime
`∏A ≈ N^{1/2}`, where the compensating `q` must also satisfy a size constraint.

**Falsifiable by**: an algorithm using `F_A` with `∏A = N^{o(1)}` that provably
excludes a positive proportion of candidate primes.

---

## C5. The fingerprint fibre as a flat bundle — **closed in this cycle**, and its non-abelian successor

**Closed.** `Catalog/Bridges/ResidueLeakageTorsorTriviality.lean` proves the
conjecture in the precise form asked for.  With
`Φ(N₀) = {(F_A(p), F_A(q)) : p, q prime outside A, F_A(p·q) = F_A(N₀)}`:

* `consistentPairs_eq` — `Φ(N₀) = {(u, F_A(N₀)·u) : u ∈ {±1}^K}`, a coset of the
  anti-diagonal `Δ⁻ = {(w,w)}`;
* `consistentPairs_simply_transitive` — any two points of `Φ(N₀)` differ by a
  **unique** `w ∈ {±1}^K` acting diagonally, i.e. `Φ(N₀)` is a trivial
  `Δ⁻`-torsor with no monodromy;
* `consistentPairs_fst_eq` — the projection to the first factor is onto
  `{±1}^K` (no-pruning in torsor form) and `consistentPairs_ncard` gives
  `|Φ(N₀)| = 2^K` exactly.

**Successor conjecture (C5') — settled in this cycle, and it splits.**
C5' asked: replace the quadratic characters by Artin symbols of a *non-abelian*
Galois extension `L/ℚ` with group `G`, so that the factorisation fibre becomes
`{(C_p, C_q) ∈ Cl(G)² : σ_N ∈ C_p C_q}`; the conjecture was that this fibre is
a trivial torsor **iff** `G` is abelian, and that for non-abelian `G` a
positive proportion of candidate classes is excluded — the first residue-type
channel with nonzero pruning.  `Catalog/Bridges/ResidueChannelNonabelianTorsor.lean`
proves both halves, with opposite answers:

* **Pruning half: FALSE.** `nonabelian_no_pruning` — in *any* group, for any
  target `σ` and any candidate `p`, the element `q = p⁻¹σ` compensates.  Since
  `classCompatible_conj_left/right` show the relation depends only on the two
  conjugacy classes, the fibre always projects **onto** all of `Cl(G)`: a
  non-abelian Artin channel prunes exactly nothing either.  The group-theoretic
  no-pruning barrier is therefore not an artefact of commutativity.
* **Torsor half: TRUE, as an exact characterisation.** `torsor_iff_abelian` —
  the compensating class is unique for every target and candidate **iff** the
  group is abelian.  `nonabelian_two_nonconj_compensators` produces explicit
  non-conjugate compensators from any non-commuting pair, `perm3_not_torsor`
  instantiates this in `S₃`, and `compensator_multiplicity_jump` shows the
  compensator count actually *jumps* between candidate classes.
* **Where the dichotomy comes from.** `elementFibre_ncard` — at the level of
  group *elements* the fibre is a torsor of size exactly `|C_p|` in every
  group; the abelian/non-abelian split is created purely by passing to
  conjugacy classes.

**Remaining conjecture (C5'').** Since no candidate class is excluded, the only
possible non-abelian gain is *statistical*: for a non-abelian `G`, let
`w_G(C_p | σ) = |{(x,y) : x ∈ C_p, y ∈ C_q, xy = σ}| / |G|` be the induced
weight on candidate classes.  Conjecture: `w_G(· | σ)` is non-uniform for every
non-abelian `G` and some `σ` (it is exactly uniform for abelian `G`), and the
resulting advantage in a divisor search is `O(1)` — bounded by
`max_C w_G(C|σ) / min_C w_G(C|σ) ≤ |G|^{O(1)}`, hence never superpolynomial.

*The key insight is* that the class-algebra structure constants
`a_{C_p C_q}^{σ}` are given by the character sum
`(|C_p||C_q|/|G|) Σ_χ χ(C_p)χ(C_q)χ(σ⁻¹)/χ(1)`, which is strictly positive for
all class triples in many non-abelian groups but *unequal* across `C_p`: the
channel reweights candidates without ever killing one, so its power is a
constant-factor speedup, exactly the verdict of the QRLEAK experiment.

*Why now?* The qualitative sides are now machine-checked here, so the only
remaining variable is the weight, which is a finite character-sum computation
per group — falsifiable on `S₃`, `A₄`, `S₄` by direct enumeration, and provable
in general from the Frobenius formula plus Chebotarev equidistribution.

**Falsifiable by**: a non-abelian `G` and a target `σ` whose candidate weights
are uniform (killing the statistical gain outright), or a family of groups in
which the weight ratio grows superpolynomially in `log |G|`.

---

## C6. Sieve-independence — **closed in this cycle** in filter form, and its successor

**Closed.** `Catalog/Bridges/ResidueLeakageNoSoundFilter.lean` proves the
sieve-independent form of the no-pruning barrier.  Model an arbitrary
residue-based candidate filter as a predicate `P v p` ("after observing the
fingerprint `v`, keep `p`"), and call it *sound* if it never discards a genuine
factor of an admissible semiprime.  Then:

* `no_sound_residue_filter` — every sound filter accepts **every** admissible
  candidate for every admissible observation;
* `sound_filter_accepts_all` — its accepted set is literally the full candidate
  set `{p : AdmissibleCandidate A p}`;
* `no_strictly_pruning_filter` — contrapositive: a filter that rejects even one
  admissible candidate is unsound, i.e. it destroys a true factorisation;
* `exists_admissible_compensator` — the compensating prime can always be chosen
  odd, distinct from the candidate and outside the probe set.

This upgrades the thread's results from "this particular sieve fails" to "no
sieve of this shape can exist", which is the precise sense in which the QRLEAK
verdict (REFUTED) is a barrier rather than an experimental observation.

**Remaining conjecture (C6').** Strengthen from *predicates* to *weights*: for
any sound randomised filter — a map `W : List ℤ → ℕ → [0,1]` assigning survival
probabilities, sound in the sense that the true factor survives with
probability at least `1 − ε` — the expected candidate-set size shrinks by at
most a factor `1/(1−ε)`.  Equivalently, the mutual information between
`F_A(N)` and the smaller prime factor of `N` is `O(1)` bits, independent of the
number `K` of probes.

*The key insight is* that the fibre description `consistentPairs_eq` makes the
conditional distribution of `F_A(p)` given the observation exactly uniform on
`{±1}^K`; a randomised filter can therefore only reweight within a fibre on
which the posterior is flat, so any soundness constraint immediately bounds the
achievable shrinkage.

*Why now?* The deterministic case is proved here, and the missing ingredient is
a single equidistribution statement (C2's density half) that turns the flat
posterior into an information-theoretic bound — after which the "constant-factor
tool" verdict becomes a theorem with an explicit constant.

**Falsifiable by**: a sound randomised residue filter whose expected surviving
candidate set is smaller than `(1−ε)` times the admissible set, for some
admissible observation.

## NET-17 — Attention-cost law at d=16 (speed-axis round 4): the k* = 4·d law is confirmed at the third depth

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab. Round-net-17. Real causal word LM (5 Gutenberg novels, dm=64, 4 heads, vocab 4097, ctx 128, causal, 2000 AdamW steps; d=16 s0, full acc **0.1610**, bar 0.98·full = **0.1578**, full loss **5.0830**). Same testbed family as NET-15/16. Script /tmp/exp_net_attncost_d16.py.

### Part A — concentration law: diffuse at every depth, but mildly depth-DRIFTING (NET-16's "depth-independent" overstated)

- Effective support exp(H): **53.28/128** mean (uniform-causal ≈64.5); per-head 44.7–58.1; intra-model gradient early 45–52 (l0–3) vs late 52–58 (l4–15).
- Across depth: 46.6 → 50.1 → **53.3** (+14% relative). Top-k mass falls monotonically: top-4 0.311→0.285→0.257, top-8 0.450→0.419→0.388, top-16 0.617→0.586→0.556, top-32 0.795→0.772→0.750.
- Attention remains DIFFUSE at every depth (53.3 ≪ 64.5 uniform-causal — only ~17% more concentrated), so the headline DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE survives.

### Part B — k* = 64 = 4·16 CONFIRMED (data-free top-k, joint evals, renormalized)

| k | retained | loss | Δloss | FLOP ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.808 ✗ | 5.4640 | +0.381 | 32× |
| 8 | 0.877 ✗ | 5.3007 | +0.218 | 16× |
| 16 | 0.929 ✗ | 5.1849 | +0.102 | 8× |
| 32 | 0.972 ✗ | 5.1177 | +0.035 | 4× |
| **64** | **0.995 ✓** | 5.0886 | **+0.006** | **2×** |
| 96 | 1.000 ✓ | 5.0836 | +0.001 | 1.3× |

The three-depth ladder k*=16/32/64 is exact — **k* = 4·d CONFIRMED across {4,8,16}**.

**Mechanism — per-layer compounding retained(k,d) ≈ r(k)^d:** d=8 per-layer retentions predict the d=16 totals within 0.006 (k=16 pred 0.924 vs 0.929; k=32 0.966 vs 0.972; k=64 0.994 vs 0.995). The knee is where r(k)^d crosses 0.98.

### Part B2 — random-k selection gap WIDENS with depth

- random-16 0.812 (top-k +**11.7 pts**), random-32 0.874 (+**9.8 pts**).
- Monotone: +6.2/+4.8 (d=4) → +9.5/+7.1 (d=8) → +11.7/+9.8 (d=16) — the compounding signature.

### Cost law — speedup ≈ ctx/(4d)

- At fixed ctx=128 the lever decays **8×→4×→2×** with depth.
- k* grows LINEARLY in depth, NOT in context — at real-LM context the lever grows: projected **64×** at ctx=4096, d=16. k*'s ctx-independence is UNTESTED — the natural next speed check.

### Barriers (a–h)

(a) top-k from each eval input's own causal attention at inference, joint evals, k=96 recovers full loss exactly (5.0836 vs 5.0830) — nothing injected. (b) top-k sparse attention is known; the k* = 4·d three-depth law + r(k)^d mechanism + depth-widening gap + eff-support drift are new; Catalog scan (698 pkgs) has no attention-cost law on a real small causal LM. (c) real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab. (d) data-free, contiguous no-overlap split, held-out. (e) 1 seed/depth, monotone sweep with clean knee at each depth, compounding model predicts d=16 from d=8 within 0.006. (f) 0.98 bar + raw loss, 6-pt sweep + 2-pt random control (seed 12345), k=96 exact numerics, eval noise ≈0.15% ≪ k*=64 margin. (g) full-attention reference + random-k at same k (+11.7/+9.8 pts, wider than d=4/d=8), same bar. (h) real lever, reframed as ctx/(4d) — decays with depth at fixed ctx (2× at d=16) but grows with context (projected 64× at ctx=4096); k*'s ctx-independence untested.

### Verdict

**LAW: LOSSLESS-K-SCALES-WITH-DEPTH — k* = 4·d CONFIRMED across {4,8,16}** with per-layer compounding r(k)^d and a depth-widening selection gap; concentration law corrected to mildly depth-drifting (still diffuse at every depth). DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE survives at depth, quantified as a linear-in-depth lossless-k law. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/17_AttentionCostDepthScalingSmallLM.md. Assessment v18, 18 experiments.
directions.title: NET-17: k* = 4·d CONFIRMED across {4,8,16} — lossless top-k key/value pruning at d=16 needs k*=64, per-layer compounding r(k)^d, speedup ≈ ctx/(4d)

## Round-net-18 (compression axis, depth-robustness check)

**Hypothesis.** NET-12's per-channel practical optimum (per-row uniform-4, lossless 0.987 @ 4.00 bits at d=4) — does it survive d=8 on the same real causal LM?

**Setup.** Same 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads, d=8 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc 0.1619 (bar 0.1587), loss 5.0788. 52 matrices, per-row symmetric RTN, every eval JOINT (fresh loaded copy, full held-out 60k forward).

**Results (d=8; d=4 NET-12 refs in parens).**

| config | primitive | d=8 retained | d=4 retained | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform-4 | per-row | **0.967** | **0.987 ✓** | −2.0 pts |
| uniform-3 | per-row | 0.873 | 0.947 | −7.4 pts |
| role(4/3/2) | per-row | 0.801 | 0.892 | −9.1 pts |
| uniform-3 | per-tensor | 0.705 | 0.825 | −12.0 pts |

**LAW: DEPTH-DEEPENS-QUANT-FLOOR.** The 4-bit per-channel interface floor is a d=4 property: uniform-4 falls below the 0.98 lossless bar at d=8 (0.967). The depth penalty lands at every bit level, worst where the schedule sits near the robustness cliff (uniform-3, role, per-tensor uniform-3 — agrees with NET-11's d=8 0.73 within eval noise). Both axes' lossless operating points shrink with depth at fixed width — the compression mirror of NET-16's k*≈4d. **Quote the depth with any 4-bit lossless claim.**

**Barriers (a–h):** joint evals / data-free RTN (a); per-channel quant known, depth-dependence of the floor new — Catalog 698 pkgs no depth sweep on a real causal LM (b); real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, d=8 (c); no leakage (d); 1 model/depth, exact family reproduction, eval noise ≈0.15% (e); 0.98 bar + raw loss, cross-check vs NET-11 (f); uniform-2/3/4 + role joint baselines, d=4 refs same family (g); real consequence: depth must be quoted (h).

Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/18_CompressionFloorDepthScalingSmallLM.md
Script: /tmp/exp_net_d8quant.py
directions.title: NET-18: The 4-bit compression floor is NOT depth-robust — per-channel uniform-4 loses losslessness at d=8 (DEPTH-DEEPENS-QUANT-FLOOR)

## NET-16 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-16, speed axis — depth-scaling check of the NET-15 DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE law)

**Hypothesis.** NET-15 (d=4) established: trained causal attention is diffuse (eff support 46.6/128) yet data-free top-k key/value pruning is lossless at k*=16 (0.984 ≥ 0.98 bar, 8× attention-core FLOPs). Its stated caveat was scale. This round tests DEPTH: does lossless-k / the concentration law shift at d=8 on the same real causal LM?

**Setup (identical NET-15).** 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 word vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads, **d=8 s0**, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc **0.1619** (d=4 0.1571 — deeper trains slightly better), bar 0.98·full=**0.1587**, full loss **5.0788** (d=4 5.1188). Same explicit causal-attention eval (k=96 recovers full loss exactly, 5.0789). Top-k mask from each eval input own causal attention at inference — data-free.

**Results.**

1. **Part A — the concentration law is DEPTH-INDEPENDENT.** Effective support per head 43.3–56.3, **mean 50.1/128** (d=4 46.6) — if anything slightly MORE diffuse with depth. Top-k mass lower at every level (top-16 0.586 vs 0.617). The diffuse regime is a stable property of this model scale.
2. **Part B — lossless-k GROWS with depth: k* ≈ 4·d.** k=4 0.873 ✗ (d=4 0.940), k=8 0.919 ✗ (0.971), **k=16 0.961 ✗ (d=4 0.984 ✓)** — the 8× lever FAILS at d=8, Δloss +0.047; **k=32 0.983 ✓** (d=4 0.998), Δloss +0.015; k=64 0.997 ✓; k=96 0.999 ✓. Every retained fraction lower and Δloss roughly doubled at each k — per-layer top-k error compounding through the residual stream, the speed-axis mirror of NET-11 compression compounding (deeper = worse).
3. **Part B2 — selection importance GROWS with depth.** Random-k gap: k=16 top-k 0.961 vs random 0.866 = **+9.5 pts** (d=4 +6.2); k=32 0.983 vs 0.912 = **+7.1 pts** (d=4 +4.8). The deeper model relies more on the trained selection information.

**Verdict.** **LAWS: CONCENTRATION-LAW-DEPTH-INDEPENDENT** (eff support ≈47–50 both depths) + **LOSSLESS-K-SCALES-WITH-DEPTH (k* ≈ 4d at fixed ctx)** + **SELECTION-IMPORTANCE-GROWS-WITH-DEPTH**. DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE survives with a documented depth boundary: the 8× attention-core lever at d=4 is a **4×** lever at d=8, and the d=16 prediction (k*=64, 2×) is under test (round-net-17, running). The attention-cost lever is real but a shallow-depth property at fixed ctx — scale-up claims must quote depth.

**8-barrier check:** (a) top-k from eval-input causal attention at inference, joint evals, k=96 exact-loss match (5.0789 vs 5.0788) — nothing injected; (b) top-k sparse attention known, but the k*≈4d depth-scaling + flat concentration law is new; catalog 698 pkgs no depth-scaling attention-cost law on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, 0.98 bar on real next-token; (d) top-k data-free (eval-input attention), contiguous split, held-out eval; (e) 1 model/depth, reproduced exactly 6×, monotone sweep with a knee that MOVED (16→32) in the direction consistent with NET-11 both-depth compounding; (f) 0.98 bar + raw loss, 6-pt sweep + 2-pt random control (fixed seed), k=96 exact numerics, retained vs each model own full (full-loss change 5.1188→5.0788 reported); (g) full ref at each depth + random-k control (+9.5 pts), same bar; (h) real lever (4× at d=8) but depth-scaling is the honest caveat for scale-up claims.

**Assessment:** v16, 16 experiments (NET-1..NET-16). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/16_AttentionCostDepthScalingSmallLM.md`. Script: /tmp/exp_net_attncost_d8.py.

**Next (fan-out running):** round-net-17 (d=16: is k*≈4d confirmed, predicts k*=64/2×?), round-net-18 (d=8 compression floor: does per-channel uniform-4 stay lossless at depth?), round-net-19 (carry chain at scale). Speed axis now 3 real-scale iterations (NET-10 negative, NET-15 positive, NET-16 boundary).
directions.title: NET-16: The attention-cost law scales with depth — lossless-k k* ≈ 4d, concentration depth-independent
