## NET-20 — Context-scaling check of the attention-cost law (speed-axis round 5)

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab. Round-net-20. Real causal word LM (5 Gutenberg novels, dm=64, 4 heads, vocab 4097, causal, 2000 AdamW steps; **d=4, ctx=256** — 2× the NET-15 context; full acc **0.1612**, bar 0.1579, full loss **5.0877**). Script /tmp/exp_net_ctx256.py.

### The untested assumption (from NET-17 barrier h)

k* = 4·d (NET-16/17) at fixed ctx=128 carries the cost law speedup ≈ ctx/(4d), which projects **64× attention-core reduction at ctx=4096, d=16**. That projection assumes k* does NOT grow with context. This round tests it: same d=4 model, same corpus, same 2000 steps, context doubled to 256.

### Part A — concentration law is context-DEPENDENT (more diffuse at longer context)

- Effective support: **82.94/256** vs 46.6/128 (relative to uniform: 0.36 → **0.65** — LESS concentrated with more context).
- Top-k mass at fixed k falls below ctx=128: top-8 0.363 vs 0.450, top-16 0.503 vs 0.617, top-32 0.662 vs 0.795.
- **Per-position (new):** eff support grows with past available — early(0–31) **11.3**, mid(96–127) **72.3**, late(224–255) **155.4** — **no bounded working set**; attention spreads over most of whatever context is present.

### Part B — k* doubles when context doubles

| k | retained | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.947 ✗ | |
| 16 | 0.971 ✗ | was LOSSLESS at ctx=128 (0.984 ✓) |
| **32** | **0.989 ✓** | **the knee** |
| 64 | 0.996 ✓ | |
| 128 | 1.000 ✓ | |
| 192 | 0.999 ✓ | exact loss match |

**k* = 32 = exactly 2× the ctx=128 knee.** At d=4, k* ∝ ctx in the tested range (k* = ctx/8: 16@128, 32@256).

### Corrected cost law — the lever is context-CONSTANT

Unified across NET-16/17/20 (3 depths @ 128 + this point): **k* = d·ctx/32 ⇒ speedup = 32/d, independent of context.**

| | ctx=128 | ctx=256 |
|---|---|---|
| d=4 | k*=16, 8× | k*=32, 8× |
| d=8 | k*=32, 4× | — |
| d=16 | k*=64, 2× | — |

**NET-17's projected 64× @ ctx=4096 is REFUTED** — long context buys no additional relative saving, because the lossless window scales with it. The surviving claim is the depth-only lever: **8× at d=4 at any context (within ctx∈[128,256]), 4× d=8, 2× d=16**.

### Part B2 — selection still matters at 2× context

random-16 0.884 (top-k **+8.7 pts**), random-32 0.929 (**+6.0**) — same gap magnitude as ctx=128.

### Barriers (a–h)

(a) top-k from each eval input's own causal attention at inference, joint evals, k=192 recovers full loss exactly (5.0877 = 5.0877) — nothing injected. (b) top-k sparse attention known; the k* ∝ ctx proportionality + context-constant lever + concentration diffusion with context are new; Catalog scan (698 pkgs) has no context-scaling law of sparse-attention pruning on a real small causal LM. (c) real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, 2× context. (d) data-free, contiguous no-overlap split, held-out. (e) 1 seed; context ladder = 2 points (128/256) — the proportionality is exact at this resolution but not extrapolated; a ctx=512 or seed-1 point would strengthen; the qualitative claim is robust (k=16 clearly fails at 256 vs clearly passes at 128; k=32 clearly passes). (f) 0.98 bar + raw loss, 6-pt sweep + 2-pt random control (seed 12345), k=192 exact numerics, eval noise ≈0.15% ≪ k=32 margin. (g) full reference + random-k at same k (+8.7/+6.0 pts), same bar. (h) reframed negative: the 64× long-context hope is dead; the real lever is depth-only 32/d; claim boundary ctx∈[128,256].

### Verdict

**LAW: LOSSLESS-K-SCALES-WITH-CONTEXT** (k* ∝ ctx at fixed depth) ⇒ **the attention-FLOP lever is context-CONSTANT: speedup = 32/d** (a depth-only property), unifying depth and context dependence as **k* = d·ctx/32**. Concentration law corrected to context-DEPENDENT (more diffuse with context, no bounded working set). DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE survives with a context-constant lever. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/20_AttentionCostContextScalingSmallLM.md. Assessment v19, 19 experiments.
directions.title: NET-20: k* is NOT context-independent — the attention-FLOP lever is context-CONSTANT (8x at d=4), refuting the projected 64x long-context speedup

# Future Directions

Five falsifiable conjectures distilled from what survived, and what resisted, in this cycle.
Each is stated so that it can be written down as a Lean 4 theorem on top of the definitions
already in `Catalog/Physics/EntanglementMonotone/`.

Background actually established (all sorry-free): the variational trace norm
`‖X‖₁ = inf {tr P + tr Q : X = P − Q, P,Q ⪰ 0}` equals `∑ᵢ|λᵢ|`; both the primal infimum and
the dual supremum `sup {Re tr(XW) : −1 ⪯ W ⪯ 1}` are attained; `E_N = log‖Γρ‖₁` is monotone
under PPT operations (hence under LOCC), strongly monotone under PPT instruments, vanishes
exactly on PPT states, is additive under tensor products, is bounded by `½ log(d_A d_B)`, and
attains that bound only at the maximally entangled state.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Exact duality formula for the monotone)

`E_N(ρ) = log (max {Re tr(Γρ · W) : W Hermitian, −1 ⪯ W ⪯ 1})`, and the maximising `W` may
always be taken of the form `Γ(entanglement witness)`; consequently `E_N` extends to a
PPT-monotone functional on the whole real vector space of Hermitian operators, not just
states, that is *concave along the PPT boundary*.

**The key insight is** that strong duality — proved here in the form
`exists_contraction_traceNorm_eq` — turns the monotone from an infimum (hard to bound from
below) into a maximum over a *compact convex* set of certificates, so every lower bound on
entanglement becomes an explicit finite-dimensional witness, and witness geometry (a convex
geometry question) becomes directly available to the trace-norm theory (an operator-algebra
question).

**Why now?** The attainment statement, which is the analytic obstruction, is now formalised;
what remains is convex geometry of the contraction ball, for which Mathlib's convexity and
compactness libraries are already adequate.

## Conjecture 2 (Rigidity of the maximiser)

On `ℂ^d ⊗ ℂ^d`, `E_N(ρ) = log d` **only** for maximally entangled states: if `E_N(ρ) = log d`
then `ρ = (U ⊗ V) Φ_d (U ⊗ V)ᴴ` for local unitaries `U, V`.

**The key insight is** that the Cauchy–Schwarz step `∑|λᵢ| ≤ √N √(∑λᵢ²)` used in
`logNeg_le_log_dim` is an equality only when all `|λᵢ|` coincide, and the purity step
`tr ρ² ≤ 1` is an equality only for pure states; chaining the two equality cases forces the
partial transpose to have flat spectrum `±1/d`, which is a rigidity statement about the
swap operator.

**Why now?** The inequality chain is already formalised as a chain of named lemmas, so the
conjecture reduces to the equality analysis of two standard inequalities — no new analytic
input is required, only the equality conditions.

## Conjecture 3 (Asymptotic distillation and irreversibility)

For every state `ρ`, and every `n, m` with an *exact* PPT protocol `Λ` mapping `ρ^{⊗n}` to
`Φ_{2^m}`, one has `m log 2 ≤ n E_N(ρ)`; moreover there exist states (PPT-entangled ones) for
which the entanglement *cost* under PPT operations is strictly positive while this
distillation rate is `0`, so the PPT theory of entanglement is irreversible.

**The key insight is** that additivity plus monotonicity already give the single-shot rate
bound (formalised here for two copies as
`log_card_le_logNeg_of_exact_two_copy_distillation`), so irreversibility becomes a *separation*
statement between two quantities that both sandwich `E_N`, rather than a new asymptotic
analysis.

**Why now?** The `n = 2` case is proved; the general `n` case needs only a coherent
formalisation of iterated tensor regrouping (an `Equiv`-bookkeeping problem), which the
`regroup`/`tensorBipartite` machinery of this cycle already makes routine.

## Conjecture 4 (Continuity with an explicit modulus)

`|E_N(ρ) − E_N(σ)| ≤ log(1 + d‖ρ − σ‖₁)`, and this modulus is optimal up to a constant; in
particular `E_N` is continuous but *not* asymptotically continuous with a dimension-free
modulus.

**The key insight is** that `Γ` is an isometry for the Hilbert–Schmidt norm (proved here as
`trace_ptrans_sq`) but only a `d`-bounded map for the trace norm, and the logarithm converts
this multiplicative distortion into an additive modulus; the failure of dimension-free
continuity is therefore traceable to a single norm-equivalence constant.

**Why now?** Both norms and their comparison are already formalised in this development, and
the estimate `|log x − log y| ≤ |x − y| / min(x,y)` with `‖Γρ‖₁ ≥ 1` closes the gap with
Mathlib's existing logarithm lemmas.

## Conjecture 5 (Multipartite monogamy)

For a tripartite state on `ℂ^A ⊗ ℂ^B ⊗ ℂ^C`, the negativities across the three bipartite cuts
satisfy a monogamy inequality `N_{A|BC}² ≥ N_{A|B}² + N_{A|C}²`, with equality exactly for
generalised GHZ-type states.

**The key insight is** that the covariance identity `Γ((A⊗B)X(A⊗B)ᴴ) = (A⊗B̄)(ΓX)(A⊗B̄)ᴴ`
proved here for the bipartite cut applies verbatim to each cut of a multipartite system once
tensor factors are regrouped, so monogamy becomes a statement about how three different
partial transposes of the *same* matrix constrain each other — a genuinely combinatorial
constraint on a single spectrum.

**Why now?** The regrouping equivalences (`regroup`, `tensorBipartite`) and the spectral
identification of the trace norm make each cut computable from a common spectral object, so
the conjecture can be tested exhaustively on small dimensions with the exact rational
`#eval` methodology already used in `ComputationalEvidence.md` before any proof attempt.

---

### Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. **(N1)** `‖X ⊗ Y‖₁ = ‖X‖₁‖Y‖₁` extends from Hermitian to arbitrary complex matrices once
   the trace norm is defined through `√(XᴴX)`; the variational definition used here is the
   Hermitian shadow of that statement.
2. **(N2)** The set `{ρ : E_N(ρ) = 0}` is exactly the PPT cone intersected with the state
   space and is *strictly larger* than the separable set in every dimension `d_A d_B ≥ 6`
   (existence of bound entanglement).
3. **(N3)** Selective monotonicity (`logNeg_strong_mono`) is tight: for every `ε > 0` there is
   a PPT instrument whose average output negativity is within `ε` of the input's, so no
   strictly-decreasing refinement of the monotone exists on the whole state space.

# Future directions — the Walsh/GF(2) face of the factoring barrier

Derived from the Stage-3 analysis and Stage-4 critique of the results now proved in
`Catalog/Novelty/WalshSpectralFlatness.lean` and `Catalog/Novelty/SpectralFlatnessFactoring.lean`.
Each conjecture is falsifiable by a finite computation at small parameters and is stated so that a
Lean formalisation can begin immediately.

---

## C1. The ordering defect is exactly a top-bit statistic

**Conjecture.** Let `t ≥ 2`, `1 ≤ j < t`. Over the support of *ordered* odd pairs `p < q` mod `2^t`
the correlation of `p_j` with any statistic of the low block `N mod 2^t` is nonzero, but every such
correlation is bounded by `C · 2^{-t/2}`, and the entire defect is carried by the event
`p < q` — formally, the correlation equals `Cov(1[p<q], g(N)) · (something depending only on j)`
up to `O(2^{-t})`.

*The key insight is* that `lowblock_corr_zero` fails on the ordered support for exactly one reason:
the sign-reversing involution `p ↦ p XOR 2^j` used in `sum_bitSign_oddRes` does not preserve
`p < q`, so the defect must be a functional of the order statistic alone, i.e. a magnitude
statistic — the same family as the top-bit law.

*Why now?* The proof of the exact theorem isolates the involution as the single point of failure,
and the computations in `ComputationalEvidence.md` already show the defect shrinking as
`2/15, 2/31, 1/21` while the maximising parity migrates from `∅` to a *high* bit `{6}`.

---

## C2. A degree hierarchy over the prime-restricted support

**Conjecture.** For the exact `k`-bit prime semiprime support, for every fixed degree `d` there is
`k_0(d)` such that for all `k ≥ k_0(d)` and all `1 ≤ j ≤ k - 7`, every parity of degree `≤ d` of
the bits of `N` correlates with `p_j` by at most `C_d · π(2^k)^{-1/2} · polylog`, while for
`j > k - 7` the maximum degree-1 correlation stays bounded away from `0`.

*The key insight is* that the two proved theorems bracket the truth from both sides — exactly zero
below (`lowblock_corr_zero`, on the odd support) and strictly positive above (`covTop_pos`) — so the
only open content is the *transition window*, whose width the experiment measures as ~6 bits.

*Why now?* `highDegree_mass_ge` converts any such correlation bound into a statement about where
the Fourier mass lives, so a single quantitative equidistribution input (primes in short
arithmetic progressions mod `2^t`) would upgrade the empirical claim to a theorem.

---

## C3. Sharp constant for the top-bit covariance

**Conjecture.** `covTop e → (2 log 2 − 1)/4 ≈ 0.09657` as `e → ∞`.  Rescaling `p = 2^{k-1}x`,
`q = 2^{k-1}y` sends the balanced support to `S = {(x,y) ∈ [1,2]² : x ≤ y}` (area `1/2`), the event
`p_{k-2} = 1` to `A = S ∩ {x ≥ 3/2}` (area `1/8`, so `P(A) = 1/4`) and the carry-out event to
`B = S ∩ {xy ≥ 2}` (area `1 − log 2`, so `P(B) = 2(1 − log 2)`); since `A ⊆ B`, the limiting
covariance is `P(A)(1 − P(B)) = (2 log 2 − 1)/4`.

*The key insight is* that `hiSet ⊆ topSet` is a *scale-invariant* condition once `p = 2^{k-1}x`,
`q = 2^{k-1}y`, so the covariance is a Riemann sum for a fixed planar area functional and must
converge, with the observed decreasing sequence `0.222, 0.180, 0.138, 0.118, 0.107` as its
approximants.

*Why now?* `covTop_pos` already proves positivity for all `e` by a purely combinatorial argument;
the limit statement needs only a lattice-point-counting error term, well inside reach.

---

## C4. No low-degree GF(2) approximator, unconditionally, via the low block

**Conjecture.** For every `d` and every GF(2) polynomial `P` of degree `≤ d` in the bits of `N`,
the fraction of *odd* pairs `(p,q)` mod `2^t` on which `P(N) = p_j` is exactly `1/2` for all
`1 ≤ j < t` — and this remains true when `P` is allowed to read, in addition, any `o(t)` of the
high bits of the true integer product `pq` (not merely `pq mod 2^t`).

*The key insight is* that the proved theorem already handles *arbitrary* functions of the low
block, so the only extension needed is to let the predictor see a bounded amount of magnitude
information; the group-theoretic proof (`group_zero_block`) should survive as long as the extra
information is a function of a coset of a subgroup of bounded index.

*Why now?* `group_zero_block` isolates the mechanism as the regular representation, which makes the
"low block + bounded magnitude" hybrid a statement about a subgroup filtration rather than about
primes.

---

## C5. Spectral spreading is achieved by the factoring function

**Conjecture.** For the `k`-bit prime semiprime support, the number of parities with nonzero
Walsh coefficient for `f_j` is at least `2^{Ω(k)}` for every information-bearing `j` — i.e. the
lower bound in `card_support_ge_of_flat` is essentially attained, so the factoring bit is not just
flat but *maximally spread*, behaving like a random function of its input.

*The key insight is* that flatness alone (`|corr| ≤ ε` everywhere) forces support size `≥ ε^{-2}`,
and the measured `ε ≈ 10^{-2}` at `k = 14` already forces `≥ 10^4` nonzero coefficients; pushing
`ε` down to the noise floor `2^{-n/2}` would force exponentially many.

*Why now?* Both halves of the needed inequality are now formal: `exists_corr_sq_ge` gives the floor
and `card_support_ge_of_flat` converts a flatness bound into a support lower bound. Only the
support-restricted analogue of Parseval remains.

# Future Directions — Boolean-Valued Multiverse Semantics (cycle 2 output)

The results of this cycle are in

* `Catalog/Logic/Multiverse/BooleanValuedRealization.lean` — Boolean-valued
  universe, generic quotients, truth lemma, forcing closure, derived directedness,
  derived button law, derived opposite CH branches, ground/extension bimodality;
* `Catalog/Logic/Multiverse/InvariantFragment.lean` — exact frame calibration
  (`.2` ⇔ directedness, `5` ⇔ no buttons, `.3` fails with two buttons), the
  multiverse-invariant fragment theorem, and the exact Boolean criterion for a
  background to survive into both branches;
* `Catalog/Logic/Multiverse/S42Independence.lean` — a Hilbert calculus for `S4.2`,
  its soundness on all directed preorders, and the resulting non-derivability of
  `5` and of `.3`;
* `Catalog/Logic/Multiverse/FrameCounting.lean` — the exact size `3^n · 4^m` of the
  `n`-button, `m`-switch forcing frame;
* `Catalog/Logic/Multiverse/PMorphismTransfer.lean` — bounded morphisms, the truth
  and validity transfer theorems, the bounded morphisms from the control frame onto
  the pure button order and onto every finite chain, and the resulting strict
  containment of its logic in the logic of chains.

Everything below is a new, falsifiable conjecture generated by those results.

## 1. Finite-frame completeness of `S4.2` for button–switch products

**Conjecture.**  A modal formula is derivable in the calculus `S42Independence.S42`
**iff** it is valid on every frame `CWorld (Fin n) (Fin m)` with the accessibility
relation `cacc`.  Equivalently: the intersection of the logics of the finite
pre-Boolean control frames is exactly `S4.2`.

*Falsifiable by* a formula valid on all `CWorld (Fin n) (Fin m)` but not derivable
in `S42`, or by an `S42` theorem failing on some `CWorld (Fin n) (Fin m)` (the
latter is already excluded by `S42_sound` together with `cacc_refl`, `cacc_trans`,
`cacc_directed`).

The key insight is that this cycle proved the *soundness* half outright and
manufactured the two hardest refuting instances (`5` and `.3`) from buttons alone;
what remains is a filtration argument turning an arbitrary finite directed preorder
countermodel into a button–switch product, and the counting theorem
`card_cacc_pairs` shows exactly how much room such a product has
(`3^n · 4^m` pairs, growing fast enough to embed any finite directed preorder of
bounded size).

Why now?  The deductive calculus, its soundness theorem, a working supply of finite
countermodels and the bounded-morphism transfer machinery
(`msat_pmorphism`, `validity_transfer`) now all exist, so the only missing
ingredient is a bounded morphism from a button–switch product onto an arbitrary
finite rooted directed preorder; the two special cases already proved
(`forgetSwitches` onto the button order, `cardChain` onto every finite chain) show
the technique works.

## 2. A Boolean-valued Lindenbaum theorem: richness from directedness

**Conjecture.**  Every Boolean algebra arising as the algebra of Boolean values of
a *directed* forcing frame is `Rich` in the sense of
`BooleanValuedRealization.Rich` — i.e. richness need not be assumed but follows
from a frame-side amalgamation hypothesis, without any appeal to the Boolean prime
ideal theorem beyond what directedness already supplies.

*Falsifiable by* a directed frame whose value algebra has a nonzero element lying
in no generic filter.

The key insight is that the branching theorem `branch_of_undecided` is the only
place where richness is used, and in the concrete realization richness was obtained
*constructively* (principal filters, `rich_set`); this suggests the choice content
of the general statement is an artefact of the abstract formulation.

Why now?  Richness has been isolated as a single named hypothesis appearing in
exactly two theorems (`branch_of_undecided`, `background_branches_iff`), so it can
be attacked without touching the rest of the development.

## 3. The invariant fragment is closed under a modal operator

**Conjecture.**  The characterization `invariant_iff_buttonFree` extends to the
*modal* language: an assertion of the bimodal language (forcing `□` plus ground
`□̌`) is invariant along the button order iff it is equivalent to a formula in which
every atom is a switch atom **and** every modality is one of the two "stable"
combinations `□□̌` or `□̌□`.

*Falsifiable by* a bimodal formula in the proposed fragment whose truth value
changes along an allowed extension or ground move, or by an invariant formula
provably inequivalent to every member of the fragment.

The key insight is that the substitution proof of `invariant_iff_buttonFree`
(replacing button atoms by `⊥` via `subBtnFls`) is purely syntactic and should lift
to modalities once the modal depth is handled by an induction on the bimodal
zigzag, which the proved validity `tense_axiom_valid` already controls in one
direction.

Why now?  Bidirectional invariance has been formalized as a *pair* of button
conditions (`buttonFree_bidirectional`), and the ground modality with its
downward directedness and mantle is now available in the same frame.

## 4. Calibrating large-cardinal backgrounds by meet-nonzero invariants

**Conjecture.**  For any finite hierarchy of background assertions realized as
elements `b₁ ≥ b₂ ≥ … ≥ b_k` of the value algebra, the uniform preparation
principle "each `b_i` meets both `⟦CH⟧` and `⟦¬CH⟧`" is not only necessary and
sufficient for branch preservation at each level (this is proved:
`background_branches_iff`) but is *inherited upward*: if `b_k` meets both sides
then so does every `b_i`, so a preservation obstruction can only occur at the top
of the hierarchy.

*Falsifiable by* a chain in a Boolean algebra with `b_k ⊓ ⟦CH⟧ ≠ ⊥` while
`b_i ⊓ ⟦CH⟧ = ⊥` for some `i < k` — impossible for `≥`-chains, hence the real
content is the analogous statement for hierarchies ordered by *implication modulo a
background theory* rather than by `≤`.

The key insight of this cycle is that branch preservation is exactly a
*meet-nonzero* condition, so a large-cardinal hierarchy is preserved in both
branches precisely when its Boolean values avoid being swallowed by one side, and
the switch-dependent obstruction `background_obstruction` shows the criterion is
sharp.

Why now?  The preservation criterion has been proved in both directions, so it can
serve as the definition of "weakest preservation hypothesis" that Direction 4 asked
for.

## 5. Mixed validities are not generated by the two unimodal logics

**Conjecture.**  There exist two frames with the *same* forcing-modal logic and the
*same* ground-modal logic but different mixed validities; consequently the bimodal
logic of the multiverse is not the fusion of its two unimodal fragments.

*Falsifiable by* a derivation of every mixed validity of the control frame from its
two unimodal theories.

The key insight is that `bimodal_separation` already exhibits a mixed validity
(`p → □ ◇̌ p`) whose unimodal analogue (`p → □ ◇ p`) fails on the very same frame;
promoting this to a genuine non-fusion theorem requires two frames rather than one,
and the counting theorem suggests looking at button orders of the same cardinality
but different shapes (`3^n` nested pairs can be redistributed).

Why now?  Both modalities, their directedness properties and the mantle are
formalized on one frame with one satisfaction relation, so a second frame can be
added without changing any interface.

## Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. **Filtration lemma.**  Every finite rooted directed preorder is a bounded
   (p-)morphic image of some `CWorld (Fin n) (Fin m)`, extending the proved special
   cases `forgetSwitches` and `cardChain`.
2. **Constructive branching.**  `branch_of_undecided` holds for every Boolean
   algebra that is *atomic*, with principal filters as witnesses (no choice).
3. **Fusion failure.**  Two finite control frames with equal unimodal logics but
   different mixed validities, exhibited explicitly and verified by exhaustive
   enumeration in Lean.

# Future Directions — tropical reading of the round-4 closures

Derived from the analysis and adversarial review of the four Lean files in
`Catalog/Tropical/` (`TropicalTorsionCensus`, `TropicalCensusMulti`,
`TorsionProfileAmbiguity`, `FactorLocationBarriers`).

What the formalisation established, in one sentence: *for a squarefree modulus the
whole `KROOT` free-witness family (`d ↦ #{x : x^d = 1 mod N}`) is a tropical
polynomial whose data is the per-prime multiset of tropical roots, and that data is
invariant under shuffling roots between the prime factors — which is exactly why it
cannot locate a factor.* The conjectures below push on the three places where the
proofs were tight.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Tropical Sealing Conjecture). Every multiplicative "spectral" statistic of `(ℤ/Nℤ)ˣ` is root-shuffling invariant, hence cannot locate.

**Statement.** Let `F` be any function of `N` computable from the isomorphism class of
the abelian group `(ℤ/Nℤ)ˣ` alone. Then for squarefree `N = ∏ p`, `F(N)` is invariant
under any permutation of the local valuation multisets `{v_ℓ(p-1)}_{p | N}` that
preserves the multiset at each prime `ℓ`. Consequently there exist, for every
`B`, two `B`-bit semiprimes with equal `F` and coprime factorisations.

*The key insight is* that `TropicalTorsionCensus.gcd_profile_eq_of_valuations` already
proves the invariance for the torsion profile, and the torsion profile is a complete
isomorphism invariant of a finite abelian group; so the conjecture reduces to a purely
tropical statement about shuffling roots of one-variable min-plus polynomials, with the
open part being the *density* claim (existence of shuffled pairs at every bit size,
which needs a Linnik/Bombieri–Vinogradov type input on primes in progressions).

*Why now?* The invariance half is formalised and machine-checked; only the
prime-density half remains, and it is a statement about primes `p ≡ 1 + 2^a·u`, an area
where effective results exist.

---

## Conjecture 2 (Tropical Corner Barrier). No `poly(log N)`-time algorithm can evaluate the census exponent `k ↦ min(k, v₂(p-1)) + min(k, v₂(q-1))` at any `k ≥ 1` for adversarial semiprimes.

**Statement.** Evaluating `T(k)` for one `k ∈ [1, log N]` is as hard as factoring, in the
sense that an oracle returning `T(2)` for arbitrary semiprimes yields a probabilistic
polynomial-time factoring algorithm.

*The key insight is* that `T(2) = 2^{min(2,a)+min(2,b)}` distinguishes `a = 1` from
`a ≥ 2`, i.e. it reveals `p mod 4`-type information about the *unordered* pair, and
combining this with the classical square-root-of-1 factoring reduction (which our
`energyGroundSet_eq` four-point ground space makes explicit) should upgrade the oracle
into a factorisation, showing that the *sealing* result of
`census_cannot_locate` is tight rather than an artefact.

*Why now?* The exact formula `torsionCensus_eq` is now a theorem, so the reduction can
be attempted symbolically rather than experimentally.

---

## Conjecture 3 (Level-0 invisibility is the only obstruction). The census exponent function determines the multiset `{v₂(p-1) : p | N}` completely once the number of prime factors is known.

**Statement.** For squarefree `s, t` with `s.card = t.card`,
`(∀ k, censusExponentMulti s k = censusExponentMulti t k)` implies the multisets
`{v₂(p-1) : p ∈ s}` and `{v₂(p-1) : p ∈ t}` are equal, *including* the level-0 part.

*The key insight is* that `census_determines_root_multiplicities` already gives equality
at every level `≥ 1`; the level-0 multiplicity is then forced by the cardinality
constraint, so the conjecture should follow from a counting argument — but our current
proof does not carry `s.card = t.card`, and making it do so requires a
tropical-degree statement (`deg` of a min-plus polynomial = number of roots with
multiplicity, including roots at `0`).

*Why now?* It is a two-lemma addition on top of the existing multiplicity theorem and
would complete the classification of exactly what the free-witness family sees.

---

## Conjecture 4 (Tropical hypersurface form of the factorisation problem). The set of factorisations of `N` is the corner locus of the two-variable tropical polynomial `P(X,Y) = (X ⊙ Y) ⊕ N`, and locating a corner point requires `Ω(√N)` queries in the min-plus query model.

**Statement.** In the min-plus model where a query at `(x, y)` returns
`min(x + y, log N)` plus the indicator of equality, any deterministic algorithm needs
`Ω(√N)` queries to output a nontrivial corner point of `P`.

*The key insight is* the straddle theorem `divisor_pair_straddles_corner`: every divisor
pair meets the corner `√N` from both sides, so a query at `(x,y)` only reveals which
side of the tropical line the point lies on — one bit — while the number of candidate
corner points below the corner is `√N` and exactly one is nontrivial
(`nontrivial_witness_below_corner`).

*Why now?* Both ingredients are proved; what remains is to formalise the query model
and run an adversary argument, which is a finite combinatorial statement well suited to
Lean.

---

## Conjecture 5 (Zero-entanglement is generic for algebraic witness Hamiltonians). Any energy of the form `E(a,b) = g(ab)` with `g(N) = 0` has a ground space that is a union of `τ(N)` product states, hence entanglement entropy exactly `0` and no descent gradient.

**Statement.** Formalise "product state" and "zero entanglement" for the divisor-pair
ground space and prove that the ground space of every `ab`-mediated energy is a disjoint
union of `τ(N)` rank-one tensors, so no tensor-network ansatz with bond dimension `> 1`
can help.

*The key insight is* that `energyGroundSet_eq` shows the ground space is a finite set of
*points* (not a correlated subspace), and `energy_gap` shows the landscape is a delta:
the search cost is therefore the counting `4/N²`, independent of the representation.

*Why now?* The ground-space computation is done; the remaining step is a definition of
the Schmidt rank of a finitely supported state, which Mathlib's tensor-product API can
support directly.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — next-cycle conjectures from the round-3 closures

The five round-3 hypotheses (RS-MIND, MODPAR-CERT, BURAU-ORD, DENS-SUB,
CONG-DIV) are now closed with machine-checked Lean proofs in
`Catalog/Computation/Factoring/`.  What the formalization exposed, beyond the
paper's numerics, is that all five closures factor through **two** structural
facts: (i) a CRT splitting `ℤ/N ≅ 𝔽_p × 𝔽_q` that makes every invariant a pair
of prime-level invariants, and (ii) Dirichlet's theorem, which says residue data
cannot separate those pairs.  The conjectures below are the sharpest testable
statements that this pair of facts suggests.

---

## C1. The CRT-splitting dichotomy for evaluation codes

**Conjecture.** For every `k ≤ min(p,q)` and every `N = pq`, the *weight
enumerator* of the evaluation code `C_k(N)` — not merely its minimum distance —
is the Hadamard product of the two Reed–Solomon weight enumerators, and every
one of its "gaps" (weights not attained) determines `max(p,q)`.  Consequently a
`poly(log N)`-time algorithm for *any* single nonzero coefficient of the weight
enumerator yields a factoring algorithm.

*The key insight is* that `RSMind.card_zeroSet_le` is really a statement about
the product structure of the zero set (`RSMind.card_zeroSet_le_mul`): the whole
weight spectrum, not just its minimum, is a product of prime-level spectra, so
every spectral feature is a free witness.

*Why now?* The minimum-distance case is fully proved (`min_distance_general`,
exact for all `k ≤ p`); the general spectrum needs only a counting refinement of
the same CRT injection, with no new machinery.

## C2. Beyond congruences: polynomial-time-determined invariants

**Conjecture.** `FreeWitness.not_revealsFactor_of_congruenceDetermined`
generalises from "determined by `N mod m`" to "determined by the value of a
fixed polynomial-size arithmetic circuit on the digits of `N`": no such
invariant names a nontrivial factor of every large semiprime, unless factoring
is in P.

*The key insight is* that the Dirichlet argument only used one property of the
class `{N : N ≡ a mod m}` — that it contains two *coprime* semiprimes.  Any
invariant whose level sets contain two coprime semiprimes is blind in exactly
the same way, and level sets of small circuits are large.

*Why now?* The meta-theorem is already stated abstractly over an arbitrary
`I : ℕ → ℕ`; only the "level sets are rich" input has to be replaced, turning a
number-theoretic lemma into a combinatorial one.

*Round-4 progress.* The *list* version of C2 is now proved:
`CandidateLists.no_bounded_candidate_list` shows that a congruence-determined
function returning a whole set of candidate divisors, of size bounded by any
fixed `k`, still fails on some large semiprime — the witness being a family of
`k+1` pairwise-coprime semiprimes in one residue class
(`CandidateLists.exists_coprime_semiprime_family`).  What remains open in C2 is
replacing "congruence-determined" by "circuit-determined".

## C3. Braid words versus order-finding: an exact equivalence

**Conjecture.** For every braid word `w ∈ B₃` whose exponent sum is `e ≠ 0`, the
order of the reduced Burau image `r_a(w)` over `ℤ/N` equals
`c(w) · ord_N(a^{e/ gcd}) ` for a word-dependent constant `c(w) ≤ 6`; hence
*every* braid word (not just `σ₁σ₂`) is an order-finding instance, and no choice
of word escapes barrier 6/8.

*The key insight is* that `Burau.bm_cube` identifies the centre `Δ² = (σ₁σ₂)³`
with the scalar `a³`, so the order of any word is controlled modulo the centre —
the quotient `B₃/Z(B₃) ≅ PSL(2,ℤ)` is virtually free, and the scalar part is the
only place where `a` can hide.

*Why now?* `Burau.orderOf_bm` proves the case `w = σ₁σ₂` exactly
(`orderOf = lcm(3, ord a)`), and `Burau.lcm_dvd_card_burauSubgroup` shows the
group order inherits it; the general word case is the same computation done
along the Zassenhaus filtration.

## C4. A decision-tree lower bound with a matching upper bound

**Conjecture.** The MODPAR primitive has query complexity exactly
`Θ(m / log m)` for recovering `{p mod m, q mod m}`: the adversary bound of
`ModPar.transcript_eq_of_avoids` (a query set avoiding ≤ 6 marked classes is
uninformative) is tight up to the `log` factor achieved by a randomized
group-testing strategy over the residues.

*The key insight is* that the parity pattern is a *sparse* Boolean vector (3 ones
out of `m`, `ModPar.card_support`), and sparse recovery from parity queries is
exactly group testing — so the true complexity should be sub-linear, contradicting
the folklore `Ω(m)` reading of the closure.

*Why now?* The support and its size are both proved exactly, so the two sides of
the bound can be compared without any further structure theory.

## C5. Games whose equilibria are *not* the answer

**Conjecture.** Every finite game whose unique pure Nash equilibrium is a
nontrivial divisor of `N` and whose payoff function is evaluable in
`poly(log N)` time yields a `poly(log N)` factoring algorithm; equivalently, in
any such game the payoff oracle must itself decide divisibility
(`CongDiv.payoff_nonneg_iff_dvd`).  Hence no game-theoretic reformulation can be
a genuine algorithm.

*The key insight is* that `CongDiv.best_response_unique_general` shows the
equilibrium is `minFac N` for *every* composite `N`, and
`CongDiv.payoff_constant_off_divisors` shows the payoff landscape has no
gradient: the only information channel is the divisibility test itself.

*Why now?* Both halves are proved for the concrete congestion game; the
conjecture asks only to abstract "payoff evaluable in poly time" into the
hypothesis, which is a definitional step.

## C6. Quantitative candidate-list growth

**Conjecture.** The bound of `CandidateLists.no_bounded_candidate_list` is
quantitatively sharp in the following sense: for a modulus `m` and a threshold
`B = N`, any congruence-determined candidate list that succeeds on all
semiprimes below `N` must have size `Ω(π(√N) / m)`, i.e. essentially the trial
division list, and the residue class contributes only a constant-factor saving.

*The key insight is* that the coprime family constructed above can be taken
inside a single class of *any* modulus, so the class structure removes no
candidates at all beyond those excluded by congruence obstructions on the
factors themselves.

*Why now?* The qualitative statement is proved unconditionally; the quantitative
version needs only a counting version of the same Dirichlet input (prime
counting in progressions), which is available in effective form.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — after the round-7 closures

The five Lean files added in `Catalog/Tropical/` make the round-7 verdicts
precise: the AGREEMENT aggregate collapses to `φ(N)/2` and to the Jacobi level
set; the zero-divisor graph is exactly `K_{q-1,p-1}` and its degree sequence is
the trace witness; the rho sample set escapes the density floor but only through
pigeonhole correlation plus quadratic aggregation; and the digit-convolution
relaxation carries an `O(1)`-norm kernel vector, so no factorisation target is
isolated. Each closure suggests a sharper, falsifiable successor.

## Conjecture A (structural-witness dichotomy)

*For every prime `p ≠ q`, any graph invariant of the zero-divisor graph of
`ℤ/pqℤ` that is computable in time `polylog N` from `N` alone is a function of
`N` alone; equivalently, every invariant that separates two semiprimes of equal
size requires `Ω(min(p,q))` vertex queries.*

**The key insight is** that `Round7ZDG.vertex_gives_factor` shows a *single*
vertex already yields a factor, so an invariant is either blind (a function of
`N`) or its evaluation embeds trial division — there is no middle regime.
**Why now?** The graph is now a formal `SimpleGraph` with a proven bipartite
adjacency and degree sequence, so query-complexity statements about it can be
formalised directly on top of `Round7ZDGDegrees`.

## Conjecture B (atomic-uniform noise floor as a theorem, not a principle)

*Let `D` be any distribution on `[1, N)` whose density is computable from `N` in
`polylog N` time and is `ε`-close to uniform in total variation. Then a single
sample from `D` reveals a nontrivial factor with probability at most
`2/min(p,q) + ε`.*

**The key insight is** that `Round7ZDG.atomic_uniform_success_le` already proves
the uniform case with the exact constant `2/p`, and the perturbation term is
forced by the total-variation bound; the content is that `polylog`-computability
prevents any density from concentrating on the `p + q - 2` zero divisors.
**Why now?** The uniform bound is formalised and the vertex set is exactly
characterised, so only the TV-perturbation layer remains.

## Conjecture C (aggregation lower bound for correlated samplers)

*Any algorithm that factors `N = pq` using only pairwise gcds of iterates of a
degree-`d` polynomial map mod `N` must perform `Ω(√p)` gcd operations, and the
`p + 1` pigeonhole bound of `exists_collision_mod_p` is tight up to the birthday
square root.*

**The key insight is** that the collision structure proved in
`Round7RhoNoiseFloor` is purely a statement about the reduced walk on `ℤ/pℤ`;
the birthday bound should therefore be provable as a counting statement about
functional graphs, independently of any randomness assumption.
**Why now?** The correlation lemma (`rhoZ_iterate_modEq`) and the extraction
lemma (`gcd_extract_of_dvd_sub`) are both formal, so the remaining step is a
purely combinatorial estimate on the rho-shaped functional graph.

## Conjecture D (lattice non-isolation in all dimensions)

*For every base `b` and every digit length `n ≥ 2`, the kernel of the digit
functional `w ↦ Σ w_{ij} b^{i+j}` on `n × n` integer matrices contains
`(n-1)²`-many independent vectors of squared norm `2`, and consequently every
rank-one target has a non-rank-one companion solution at squared distance `≤ 8`.*

**The key insight is** that the `2 × 2` commutator `[[0,1],[-1,0]]` generalises to
all "anti-diagonal transpositions" `E_{i,j+1} - E_{i+1,j}`, whose count grows
quadratically while their norm stays constant — the target's norm grows, the
noise does not.
**Why now?** The `2 × 2` case is fully proved in `Round7DigitLattice`
(`exists_spurious_solution`); the general case is the same identity indexed by a
larger family, and it would turn the "target sits at the Gaussian heuristic"
measurement into a theorem for all dimensions.

## Conjecture E (tropical corner rigidity)

*In min-plus coordinates the divisor pairs of `N` are exactly the lattice points
of the tropical line `X ⊙ Y = log N`, and the number of such points within
distance `δ` of the corner is `O(N^{δ'})` for explicit `δ'` — i.e. the corner
neighbourhood is as sparse as the balanced noise floor predicts.*

**The key insight is** that `corner_straddle` and `trop_mul_log_le` already place
every divisor pair on opposite sides of the corner; the missing ingredient is a
counting bound for divisors in a short interval around `√N`.
**Why now?** With the tropical statements in place, the corner-counting question
becomes an interval-divisor problem that can be attacked with the existing
`Nat.divisors` API rather than with new tropical machinery.

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — after Round-6: the Noise-Floor Principle and the Trace-Lemma Frontier

Round 6 closed the scalar and matrix theory of the noise floor: the minimum
excess risk of *every* spectral filter equals `b · tr(A(A+b·1)⁻¹)`
(`isLeast_filterRisk`, `trace_resolvent_eq_effDim`, `isLeast_filterRisk_matrix`),
the minimiser is unique (`filterRisk_eq_noiseFloor_iff`), ridge attains it only
under an exact isotropy relation (`ridge_optimal_iff_self_similar`) and misses it
by at least `4/3` otherwise (`ridge_strict_gap_two_modes`), the floor is squeezed
by a head/tail count and by a log-determinant capacity
(`half_minSum_le_noiseFloor`, `noiseFloor_le_capacity`), maximised at the
isotropic spectrum (`isGreatest_noiseFloor_of_energy`), early stopping
dominates matched ridge one-sidedly (`gradFlow_le_four_mul_ridge`,
`ridge_can_be_arbitrarily_worse`), and — for a geometric spectrum — the
log-corrected `1/N` scaling law is now derived rather than assumed
(`geometric_scaling_law`).

The following conjectures are the natural next cycle.  Each is falsifiable, and
each is stated so that a single Lean theorem would settle it.

---

## Conjecture D1 (Loewner monotonicity of the noise floor)

For real positive semidefinite `A ≼ B` (Loewner order) and `b > 0`,

```
tr (A (A + b•1)⁻¹)  ≤  tr (B (B + b•1)⁻¹).
```

**The key insight is** that `x ↦ x/(x+b) = 1 - b/(x+b)` is operator monotone, so
the statement reduces to the antitonicity of the matrix inverse on the positive
cone, `A ≼ B ⟹ (B+b·1)⁻¹ ≼ (A+b·1)⁻¹`, followed by taking traces — turning an
analytic inequality into a congruence-transformation argument with
`PosSemidef.sqrt`.

**Why now?** Round 6 already provides the exact resolvent diagonalisation
(`resolvent_eq`) and the identification of the trace with `effDim`, so the only
missing ingredient is the operator-inverse antitonicity, which is a
self-contained matrix lemma; with D1 the entire Part I–VI theory upgrades from
"fixed spectrum" to "monotone in the data covariance", i.e. *more data in the
Loewner sense never lowers the effective dimension.*

**Falsifier:** a pair `A ≼ B` of `2×2` PSD matrices with
`tr(A(A+b)⁻¹) > tr(B(B+b)⁻¹)`.

---

## Conjecture D2 (Sharp early-stopping constant)

The constant `4` in `gradFlow_le_four_mul_ridge` can be replaced by

```
κ* = sup_{u ≥ 0}  [ e^{-2u} + (1-e^{-u})² ] / [ (1+u)^{-2} + u²(1+u)^{-2} ]  <  2,
```

and `κ*` is attained at a unique interior `u* ≈ 2.2`; moreover no constant below
`κ*` works for any signal-to-noise ratio.

**The key insight is** that the ratio of the two per-mode risks depends on the
spectrum only through `u = μτ`, so the whole comparison collapses to a
one-dimensional extremal problem in `u` — a genuine calculus-of-one-variable
statement hidden inside a statistical folklore claim.

**Why now?** The per-mode reduction (`mode_gradFlow_le_four_ridge`) is already
formal; only the sharp scalar optimisation over `u` remains, and the numerics of
§6 of `ComputationalEvidence.md` localise the maximiser to `1.68 ≤ κ* < 2`.

**Falsifier:** a mode `u` where the ratio exceeds `2`.

---

## Conjecture D3 (Power-law scaling law)

*(The exponential case is now closed: `geometric_scaling_law` proves
`b(m+1)/2 ≤ noiseFloor ≤ b(m+1) + b/(1-r)` at the natural cut
`r^{m+1} ≤ b ≤ r^m`, i.e. `noiseFloor ≍ b·log(1/b)/log(1/r)`.  What remains is
the power-law case, where the counting function is polynomial rather than
logarithmic.)*

For the power-law spectrum `aᵢ = (i+1)^{-β}` with `β > 1`, truncated at any
`n ≥ b^{-1/β}`, there are constants `0 < c_β ≤ C_β` with

```
c_β · b^{1 - 1/β}  ≤  noiseFloor(a, b)  ≤  C_β · b^{1 - 1/β}.
```

**The key insight is** that the head/tail sandwich of Part IV converts the
analytic scaling law into pure counting: `#{i : aᵢ ≥ b}` plus a tail energy, so
the exponent `1 - 1/β` is a statement about the *counting function of the
spectrum*, not about any optimisation.

**Why now?** `half_minSum_le_noiseFloor` and `minSum_head_tail` reduce the
problem to two elementary sums, both of which have closed forms (geometric) or
standard integral comparisons (power law); this would give the first fully
formal derivation of a neural-scaling-law exponent from a variational principle.

**Falsifier:** a `β` for which the two-sided bound fails for arbitrarily small
`b`.

---

## Conjecture D4 (Capacity is the exact price of adaptivity)

Let `A_S = {a : Σ aᵢ ≤ S}`.  Then the *regret of the best single ridge parameter*
against the Wiener optimum, in the worst case over `A_S`, is governed by the
capacity gap:

```
sup_{a ∈ A_S}  [ inf_λ filterRisk(a,b,ridge λ) - noiseFloor(a,b) ]
      ≍  b · ( logDet(a*, b) - effDim(a*, b) )   for the maximising a*.
```

**The key insight is** that both the ridge deficiency and the capacity gap
measure the same thing — the spread of the numbers `aᵢ/(aᵢ+b)` around their mean
— so an inequality between two symmetric concave functionals should be provable
by the same tangent-line technique used in `noiseFloor_le_flat`.

**Why now?** Round 6 supplies all three quantities in formal form (`filterRisk`
for ridge, `noiseFloor`, `logDet`) plus the tangent-line machinery
(`tangent_identity`); the conjecture is the first quantitative link between
information-theoretic capacity and the *suboptimality of a hyperparameter
family*, rather than of an estimator.

**Falsifier:** a spectrum with a large capacity gap but ridge-optimal risk (or
vice versa), e.g. found by optimising over `Fin 3` spectra numerically.

---

## Conjecture D5 (Noise floor of a random covariance: Marchenko–Pastur regime)

For `A = (1/N) XᵀX` with `X` an `N × n` matrix of i.i.d. standard Gaussians and
`n/N → γ ∈ (0,1)`,

```
(1/n) · tr (A (A + b•1)⁻¹)  →  1 - b · m_γ(-b),
```

where `m_γ` is the Stieltjes transform of the Marchenko–Pastur law; consequently
the noise floor per parameter converges to `b (1 - b m_γ(-b))`.

**The key insight is** that the trace lemma turns the noise floor into a linear
spectral statistic of the sample covariance, precisely the class of quantities
controlled by the Stieltjes transform — so a random-matrix limit theorem
transfers verbatim to a learning-theoretic constant.

**Why now?** The catalog already contains a Wigner semicircle development
(`Catalog/MachineLearning/WignerSemicircle/`), and Round 6 supplies the exact
identity `tr(A(A+b)⁻¹) = Σ μᵢ/(μᵢ+b)` needed to phrase the limit as convergence
of an empirical spectral integral; joining the two files is the shortest path to
a formally verified "double descent"-style curve.

**Falsifier:** a mismatch between the finite-`n` numerics of
`tr(A(A+b)⁻¹)/n` and `1 - b m_γ(-b)` beyond `O(n^{-1/2})`.

---

### Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures (recursive abduction)

1. **D1a (scalar shadow of D1):** if `a ≤ a'` pointwise *after sorting*, then
   `effDim a b ≤ effDim a' b` — already true for the unsorted case
   (`effDim_mono_spectrum`); the sorted version is what Weyl's inequalities
   deliver from `A ≼ B`.
2. **D2a:** `(1-e^{-u})(1+u) ≤ 3u/2` for all `u ≥ 0` (would immediately improve
   the early-stopping constant from `4` to `9/4`).
3. **D3a:** for antitone spectra the head set is an initial segment:
   `{i : b ≤ aᵢ} = Iio k` with `k = #head` — the missing combinatorial step in
   front of every scaling-law computation.

Abstract: Two graphs $G$ and $H$ are homomorphism indistinguishable over a graph class $\mathcal{F}$ if they admit the same number of homomorphisms from every graph in $\mathcal{F}$. A wide range of relaxations of graph isomorphism arise this way: isomorphism itself over the class of all graphs [Lovász, Acta Math. Hung. 1967], equivalence under the $k$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm over the graphs of treewidth $\leq k$ [Dvořák, J. Since the class $\mathcal{F}$ is typically infinite, it is not clear a priori whether homomorphism indistinguishability over $\mathcal{F}$ is decidable; for planar graphs it is undecidable. Every class for which decidability was previously known is sparse. # FUTURE DIRECTIONS — after Experiment 391 (Berggren–Price interlock)

The Pythagorean-tree line for factoring is now closed with exact statements
(`Catalog/Algebra/BerggrenPriceInterlock/`, five files, all `sorry`-free):
both trees enumerate the same vertex set exactly once, every odd coprime factorisation
`N = pq` is the node `((p+q)/2,(q−p)/2)` with odd leg exactly `N`, the two descents are
inequivalent (determinants `±1` vs `±2`, leg-swap symmetric vs not, exactly two shared
edges), and the traversal cost is inversely coupled to Fermat's cost
(`m ≤ 2·s·(2d+3)²`). The following conjectures are the natural next cycle.

## C1. Exact Berggren depth = odd-continued-fraction length

**Conjecture.** For every node `(m,n)` the Berggren depth equals
`d_B(m,n) = Σ_i a_i − (number of "reflect" steps)`, where `a_i` are the partial
quotients of the *subtractive* expansion of `m/n` generated by the three parent rules
(`m < 2n`: reflect; `2n < m < 3n`: reflect-and-shift; `m > 3n`: subtract `2n`).
In particular `d_B(m,1) = (m−2)/2` exactly, and `d_B` is a function of the ratio `m/n`
alone in the sense that `d_B(m,n) = d_B(m',n')` whenever `m/n = m'/n'` (which for
coprime pairs is a tautology, so the content is the closed formula, not the invariance).

*The key insight is* that `berg_ratio_bound` (`m ≤ (2d+3)n`) is the crude shadow of an
exact identity: the Berggren descent **is** the slow (subtractive) Euclidean algorithm on
`(m,n)`, so its depth must be the sum of partial quotients, not their number.
*Why now?* The parent rule is already formalised (`berg_parent`) and the ratio bound is
proved; only the accounting of the three branch types against the continued-fraction
digits remains, and it is a finite induction over the same three cases.

## C2. Price depth is `Θ(log m)` — a matching upper bound

**Conjecture.** Every node satisfies `d_P(m,n) ≤ 2·log₂(m) + O(1)`; combined with the
proved lower bound `m ≤ 2^(d+1)` this makes Price depth `Θ(log m)`, and hence
`d_P = Θ(log N)` at the `N`-node, matching the observed `≈ 1.4·log₂(p+q)`.

*The key insight is* that the Price parent halves `m` when `m` is even and halves `n`
when `m` is odd, and the parity of `m` cannot stay odd twice in a row along a descent
once one tracks `(m mod 2, n mod 4)`: a two-step potential `Φ = log₂(m·n)` decreases by
at least `1` per two steps. *Why now?* `price_parent` is formalised with all four cases
explicit, so the potential argument is a direct induction; this would upgrade
`price_level_gt_fermat` from "level width beats Fermat" to a *complete* cost model of the
Price tree.

## C3. No polynomial-size branch predicate for the `N`-node

**Conjecture (barrier).** There is no predicate `P(N, w)` computable in time
`poly(log N, |w|)` such that, for every odd semiprime `N`, `P(N, w)` holds exactly for
the prefixes `w` of the Berggren (or Price) address of the `N`-node. Equivalently, the
address string is incompressible relative to `N`.

*The key insight is* that a prefix predicate would let one binary-search the address and
so factor in polynomial time, while the trade-off theorem
`m ≤ 2·s·(2d+3)²` shows the address *length itself* already encodes the size of Fermat's
scan — so the predicate would have to decide Fermat's cost from `N` alone.
*Why now?* The trade-off inequality gives the first formal handle: it converts "no
pruning rule" from folklore into a statement about a proved numerical coupling.

## C4. The `±2` obstruction is the only obstruction: classify the ternary Pythagorean trees

**Conjecture.** Up to relabelling, the only triples of integer linear maps that act as a
ternary tree on the node set `{1 ≤ n < m, gcd = 1, m+n odd}` with root `(2,1)` are the
Berggren triple (determinants `±1`) and the Price triple (determinants `±2`), and no
triple of determinant `|det| ≥ 3` exists.

*The key insight is* that determinant `d` forces the gcd of an image pair to divide `d`,
which together with the parity condition (`a+c` and `b+d` odd, proved to be necessary)
leaves only finitely many candidate matrices with entries bounded by the growth of `m`.
*Why now?* An exhaustive search over `|entries| ≤ 3` already returns exactly the six
known generators, so the classification is within reach of a finite case analysis in
Lean.

## C5. A hypotenuse-side tree over the Gaussian integers

**Conjecture.** The obstruction `not_dvd_hypot` (no node has `N ∣ m²+n²` when
`N` has a prime factor `≡ 3 mod 4`) is sharp: for `N` all of whose prime factors are
`≡ 1 (mod 4)`, the nodes with `N ∣ m²+n²` form exactly `2^{ω(N)}` congruence classes of
`(m : n) mod N`, one for each factorisation of `N` into Gaussian primes up to units and
conjugation, and each class contains a node at Price depth `O(log N)`.

*The key insight is* that `m² + n² = |m + in|²`, so hypotenuse divisibility is a
statement about Gaussian ideals, and the tree structure should intertwine with the
Gaussian class group action rather than with the rational ratio `m/n`.
*Why now?* The mod-4 obstruction is proved, so the complementary case is precisely
delimited; Mathlib's `ZMod`, `legendreSym` and Gaussian-integer API make the counting
statement formalisable.

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab — round-net-19 (depth axis, round 9; the carry chain at scale). Paper 63, issue #115. Assessment v20.

## Question
NET-4/5 decomposed the decomposable-error regime on LSB-first base-10 addition: the copy-self basin is a tied-readout artifact (untie ⇒ escape, NET-5), but the **carry chain** is a width/depth/readout-immune credit-assignment wall. The last open question: **does scale unlock depth pay?** Scale up vs NET-5 — dm=192 (untied, 4.5–18× params), bs=256 (2×), 12000 steps (~3× distinct pairs). d∈{1,2,4}×3 seeds = 9 configs, n=6, untied head, per-digit CE, teacher-forced GO-shift, pre-LN, 4 heads, d_mlp=4·dm.

## Part A — 9/9 MASTER, depth pays NOTHING (flat-mastery horn)
| depth | full (mean±std) | per (mean±std) | escape | masters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.9940 ± 0.0085 | 0.9991 ± 0.0013 | [1000,1000,1000] | 3/3 |
| 2 | 1.0000 ± 0.0000 | 1.0000 ± 0.0000 | [1000,1000,1000] | 3/3 |
| 4 | 0.9976 ± 0.0035 | 0.9997 ± 0.0005 | [1000,1000,1000] | 3/3 |

**Scale unlocked depth-1 mastery** (NET-5's d=1 failed 2/3; here all 3 d=1 seeds master). But the d=1 vs d=4 gap is 0.0036 — within seed noise. Deeper nets do NOT beat shallow ones at 4.5–18× params and 3× data; credit-assignment depth-immunity holds at scale. The copy-self-basin + stochastic-escape mechanism reproduces at dm=192 (d=2 s=2: per≈0.87/full≈0.10 plateau st=2000–3000, per⁷=0.38≫full, jump to full=1.0000 at st=4000). Per-position: errors spread thin across interior columns — the model computes the full n=6 sum algorithmically (fresh-draw 1.0000 on a 10¹² pair space rules out memorization).

## Part B — the length wall survives scale: 9/9 at CHANCE
Every mastered config re-trained at n=3, then tested n=4/5/6 (chance 1e-5/1e-6/1e-7):
- 8/9 n=3 trainers master perfectly (full=1.0000); **d=1 s=2 reproduces the NET-5 carry-chain dissociation at 18× params** (per=0.8010 but full=0.2041 — per-high/full-low correlated errors).
- **full=0.0000 at every depth and seed** on n=4/5/6; per-digit ≈0.09–0.22 ≈ the digit floor. Examples: d=1 s=0 n=4 per 0.219; d=4 s=1 n=5 per 0.087 (below the 0.1 floor — the n=3 algorithm misfires structurally); d=4 s=2 all lengths ≈0.10–0.12.
- Deterministic replication: the fast probe (task #89) matched the marathon's d=1 s=0 and d=4 s=0 numbers BYTE-IDENTICAL (same seed/settings ⇒ identical results), confirming the wall at the two depth extremes ~6h before the marathon finished.

## Law
**SCALE-UNLOCKS-LENGTH-SPECIFIC-MASTERY, NOT COMPOSITION + CREDIT-ASSIGNMENT-DEPTH-IMMUNITY-HOLDS-AT-SCALE.** Fixed-length carry computation is depth-flat AND scale-solved (solved at every depth, d=1 included); length-general carry composition is depth- AND scale-immune (chance at every depth, every seed, at the largest arithmetic scale in the program). The carry chain's hard part is NOT capacity — it is length-general composition (memorize-without-compose, NET-3 leg-2 / NET-4/5), a training-objective problem.

## Barriers
- (a) Clean: fresh held-out 2048/batch, 10¹² pair space, no injection. (b) Partial: scale-invariant shallow-transformer results known; NEW = scale-resolution of NET-5's under-powered d=1 + the scale-immune length wall + the d=1 s=2 dissociation at 18× params; Catalog (698 pkgs) no carry-chain-at-scale depth law. (c) CONFRONTED — dm=192/bs=256/12000 steps is the largest arithmetic setup in the program; the scale-up failed to break the law, that IS the finding. (d) Clean: fresh random held-out batches, no test pair ever trained. (e) 3 seeds × every config (9/9 + 9/9) + byte-identical probe replication. (f) Per-digit AND full-number separated, chance ceilings per length, per^7 correlated-error diagnostic, per-position across all 7 columns, two-step d=2 s=2 escape documented. (g) Within-program d=1/d=2/d=4 identical architecture, NOT budget-matched (generous to depth) and still flat. (h) Honest negative: **do not scale depth or width to fix length-general arithmetic** — attack the objective (carry curriculum, scratchpad/CoT intermediates, a stateful carry cell / recurrence).

## Next
The depth axis has had 9 iterations (all flat — the load-bearing boundary still needs NON-POSITIONAL stack content / s≫64 / unbounded nesting WITH causal masking). Standing alternatives: attention-cost law at a second seed (k* ∝ ctx proportionality is 1-seed-per-point), or a fresh axis. Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_carry_scale.py (ALL_DONE), /tmp/exp_net_carry_lenprobe.py (PROBE_DONE).
directions.title: NET-19: Scale unlocks length-SPECIFIC mastery but NOT length-general composition — the carry chain is solved at every depth at dm=192, the length wall is depth- and scale-immune (credit-assignment depth-immunity holds at scale)

# Future Directions — Spectral Free-Witness, next cycle

Derived from the analysis and adversarial review of this cycle's verified results
(`Catalog/Algebra/SpectralFreeWitness.lean`, `…Walk.lean`, `…Sharp.lean`, `…Lower.lean`).

Established this cycle (all machine-checked, 0 sorries):

* **Doubling lemma** `exists_dyadic_quarter`, spectral gap `μ_k ≤ 1 − 1/(2(M+1))`.
* **Recovery** `heat_kernel_order_recovery`: `round(1/p_n(e)) = r` at `n = 8(M+1)²`
  whenever `r ≤ N ≤ 2^M`; corollary for `r = ord_N(b)`.
* **Operational grounding** `walk_return_eq_heatReturn`: the spectral expression *is*
  the `n`-step return probability of the diffusion (characters are eigenvectors +
  discrete Fourier inversion).
* **Sharpness** `dyadic_gap_isTheta` and **necessity** `heat_kernel_needs_quadratic_time`:
  the diffusion time is `Θ((log N)²)`, not `O(log N)`.
* **Correction** `heatReturn_approx_multiplicative`: the witness *value* is
  multiplicative in the order up to `1/N²`; only the mechanism is spectral.
* **Payload** `factor_from_even_order`: a recovered even order splits `N` by one gcd.

---

## C1. The sharp dyadic deficiency constant is 2

**Conjecture.** For every `r ≥ 2`, every `k ≢ 0 (mod r)` and every `M` with `r ≤ 2^M`,

  `Σ_{t=0}^{M} (1 − cos(2π k 2^t / r)) ≥ 2`,

with equality only for `(r, k) = (2, 1)`.  Consequently `λ_k ≤ 1 − 2/(M+1)` and
`μ_k ≤ 1 − 1/(M+1)`, halving the mixing constant to `n = 4(M+1)²`.

*The key insight is* that the doubling lemma produces not just one far-arc visit but a
**budget**: the orbit `x, 2x, 4x, …` must cross the far arc, and the crossing costs at
least `1` in deficiency, while the *approach* to the crossing (the last doubling before
it, whose circle distance is exactly half) costs a further amount that never vanishes.

*Why now?* Our proof only extracts the single crossing term (giving `≥ 1`); the
exhaustive search in `ComputationalEvidence.md` §5 shows the truth is exactly `2` for all
`M ≤ 9`, so the missing factor is a bookkeeping argument over consecutive doublings, not
a new idea.  Falsifiable by a single `(r, k, M)` with deficiency `< 2`.

## C2. The Mersenne family is the extremal gap family, with constant `c* ≈ 3.3946`

**Conjecture.** `lim_{M→∞} (1 − λ₁(2^M − 1, M)) (M+1) = c*` exists, `c* = 2π²/3 · κ` for an
explicit `κ`, and for all `r ≤ 2^M` and `k ≢ 0`, `(1 − λ_k)(M+1) ≥ 2` with the supremum of
the *minimal-gap-over-large-r* profile attained along Mersenne cycles.

*The key insight is* that for `r = 2^M − 1` the dyadic orbit `{2^t}` is exactly the set of
binary place values, so the deficiency is a geometric series `Σ 4^t/r²` truncated at the
top — a self-similar quantity, which is why the numerics converge to five digits by
`M = 12`.

*Why now?* `dyadicEigen_mersenne_ge` already gives the `Θ(1/M)` shape with constant 106;
closing the gap between 106 and 3.3946 needs only sharper cosine control at the few top
frequencies (`t ≥ M − 3`), where the quadratic bound is wasteful.

## C3. Lacunary base-`a` walks: gap `Θ(1/(M_a + 1))` with `M_a = ⌈log_a r⌉`

**Conjecture.** For any integer `a ≥ 2`, the walk with generators `{± a^t : t ≤ M_a}` on
`Z/rZ` (with `gcd(a, r)` arbitrary) has all nontrivial eigenvalues `≤ 1 − 1/(M_a + 1)`,
and the corresponding recovery `round(1/p_n(e)) = r` holds at `n = 8 (M_a+1)²`; moreover
the constant degrades exactly like `log a`, so `a = 2` is optimal among all lacunary bases.

*The key insight is* that the doubling lemma is really an *`a`-adic drift* lemma: the
circle distance is multiplied by `a` at every step until it exceeds `r/(2a)`, so the arc
one lands in is `[r/(2a), 1 − r/(2a)]` and the negative-cosine window shrinks with `a`.

*Why now?* Our `cdist_double` / `cdist_pow_two` proofs are entirely arithmetic and
generalise verbatim with `2 → a`; the only new ingredient is the cosine sign on the
narrower arc.  Falsifiable computationally for `a = 3, 5, 10` in minutes.

## C4. Aggregation necessity in the straight-line model (barrier-4, formalisable form)

**Conjecture.** Any straight-line arithmetic program that, given `r` and `M`, outputs a
number `p` with `|p − p_n(e)| < 1/(4r²)` while reading only `o(r)` of the eigenvalues
`μ_0, …, μ_{r−1}` as inputs, must fail on some instance.  Equivalently: the heat-kernel
witness is *sealed by aggregation* in the read-limited model.

*The key insight is* that the recovery map is rigid — `heatReturn_injective` shows the
value determines `r` exactly — so any program reading few coordinates can be fooled by
switching an unread eigenvalue, since each `μ_k^n` can be made to carry `Θ(1/r)` of the
total mass by choosing `k` in the slow band.

*Why now?* Rigidity is already proved; what remains is a purely combinatorial adversary
argument in a model simple enough to formalise (finite index sets, no real-RAM
subtleties).  This is the first version of "barrier 4" that is actually a theorem
statement rather than a slogan.

## C5. Witness-value multiplicativity is not an accident: a classification dichotomy

**Conjecture.** Every free witness that recovers a residue/order coordinate `r ≤ N` to
accuracy `o(1/r²)` is, as a function of `r`, within `O(1/N²)` of a *multiplicative*
function of `r`; the "spectral vs. CRT-multiplicative" distinction therefore lives in the
*computation*, never in the witness value.

*The key insight is* that exact rounding forces the witness to agree with `1/r` (or an
invertible reparametrisation of it) to accuracy `1/(2r²)`, and `1/r` is multiplicative —
this is exactly what `heatReturn_approx_multiplicative` proves for the heat kernel.

*Why now?* This cycle turned a qualitative classification label into a quantitative,
checkable statement; the general version needs only an abstract "recovery ⇒ proximity to
`1/r`" lemma, which our rounding lemma `round_one_div_of_close` already contains in germ.

# Future directions — after the asymmetric/symmetric divisibility dichotomy

The formal results of this run (all in `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHint*.lean`, 0
sorries, only the standard axioms) are:

1. **Fibre dichotomy** (`asym_fiber_card`, `sym_fiber_card`,
   `sym_fiber_card_incl_excl`): in any finite group, a one-sided condition on a
   factorisation `n = a·b` has an `n`-independent count `|A|`, while the two-sided
   condition has count `|A ∪ n·A⁻¹| = 2|A| - |A ∩ n·A⁻¹|`.
2. **Information form** (`miF_asym_zero`, `mi_asym_three`, `mi_sym_three`,
   `mi_sym_three_bounds`, `information_dichotomy`): the asymmetric mutual information is
   *exactly* `0` for every finite group and every `A`; the symmetric one is
   `3/2 - (3/4)·log₂3 ∈ (0.30, 0.32)` bits at `l = 3` and strictly positive for every
   odd prime.
3. **Classification** (`miF_symJointG_eq_zero_iff_autocorrelation`): the symmetric leak
   vanishes *iff* the autocorrelation `n ↦ |A ∩ n·A⁻¹|` is constant — the perfect
   difference-set condition.
4. **Unconditional impossibility** (`asym_no_residue_dial_any_modulus`,
   `asym_no_residue_dial_three_factors`, `smoothness_no_residue_dial_1155`,
   `no_pm_one_smoothness_hint`): no function of `N mod M` — for *any* `M`, and for two-
   or three-factor moduli — computes `l ∣ p-1`, nor `10`-smoothness of `p-1`; and the
   `N ± 1` smoothness bits are logically independent of the secret bit.
5. **Tropicalisation** (`fibreSum_left`, `tropical_firstCost_const`,
   `tropical_dichotomy`): the dichotomy is a property of the fibration `G × G → G`
   valued in an arbitrary commutative monoid, so it survives into the min-plus semiring,
   where the symmetric statistic becomes a *cheapest factorisation with all factors
   cheap* cost.
6. **Closed form and decay** (`symMI`, `miF_symJointG_singleton_eq_symMI`,
   `mi_sym_units`, `symMI_two`, `symMI_four`, `mi_sym_five_bounds`,
   `symMI_lt_two_div_sq`, `neg_lt_symMI`, `symMI_tendsto_zero`, `mi_sym_decay`,
   `dichotomy_with_rate`): the symmetric leak in a finite group of order `d` equals
   `symMI d` exactly; at `l = 5` this is certified to lie in `(0.0355, 0.036)`, matching
   the measured `0.036`; and `symMI d = O(1/d²) → 0`, so the visible half of the
   dichotomy is itself asymptotically invisible.  (This closes the previous cycle's
   Conjecture A, and corrects its guessed rate `c/g` to `c/g²`.)

7. **The sharp rate** (`log_div_bounds`, `symMI_envelope`, `symMI_asymptotic`, in
   `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHintAsymptotics.lean`): `d²·symMI d → log₂ e - 1 =
   0.442695…`, so the symmetric leak is asymptotically exactly `(log₂ e - 1)/(l-1)²`
   bits.  (This closes the Conjecture A′ of the second cycle.)

8. **Subgroup targets always leak** (`sym_fiber_subgroup_mem`,
   `sym_fiber_subgroup_not_mem`, `miF_symJointG_pos_of_subgroup`, in
   `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHintSubgroupTargets.lean`): for any subgroup `H ⪇ G` the
   symmetric fibre count is `|H|` on `H` and `2|H|` off it, so the leak is strictly
   positive — this covers the quadratic-residue and `k`-th-power events, and it *refutes*
   the previous cycle's guess that cosets of subgroups are the invisible sets.

9. **Invisible targets classified for abelian groups** (`reprCount`,
   `autocorrelation_eq_reprCount`, `charSum_sq_eq_reprCount_sum`,
   `reprCount_const_iff_trivial`, `miF_symJointG_eq_zero_iff_trivial`,
   `abelian_dichotomy`, `miF_symJointG_pos_units_of_nontrivial`, in
   `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHintInvisibleTargets.lean`): in a finite **abelian**
   group the representation count `r_A(n) = #{(a,b) ∈ A² : ab = n}` is constant *only*
   for `A = ∅` and `A = G`, hence the symmetric leak vanishes iff the target is trivial
   and is strictly positive for every other target.  The proof is Fourier analysis on
   `Additive G`: `r̂_A = (1̂_A)²`, so constancy kills every nontrivial character sum and
   `1_A` must be constant.  This **closes the previous cycle's Conjecture B in the
   abelian case**, which is the case relevant to `(ZMod l)ˣ` and hence to the
   divisibility events `l ∣ p - 1`.

10. **Positive information, zero prediction advantage** (`predCount`,
   `predCount_le_bayes`, `predCount_asym_le_best_constant`,
   `predCount_sym_singleton_le_constant`,
   `sym_singleton_positive_information_zero_advantage`,
   `predCount_sym_beats_constants_of_card_three`,
   `units_positive_information_zero_advantage`, in
   `Catalog/Tropical/SmoothSelfHintPredictionAdvantage.lean`): scoring a
   residue-reading predictor `f : G → Bool` by the number of ordered pairs it classifies
   correctly, **no** predictor beats the better constant predictor for the asymmetric
   event (any target, any group), and — the new phenomenon — none beats the constant
   predictor for the *symmetric* event with the arithmetic target `A = {1}` as soon as
   `4 ≤ |G|`, even though the mutual information there is strictly positive.  The
   hypothesis is sharp: in a group of order `3` the Bayes predictor scores `6` against
   `5` and `4` for the two constants.  Arithmetically (`l ≥ 5` prime): the symmetric
   divisibility event leaks bits about `N mod l` that no algorithm can convert into a
   better-than-trivial guess.  So the visible half of the dichotomy is visible only in
   the information-theoretic sense — operationally the whole dichotomy is invisible.

Below are the next conjectures, ranked by expected impact.

## Conjecture A″ (a variance law for arbitrary targets)

For an arbitrary target `A ⊆ G` with `|G| = d` write `f_A(n) = |symFiber A n|` for the
symmetric fibre count.  Conjecture: as `d → ∞` along any family with
`f_A(n)/d → 0` uniformly,

```
miF (symJointG A) = (log₂ e / 2) · Var_n(f_A(n)) / (d² · E_n f_A(n)) · (1 + o(1)),
```

i.e. the leak is a chi-squared statistic of the autocorrelation of `A`.  The singleton
case `f_A ∈ {1, 2}` gives `Var = (d-1)/d²`, `E = (2d-1)/d`, and the formula reproduces
the proved constant `log₂ e - 1` up to the exact correction computed here.

*The key insight is* that mutual information is a second-order quantity: to leading order
it is `(log₂ e / 2)` times the chi-squared divergence between the joint law and the
product of its marginals, and by the classification theorem that divergence is exactly
the variance of the autocorrelation `n ↦ |A ∩ n·A⁻¹|`.

*Why now?* The classification (`miF_symJointG_eq_zero_iff_autocorrelation`) already says
the leak vanishes iff that variance vanishes; this conjecture is its quantitative form,
and the singleton case is now proved with an explicit envelope that generalises verbatim
once `f_A` replaces `1`/`2`.

## Conjecture B′ (invisible targets in *nonabelian* groups)

Result 9 settles the abelian case.  Conjecture: the same classification holds with no
commutativity hypothesis — in **any** finite group, `r_A(n) = #{(a,b) ∈ A² : ab = n}` is
constant only for `A ∈ {∅, G}`, so `miF_symJointG_eq_zero_iff_trivial` holds verbatim for
`G` nonabelian.

*The key insight is* that the abelian proof reads `r̂_A(χ) = (1̂_A(χ))²` and concludes
`1̂_A(χ) = 0`; for a nonabelian `G` the same computation gives `ρ(1_A)² = 0` for every
nontrivial irreducible `ρ`, and a *nonzero nilpotent* matrix is not excluded by the
identity alone — so the conjecture is equivalent to ruling out nilpotent Fourier
coefficients of a `0/1`-valued class-free function, which should follow from the
self-adjointness relation `ρ(1_A)^* = ρ(1_{A^{-1}})` together with `A = A⁻¹` after
replacing `A` by `A ∪ A⁻¹`.

*Why now?* The abelian argument is fully formalised here, and the only missing input is
the matrix-valued Fourier inversion for finite groups, whose ingredients
(`MonoidAlgebra`, character orthogonality) are already in Mathlib.

## Conjecture C (no self-hint from any symmetric functional)

For every `M`, no function of the *unordered* data — the residue `N mod M` together with
any symmetric functions of the factors, e.g. `p + q` mod `M` — determines `l ∣ p - 1`.
Only an oracle that breaks the `p ↔ q` symmetry can.

*The key insight is* that the swap construction of `asym_indistinguishable_mod` produces
two instances related by exchanging the residues of the factors, so **every** symmetric
functional agrees on them while the asymmetric bit flips.

*Why now?* The construction is already unconditional (Dirichlet only), and the
three-factor extension shows it is robust; the remaining work is to make the swap into
an involution on the chosen progressions so that `p + q` is preserved as well.

## Conjecture D (tropical smoothness profile is a genuine invariant)

Define `w(N) = min over factorisations N = a·b of max(log a, log b)`.  Then `w` is not
computable from `N mod M` for any `M`, `w` is a monotone min-plus functional of the
multiset of prime factors, and the distribution of `w` on `k`-bit semiprimes converges
after normalisation to a Dickman-type law — the `~0.04` fit reported for the density.

*The key insight is* that `worstCost`, already defined and shown non-constant here, is
the finite-group shadow of the smoothness profile, so the fibre argument that kills the
asymmetric leak also explains why only the symmetric smoothness statistic is visible.

*Why now?* `fibreSum_left` gives the min-plus transfer principle for free; the missing
ingredient is a Lean-formalised Dickman function.

## Conjecture E′ (an exact threshold for actionable leakage)

Result 10 proves zero advantage for the singleton target once `4 ≤ |G|`, and exhibits
order `3` as the unique exception.  Conjecture the general criterion: for an arbitrary
target `A`, the Bayes predictor of the symmetric event beats both constant predictors
**iff**

```
∑_n max(f_A(n), |G| - f_A(n))  >  max(∑_n f_A(n), ∑_n (|G| - f_A(n))),
```

which — since `f_A(n) = 2|A| - |A ∩ n·A⁻¹|` — happens iff the autocorrelation
`n ↦ |A ∩ n·A⁻¹|` crosses the level `2|A| - |G|/2`.  In particular no target with
`|A| ≤ |G|/4` is ever actionable, so *actionable* leakage requires a dense target, while
*informational* leakage requires only a nonconstant autocorrelation: the two thresholds
differ by a factor `|G|`.

*The key insight is* that `predCount_le_bayes` makes the optimum an explicit sum of
pointwise maxima, so the whole question reduces to comparing `∑ max(f, |G| - f)` with the
two constant sums — a purely combinatorial inequality about the autocorrelation, with no
information theory left in it.

*Why now?* Both sides of the inequality are already definable and the singleton instance
is proved in both directions (zero advantage for `|G| ≥ 4`, positive advantage for
`|G| = 3`), so the general statement is a strict generalisation of a formalised
special case.
