## Round-net-18 (compression axis, depth-robustness check)

**Hypothesis.** NET-12's per-channel practical optimum (per-row uniform-4, lossless 0.987 @ 4.00 bits at d=4) — does it survive d=8 on the same real causal LM?

**Setup.** Same 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads, d=8 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc 0.1619 (bar 0.1587), loss 5.0788. 52 matrices, per-row symmetric RTN, every eval JOINT (fresh loaded copy, full held-out 60k forward).

**Results (d=8; d=4 NET-12 refs in parens).**

| config | primitive | d=8 retained | d=4 retained | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| uniform-4 | per-row | **0.967** | **0.987 ✓** | −2.0 pts |
| uniform-3 | per-row | 0.873 | 0.947 | −7.4 pts |
| role(4/3/2) | per-row | 0.801 | 0.892 | −9.1 pts |
| uniform-3 | per-tensor | 0.705 | 0.825 | −12.0 pts |

**LAW: DEPTH-DEEPENS-QUANT-FLOOR.** The 4-bit per-channel interface floor is a d=4 property: uniform-4 falls below the 0.98 lossless bar at d=8 (0.967). The depth penalty lands at every bit level, worst where the schedule sits near the robustness cliff (uniform-3, role, per-tensor uniform-3 — agrees with NET-11's d=8 0.73 within eval noise). Both axes' lossless operating points shrink with depth at fixed width — the compression mirror of NET-16's k*≈4d. **Quote the depth with any 4-bit lossless claim.**

**Barriers (a–h):** joint evals / data-free RTN (a); per-channel quant known, depth-dependence of the floor new — Catalog 698 pkgs no depth sweep on a real causal LM (b); real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, d=8 (c); no leakage (d); 1 model/depth, exact family reproduction, eval noise ≈0.15% (e); 0.98 bar + raw loss, cross-check vs NET-11 (f); uniform-2/3/4 + role joint baselines, d=4 refs same family (g); real consequence: depth must be quoted (h).

Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/18_CompressionFloorDepthScalingSmallLM.md

## NET-16 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-16, speed axis — depth-scaling check of the NET-15 DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE law)

**Hypothesis.** NET-15 (d=4) established: trained causal attention is diffuse (eff support 46.6/128) yet data-free top-k key/value pruning is lossless at k*=16 (0.984 ≥ 0.98 bar, 8× attention-core FLOPs). Its stated caveat was scale. This round tests DEPTH: does lossless-k / the concentration law shift at d=8 on the same real causal LM?

**Setup (identical NET-15).** 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 word vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads, **d=8 s0**, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc **0.1619** (d=4 0.1571 — deeper trains slightly better), bar 0.98·full=**0.1587**, full loss **5.0788** (d=4 5.1188). Same explicit causal-attention eval (k=96 recovers full loss exactly, 5.0789). Top-k mask from each eval input own causal attention at inference — data-free.

**Results.**

1. **Part A — the concentration law is DEPTH-INDEPENDENT.** Effective support per head 43.3–56.3, **mean 50.1/128** (d=4 46.6) — if anything slightly MORE diffuse with depth. Top-k mass lower at every level (top-16 0.586 vs 0.617). The diffuse regime is a stable property of this model scale.
2. **Part B — lossless-k GROWS with depth: k* ≈ 4·d.** k=4 0.873 ✗ (d=4 0.940), k=8 0.919 ✗ (0.971), **k=16 0.961 ✗ (d=4 0.984 ✓)** — the 8× lever FAILS at d=8, Δloss +0.047; **k=32 0.983 ✓** (d=4 0.998), Δloss +0.015; k=64 0.997 ✓; k=96 0.999 ✓. Every retained fraction lower and Δloss roughly doubled at each k — per-layer top-k error compounding through the residual stream, the speed-axis mirror of NET-11 compression compounding (deeper = worse).
3. **Part B2 — selection importance GROWS with depth.** Random-k gap: k=16 top-k 0.961 vs random 0.866 = **+9.5 pts** (d=4 +6.2); k=32 0.983 vs 0.912 = **+7.1 pts** (d=4 +4.8). The deeper model relies more on the trained selection information.

**Verdict.** **LAWS: CONCENTRATION-LAW-DEPTH-INDEPENDENT** (eff support ≈47–50 both depths) + **LOSSLESS-K-SCALES-WITH-DEPTH (k* ≈ 4d at fixed ctx)** + **SELECTION-IMPORTANCE-GROWS-WITH-DEPTH**. DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE survives with a documented depth boundary: the 8× attention-core lever at d=4 is a **4×** lever at d=8, and the d=16 prediction (k*=64, 2×) is under test (round-net-17, running). The attention-cost lever is real but a shallow-depth property at fixed ctx — scale-up claims must quote depth.

**8-barrier check:** (a) top-k from eval-input causal attention at inference, joint evals, k=96 exact-loss match (5.0789 vs 5.0788) — nothing injected; (b) top-k sparse attention known, but the k*≈4d depth-scaling + flat concentration law is new; catalog 698 pkgs no depth-scaling attention-cost law on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, 0.98 bar on real next-token; (d) top-k data-free (eval-input attention), contiguous split, held-out eval; (e) 1 model/depth, reproduced exactly 6×, monotone sweep with a knee that MOVED (16→32) in the direction consistent with NET-11 both-depth compounding; (f) 0.98 bar + raw loss, 6-pt sweep + 2-pt random control (fixed seed), k=96 exact numerics, retained vs each model own full (full-loss change 5.1188→5.0788 reported); (g) full ref at each depth + random-k control (+9.5 pts), same bar; (h) real lever (4× at d=8) but depth-scaling is the honest caveat for scale-up claims.

**Assessment:** v16, 16 experiments (NET-1..NET-16). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/16_AttentionCostDepthScalingSmallLM.md`. Script: /tmp/exp_net_attncost_d8.py.

**Next (fan-out running):** round-net-17 (d=16: is k*≈4d confirmed, predicts k*=64/2×?), round-net-18 (d=8 compression floor: does per-channel uniform-4 stay lossless at depth?), round-net-19 (carry chain at scale). Speed axis now 3 real-scale iterations (NET-10 negative, NET-15 positive, NET-16 boundary).
directions.title: NET-16: The attention-cost law scales with depth — lossless-k k* ≈ 4d, concentration depth-independent

directions.description:
## NET-15 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-15, speed-axis rotation — the attention-cost law, FIRST POSITIVE REAL-SCALE SPEED RESULT)

**Hypothesis.** Trained causal attention is concentrated (small effective support), so a data-free top-k key/value cap (keep only the k most-attended past positions per query, chosen at inference from the input own causal attention weights, renormalize) preserves held-out accuracy at an L/k attention-FLOP reduction. Two independent claims: (A) is attention concentrated? (B) is top-k pruning lossless at k ≪ ctx?

**Setup (identical NET-10/11/12/13/14 family).** 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 word vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads (head dim 16), d=4 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc reproduces **0.1571 a sixth time**; bar 0.98·full = 0.1540, full loss 5.1188. Explicit causal-attention forward verified against the standard forward (k=96 recovers full loss exactly, 5.1188). Top-k mask computed from each eval input own trained attention weights at inference — data-free, no calibration, no leakage.

**Results.**

1. **Part A — attention is DIFFUSE, not concentrated.** Per-query effective support exp(H): per-head 39.5–54.7, **mean 46.6/128** vs uniform-causal baseline ≈64.5 — only ~28% more concentrated than uniform. Top-k mass fraction: top-4 0.311, top-8 0.450, top-16 0.617, top-32 0.795. The classical "attention focuses on a few tokens" picture does NOT hold at this scale.
2. **Part B — yet top-k pruning is LOSSLESS at 12.5% of context.** k=4 0.940 ✗ (loss +0.084), k=8 0.971 ✗ (+0.043), **k=16 0.984 ✓ (loss +0.018, +0.36% rel) — 8× attention-core FLOP reduction**, k=32 0.998 ✓ (+0.005, 4×), k=64 1.001 ✓, k=96 1.000 ✓ (≈0 loss). Knee between k=8 and k=16. At ctx 128 attention ≈95% of inference FLOPs (≈260·L² per token per layer vs ≈33k projections + ≈66k MLP), so 8× attention-core ≈ **5–6× total-model speedup**, data-free, no retraining.
3. **Part B2 — the selection is genuine.** Random-k control: k=16 0.922 vs top-k 0.984 = **−6.2 pts**; k=32 0.950 vs 0.998 = **−4.8 pts**. Notably random-16 (0.922) is even WORSE than top-8 (0.971) — selecting the best 8 positions by weight beats selecting any 16 at random.

**Mechanism reconciling A and B.** Attention is diffuse, but the mass beyond the top-k positions is LOW-INFORMATION — renormalizing over the top-k concentrates the retained mass onto the information-carrying positions. Pruning accuracy tracks the weight-selected positions, not the total retained mass.

**Verdict.** The concentration premise (A) is REFUTED (effective support ≈ 47/128) yet data-free top-k pruning is **LOSSLESS at k=16** (0.984 ≥ 0.98 bar, loss +0.018, 8× attention-core / ~5–6× total FLOP reduction), with weight-selected positions genuinely better than random (+6.2 pts). LAW: **DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE** — attention need not be sharply concentrated for lossless top-k pruning at ~12% of context on real text; the speed lever works without a concentration assumption. **First positive real-scale speed result** (toy positives NET-6/7/8; real-scale negative NET-10).

**8-barrier check:** (a) top-k mask uses the model own causal attention weights computed on each eval input at inference — the deployed algorithm; k=64/96 recover the full loss exactly, confirming the explicit-attention path matches the standard forward; nothing injected; (b) top-k sparse attention is a known family (Longformer-style/streaming) but the specific law — lossless at 12.5% of context *despite* diffuse attention (eff support 47) — runs against the concentration-justifies-sparsity story; catalog 698 pkgs, no prior attention-cost law on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, 0.98 bar on real next-token; (d) top-k from the eval input own causal attention, contiguous no-overlap split, held-out eval — no leakage; (e) 1 model reproduced exactly 6×, every eval a full joint forward on 60k held-out tokens, monotone k-sweep with clean knee; (f) 0.98·full bar AND raw loss both reported, 6-point k-sweep + 2-point random control (fixed seed), explicit causal attention verified against standard forward (k=96 exact loss match), eval noise ≈0.15% ≪ k=16 margin; (g) full-attention reference (0.1571/5.1188) + random-k control at the same k (+6.2 pts), same bar; (h) real lever: 8× attention-core / ~5–6× total-model speedup lossless by the accuracy bar (loss +0.36%), data-free and retraining-free — caveated to scale (measured at dm=64/ctx 128; lossless-k and the concentration law may shift at larger scale).

**Assessment:** v15, 15 experiments (NET-1..NET-15). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/15_AttentionCostSmallLM.md`. Script: /tmp/exp_net_attncost.py.

**Next:** does the attention-cost law / lossless-k shift at LARGER scale (d=8, bigger dm, longer ctx — re-measure effective support + k-sweep)? OR carry chain at scale; OR the d=8 compression floor check; OR load-bearing depth (non-positional stack content with causal masking). Speed axis now has 2 real-scale iterations (NET-10 negative, NET-15 positive).
directions.title: NET-15: Attention is diffuse but data-free top-k pruning is lossless at 8× — the DIFFUSE-BUT-PRUNABLE attention-cost law (first positive real-scale speed result)

## NET-14 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-14, compression-axis rotation — the LAST lever)

**Hypothesis.** NET-13 explicitly left one mechanism untested: activation-aware quantization WITH calibration passes — AWQ/SmoothQuant-style per-channel *activation* scales (from a calibration forward pass) absorbed into the weight quantizer. If this breaks the 4-bit interface floor, calibration passes are the sub-4-bit lever.

**Setup (identical NET-10/11/12/13 family).** 5 Gutenberg novels, top-4097 word vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer dm=64/4 heads, d=4 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc reproduces **0.1571 a fifth time**; bar 0.98·full = 0.1540. Calibration: forward pass on 512 **training** sequences (held-out eval never sees it — no leak). AWQ weight-only quantizer: W[:,j] ← W[:,j]/act_max_j^α, per-row RTN, scale back.

**Results.**
1. **Key diagnostic — the activation scales are near-FLAT.** Mean per-channel activation max: un 2.130, wq0 2.116, mi0 2.117, mo0 1.820; max/mean 1.07–1.24. AWQ's absorption only pays when some channels carry 10–100× the activation magnitude of others — this scale has no channel heterogeneity to exploit (activation-side mirror of NET-13's flat weight outliers).
2. **Part A — no help at uniform-3.** AWQ α=0.25 0.938, **α=0.50 0.943** (vs plain per-row 0.947 — marginally *worse*), α=1.00 0.888 (much worse). Uniform-4 identically lossless both ways (0.987).
3. **Part A2 — interface-at-3 still fails.** Interface (embed/pos/un) at 3 with AWQ scales, interior clean: **0.958 @ 3.18 bits**, 2.2 pts short of the bar.
4. **Part B — activation-informed allocation is a BAD signal.** 25 Linears ranked by mean per-channel act max, terciles 4/3/2: **0.828 @ 3.69** (0.841 with AWQ) vs weight-based role 0.892 @ 3.64, uniform-4 0.987 @ 4.00. The ranking only re-discovers the interface is fragile; it cannot allocate below 4 bits.

**Verdict.** The 4-bit interface floor is not just data-free-irreducible (NET-13) but **activation-irreducible** (NET-14) at this scale — even calibration passes don't buy sub-4-bit lossless weight quantization on a small causal LM, because the per-channel activation scales are near-uniform (max/mean ≈ 1.2). **The compression axis at small real-LM scale is EXHAUSTED:** every primitive (per-tensor 5.31 bits, per-row/per-column uniform-4 = 4.00 lossless floor, magnitude-split, percentile-clip, activation-calibration) leaves the interface irreducible below 4 bits. Per-channel uniform-4 (4.00 bits, data-free, 0.987) is the practical optimum.

**8-barrier check:** (a) joint evals, AWQ = standard data-free-of-test transform, calibration on training only — no injection; (b) AWQ/SmoothQuant are mature — the NEGATIVE (doesn't transfer to a small causal LM because activation heterogeneity is absent) is the content; catalog 698 pkgs, no prior activation-calibration test on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab; (d) calibration = training sequences only, eval = held-out; (e) 1 model reproduced exactly 5×, every eval a full joint held-out forward; (f) 0.98 bar, 3-value α-sweep, raw activation stats, plain per-row refs re-verified in-run; hook-closure bug crashed the first launch before data, fixed + re-run clean; (g) plain per-row refs re-measured + role/uniform-4 refs from NET-12; (h) negative closes the compression branch at this scale — rotation to speed (carry chain at scale / attention-cost laws) or a larger-scale compression check (d=8) is next.

**Assessment:** v14, 14 experiments (NET-1..NET-14). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/14_ActivationAwareQuantSmallLM.md`. Script: /tmp/exp_net_act.py.

**Next:** rotate to the speed axis (carry chain at scale / attention-cost laws — speed has had 1 real-scale iteration) OR the one open compression question: does the 4-bit interface floor shift at d=8 / bigger dm?
directions.title: NET-14: Activation-aware quantization WITH calibration passes is a no-op — the compression axis is exhausted at small real-LM scale

directions.description:
## NET-13 — Network/LLM research lab (round-net-13, compression-axis rotation)

**Hypothesis.** NET-12's 4-bit interface (embed/pos/un) floor is an outlier artifact; an activation-aware/outlier-aware primitive (input-channel axis, magnitude split, or outlier clipping) breaks it below 4.0 avg bits.

**Setup (identical NET-10/11/12 family).** 5 Gutenberg novels, word-level top-4097 vocab, ctx 128, contiguous 90/10 split, causal transformer (is_causal=True) dm=64/4 heads, d=4 s0, 2000 AdamW steps. Full acc reproduces **0.1571 a fourth time**; bar 0.98·full = 0.1540. All evals joint (independent loaded copy, full held-out).

**Results.**
1. **Axis:** per-COLUMN (input-channel) RTN is WORSE than per-row — uniform-2 0.413 vs 0.588, uniform-3 0.900 vs 0.947, role 0.923. The standard group-quant axis does not break the floor.
2. **Outlier diagnostics (the key):** top-1% of magnitude holds only ~3.5% of the mass in EVERY matrix (embed 3.6%, un 3.5%, interior 3.0–3.4%); row-norm max/mean 1.1–1.9; heaviest tail un (kurtosis 9.1). This small real causal LM is NOT in the 30–70% outlier regime LLM.int8/AWQ/SmoothQuant target.
3. **Magnitude split:** interface top-k rows → 6-bit, rest → 2-bit: k=0 0.636 → k=256 (top-6%) **0.819 @ 2.74 bits** — sublinear, saturating, 16 pts short of lossless. The need is distributed.
4. **Outlier clipping:** percentile-scaled per-row RTN (99.9th/99.0th) changes nothing — uniform-3 stays 0.944–0.948 (under bar), uniform-4 stays lossless (0.982–0.985).

**Verdict.** The 4-bit interface floor from NET-12 survives **every standard data-free weight-quantization primitive** at this scale; it is structural (distributed sensitivity, no outlier mass to exploit). NET-12's remaining data-free "activation-aware allocation" idea is REFUTED. The honest remaining lever is activation-aware quantization **with calibration passes** (SmoothQuant-style per-channel *activation* scales — the one non-data-free option).

**8-barrier check:** (a) joint evals, data-free transforms — no injection; (b) primitives are standard LLM-quant methods, the NEGATIVE (none break the floor on a real causal LM) is the content; catalog (698 packages) has no outlier/activation-aware test on a real small causal LM; (c) confronted — real causal LM, real text, causal masking, 4097 vocab, and Part B quantifies why this model is not in the target regime; (d) causal masking + contiguous split + data-free quantization; (e) 1 model reproduced exactly 4×, every eval a full joint held-out forward; (f) 0.98 bar throughout, raw outlier stats, 7-point k-sweep, first-launch script bug fixed + re-run clean; (g) per-row/per-tensor refs from same family, honest uniform-2/3/4 + role baselines; (h) negative closes a branch — don't expect AWQ-style weight fixes to beat 4-bit lossless on a small causal LM.

**Assessment:** v13, 13 experiments (NET-1..NET-13). Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/13_OutlierQuantSmallLM.md`. Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_outlier.py, /tmp/exp_net_outlier_partD.py.

**Next:** activation-aware quantization WITH calibration passes / per-channel 3-bit with outlier retention / interface floor at d=8 (larger dm).
directions.title: NET-13: Activation-aware (outlier) quantization is NOT the lever — the 4-bit interface floor is structural on a real causal LM

directions.description:
## NET-12 — Joint-aware bit allocation on a real causal LM (compression axis; the confirmed real target from NET-11)

**Paper:** `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/12_JointAllocSmallLM.md` · Notebook Part 12 · Assessment v12. Scripts `/tmp/exp_net_joint.py`, `/tmp/exp_net_joint_partC.py`, `/tmp/exp_net_joint_partC2.py`.

**Setup:** the same real causal word LM (5 Gutenberg novels, dm=64, vocab 4097, ctx 128, causal masking, d=4, 2000 steps) — full acc reproduces 0.1571 a third time; lossless bar 0.98·full = 0.1540. Every eval is a **joint** quantization of an independent model copy.

### Part A — joint-marginal map
With everything else at the role schedule (4/3/2): attention projections (all 16) are **exactly indifferent at 2 bits** (retained flat at 0.878); **embed 3-bit jointly retains 0.849** (isolation ≈0.95 — compounding is real, ~11 points); readout **un 2-bit collapses to 0.280** (most fragile matrix, jointly); MLP 2-bit 0.80–0.85, 3-bit fine.

### Part B — per-tensor greedy strict-lossless frontier = **5.31 avg bits**
Greedy from all-6 keeping retained ≥ 0.98·full: **interface (embed/pos/un, 73% of params) pinned at 6**, MLP mostly 4, attention 2–3, lnf 2; retained 0.982. Even **all-4 misses the bar per-tensor (0.979 vs 0.980)**. Per-tensor static RTN cannot get under ≈5.3 bits losslessly on real text.

### Part C — per-channel (per-row) RTN is the fix
Uniform all-4 per-row is **lossless at 4.00 bits (retained 0.987)** — 1.3 bits below the per-tensor frontier. Per-row uniform-3 still fails (0.947); the **4-bit interface is irreducible under both primitives**; uniform-2 hopeless (0.588); the per-tensor-optimized frontier scores **worse per-row (0.973)** — allocation is primitive-dependent.

### Part C2 — the rotation's question, answered no
"4-bit interface + all interior 2": **0.733** @ 3.46 bits. "4-bit interface + MLP 4 + attention 2": **0.907** @ 3.82 bits. Uniform-4: 0.987. The 8-point gap between the last two is almost all attention 2→4 ⇒ **"attention is 2-bit free" is an operating-point artifact** — true in isolation and at the degraded 0.878 baseline, but 2-bit attention costs ~8 points in a clean joint network.

### Answers
- **Any data-free schedule reach lossless?** YES — per-channel uniform-4 (4.0 bits).
- **Is 4-bit interface + 2-bit interior enough?** NO (0.733 / 0.907).
- **Correction to NET-11:** "no static RTN schedule ≤3.7 bits lossless" was about the *per-tensor* primitive; per-channel uniform-4 is lossless. The practical lever is the per-channel primitive, not smarter per-tensor allocation.

### Barriers (8)
(a) joint evals on independent loaded copy, greedy = pure allocation search — no injection · (b) per-channel/group quantization is standard (rescue = known-primitive confirmation), but the joint-damage quantification is new; Catalog 2094 packages, no prior work · (c) real causal LM, causal masking, 4097 vocab — confronted head-on, toy uniform-3 fails again · (d) causal masking + contiguous split + data-free quantization · (e) 1 seed, 4 config families × 4–5 bit levels × ≤51 greedy steps, each a full joint eval; 0.1571 reproduced exactly 3× · (f) 0.98 bar throughout, all-4 knife-edge called out, eval noise ≈0.15%, greedy stopping verified, PART C 1-D-lnf crash fixed + re-run clean · (g) uniform-2/3 + role + all-4/6 + full-precision baselines at the same bar · (h) practical lever = per-channel primitive (uniform-4, data-free); 2-bit-attention "wins" measured at degraded operating points do not survive a clean net.
directions.title: NET-12: Joint-aware bit allocation on a real causal LM — per-tensor floor ~5.3 bits, per-channel uniform-4 is lossless, 'attention is 2-bit free' was an operating-point artifact

directions.description:
**Round-net-11 (compression-axis real-scale rotation). Paper:** ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/11_PRlawSmallLM.md

**Setup:** real causal LMs on 5 Gutenberg novels (dm=64, vocab 4097, ctx 128, causal masking), d=4 and d=8, 2000 AdamW steps — full held-out acc reproduces NET-10 exactly (0.1571/0.1619). For every matrix: PR=(Σs²)²/Σs⁴ and b* = min per-tensor RTN bits retaining ≥0.98·full (isolated); then joint uniform-2/3 and role-schedule joint.

**Result 1 — role structure survives, PR predictor fails.** Identical on both depths (28/52 matrices): attention projections (PR 19–32) 2-bit lossless; MLP projections (PR 31–52) need 3 bits; embed (PR 63) + pos (PR 40) need 4 bits; the readout un (PR 14.9–15.3, the LOWEST PR) needs 4 bits with catastrophic 2-bit collapse (27–32% retained); lnf (PR=1) 2-bit lossless. Low-PR readout → most bits, and same-PR attention-vs-MLP differ ⇒ corr(PR,b*)=+0.58/+0.67 is role-grouping in disguise, NOT a monotone law.

**Result 2 — NET-1's practical schedule refuted at real scale.** Joint uniform-2 collapses (retained 0.16/0.05); **joint uniform-3 is NOT lossless** (retained 0.83 d=4 / 0.73 d=8, worse with depth — per-layer isolation says ≥95% everywhere at 3 bits, but compounding costs 17–27 points, amplified by residual-stream norm growth through depth). Role schedule (embed/pos/un=4, MLP=3, attn=2): retained **0.878 at 3.64 avg bits** — +5pts over uniform-3 at +21% bits, still 12% short of lossless. **No static RTN schedule ≤3.7 avg bits is lossless on real text.**

**Verdict:** NET-1's monotone b*(PR) law and its toy practical schedule (uniform-3 lossless) do NOT transfer to a real causal LM. Surviving: coarse role structure (interface fragile / interior robust). Live compression target: joint/activation-aware allocation, not data-free per-matrix PR.

**Barriers:** (a) no injection, PR/b* independent, RTN data-free; (b) sensitivity-based mixed precision known, the real-scale negatives new (Catalog 2094 packages no prior work); (c) confronted — this IS the real-scale check and the toy law/schedule fail it; (d) causal masking + contiguous split, no leakage; (e) 2 models × every matrix, identical structure both depths; (f) 0.98·full bar with full retained fractions, exact NET-10 reproduction; (g) uniform-2/3 + full-precision baselines; (h) the negative is the win — don't ship uniform-2/3 on toy/isolated measurements.

**Scripts:** /tmp/exp_net_pr_lm.py, /tmp/exp_net_pr_role.py
directions.title: NET-11: The PR quantization law does NOT transfer to a real causal LM — role-structured bit-need survives (interface fragile/interior robust), but no static RTN schedule ≤3.7 avg bits is lossless (uniform-3 retains only 0.83/0.73, worse with depth)

directions.description:
**Round-net-10 (network/LLM lab, real-scale rotation).** Two results, both machine-verified.

## 1. Part A — the toy depth line leaked: full attention put the answer in the input

The toy TF class uses FULL (bidirectional) attention on next-token tasks: at position t the model attends to position t+1 — the very token it must output. A copy-the-future circuit yields 100% on any deterministic next-token task. The leak is PROVEN by an information bound: on Dyck-2, new-open types are iid random and 47.8% of next-tokens are opens, so the best causal accuracy is **0.7609 overall** — full-attention's recorded 1.0000 is impossible causally.

Causal re-runs (same architecture/budget, is_causal=True, 6000 steps, dm=48):
- Dyck-2 d=1: overall 0.557 / close_all 0.917 (d=2: 0.563/0.926) vs recorded 1.0000; extended budget asymptotes close_all ≈0.92 (0.9105→0.9135→0.9207 at 6k/12k/18k), still −8pts at 3× budget.
- Lookup (deterministic, ceiling 1.0): d≈1≈d≈2 ≈ 0.89 vs NET-2's 1.0000 — the artifact is NOT limited to random-type tasks.

**Survives the honesty fix:** the flat-depth SHAPE (d=1 ≈ d=2 on both classes) and transformer-beats-linear on close recovery (+17pp over the causal windowed-linear baseline — the NET-8 +25pp was a causal-baseline vs full-attention-transformer mismatch). **Corrected:** NET-8/9 'd=1 = 1.0000 / load-bearing-boundary-not-found' absolute claims withdrawn.

## 2. Part B — the exit law does NOT transfer to a real LM (0/4 lossless at crossover)

Real causal GPT on 5 Gutenberg novels (dm=64, vocab 4097, ctx 128, d∈{4,8}×2 seeds, teacc 0.157–0.162). Norm profile is **reset-then-grow** (dip then growth, crossover l=2–4), NOT the toy's flat-≈d/2-then-grow. Shared-head acc climbs monotonically through the full depth; the crossover marks the ONSET of decodability growth, not its completion. |exit*−cross| = 2/2/5/3, lossless@cross=False in 4/4. The calibration-free dynamic-depth-schedule idea is not supported at real-LM scale.

Full paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/10_CausalityScreen_ExitLawRealLM.md. Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_lm.py, /tmp/exp_net_lookup_causal.py. Barriers all checked (paper §5). Assessment v10. Now 10 network experiments.
directions.title: NET-10: The toy depth law's 1.0000s were a full-attention future-peek artifact (ceiling 0.7609 < 1.0000), and the exit law does not transfer to a real causal LM (0/4 lossless at crossover)

directions.description:
**Network/LLM research lab — round-net-9 (depth axis, round 7). Machine-verified. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/9_BoundedStack_Scaling.md. Script: /tmp/exp_net_dyck2_scale.py.**

## Hypothesis
After NET-8 refuted the load-bearing premise at s=12/dm48, find where a single layer finally breaks: (1) context scaling — at larger semilength the balance spans more levels and closes route to opens at distance up to 2s−1; (2) width scaling — one layer must hold BOTH the balance prefix-sum AND the balance-conditioned position routing, so at dm=16/12, d=2 (stack the subtasks) should win.

## Part A — depth FLAT across context scaling (s∈{16,32}, dm=48, d∈{1,2}×2 seeds, 6000 steps)
ALL 8 models: test=1.0000, close_all=1.0000, close_b4+=1.0000. **d=1 is perfect even at semilength 32 (context 64) — closes route to matching opens up to 63 tokens back.** Context length is NOT the boundary.

## Part B — depth FLAT across width scaling (dm∈{16,12}, s=12, d∈{1,2}×2 seeds)
ALL 8 models: test=1.0000 at every metric. **d=1 is perfect even at dm=12 (head dim 3).** Width is NOT the boundary either.

## Part C — non-flat screen
No config with d=1 < d=2 (close_all gap > 0.01) — every pair equal at 1.0000; the shared-head exit branch correctly not triggered (no depth-using model to exit).

## Mechanism
Single-layer soft attention implements a **bounded stack**: the stack-top STATE is the scalar running balance (one head's prefix-sum); the stack-top CONTENT is positionally stored (attention routes each close query to the matching open at balance-depth balance_before−1 via balance-conditioned key match + recency, reads the stored type). No second layer needed because the state is scalar and the content is at a computable position. Boundary needs: balance range exceeding dm precision (s≫64), unbounded nesting/length-gen (NET-4's wall), or **NON-POSITIONAL stack content** (content computed from multiple distant positions — the genuinely hard case, natural next load-bearing target).

## Barriers
(a) no circularity (fresh random words, iid types, test seed+77); (b) related circuits acknowledged (attention-as-bounded-stack is mech-interp folklore; the scaling-sweep negative + five-class × context × width flatness are new; Catalog 698 packages no prior work); (c) toy-scale AND the finding — boundary not reached at context ≤64/width ≥12; (d) no leakage (held-out 1.0000 before probing); (e) 2 seeds × every config, 16/16 consistent; (f) documented; two post-data script bugs fixed (SUMMARY 4-vs-3 tuple unpack after all models done; Part C RA 4-tuple lookup fell to RB arm — the (16,48)/(32,48) pairs verified EQUAL by direct inspection, automated screen covered dm∈{16,12}, verdict correct over all 16); (g) inherited from NET-8 (windowed baseline −25pp); (h) honest negative with a target: depth gives nothing on bounded-stack grammar at every affordable scale.

## Verdict
The load-bearing boundary is NOT found at context ≤64 / width ≥12 — flat-depth law now covers five task classes AND holds across context and width scaling on the non-regular grammar. Next load-bearing candidates: non-positional stack content, s≫64, unbounded nesting; and rotate axes to real-scale checks (exit law / PR law on a small LM — the depth axis has had 7 iterations).
directions.title: NET-9: Load-bearing boundary NOT found — depth flat across context (s≤32) and width (dm≥12) scaling of Dyck-2; single-layer soft attention implements a bounded stack

directions.description:
**Network/LLM research lab — round-net-8 (depth axis, round 6). Machine-verified. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/8_LoadBearingDepth_Dyck2.md. Script: /tmp/exp_net_dyck2.py.**

## Hypothesis
The load-bearing-depth test via the canonical NON-REGULAR context-free language. Dyck-2 (two bracket types '(' vs '[') next-token close prediction requires recovering the TYPE of the top of the stack (the last unmatched open's bracket type; chance 0.5 given only the balance) — a history-dependent discrete state. Natural construction: L1 computes balance, L2 selects+reads the last open, so d=1 should FAIL at close-type positions while d≥2 succeeds — the first genuinely load-bearing depth regime and the exit law's first potential boundary.

## Part A — depth is FLAT on Dyck-2
All 10 models (d∈{1,2,4,8,16}×2 seeds, 8000 AdamW steps, dm=48/4 heads, 100k train/20k fresh held-out) reach test=**1.0000 at every metric**: overall, b0–b4+, close_all, close_b4+. **d=1 alone recovers the stack-top type** at every depth and every close number, including closes whose matching open sits 11+ tokens back. The flat-depth law now covers **FIVE task classes**: lookups (NET-2), composition (NET-3), decomposable-error arithmetic (NET-4/5), Dyck-1 regular grammar (NET-7), Dyck-2 non-regular CFG (NET-8). Load-bearing premise refuted a third time.

## Part B — exit law holds on a 3rd task class; exit* is depth-saturated
| d | s | exit* | l=exit*−1→l=exit* | crossover | d/2 | lossless@cross | saving |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0 | 3 | 0.6903→1.0000 | 3 | 2 | True | 25% |
| 4 | 1 | 3 | 0.6477→0.9654 | 4 | 2 | True | 25% |
| 8 | 0 | 5 | 0.8875→0.9988 | 5 | 4 | True | 37.5% |
| 8 | 1 | 4 | 0.6097→0.9901 | 4 | 4 | True | 50% |
| 16 | 0 | 5 | 0.9237→0.9843 | 2 | 8 | False | 69% |
| 16 | 1 | 3 | 0.6314→0.9725 | 2 | 8 | False | 81% |

exit* ∈ {3,4,5} (does NOT scale with d); |exit*−crossover| ≤ 1 in 5/6 (**22/24 across all three task classes**); exit* ≥ crossover 5/6; lossless-at-crossover 4/6, failing exactly on the two d=16 models whose crossover fires at l=2 — confirming NET-7's refinement (the FIXED 0.95 bar, not the norm, is the reliable trigger when the crossover fires very early). **69–81% lossless inference-depth saving at d=16.**

## Part C — single-layer success is GENUINE (barrier g, quantified)
Windowed linear baselines (last-K tokens + balance + position, K∈{4,8,12}, 3 epochs): close_all = 0.7322/0.7544/0.7518 — never 1.0 even when the matching open is inside the window, because a linear map cannot route the CONDITIONAL index 'k-th close → open at distance 2k−1' (needs gating); attention can. Transformer 1.0 vs best baseline 0.7544 = **+25pp genuine long-range content**. Honest caveat: deep-balance bins rise on baselines because they're dominated by first-closes of deep runs (locally covered) — close_all is the honest hard-close diagnostic.

## Barriers
(a) no circularity (fresh random words, iid per-pair types, test seed+77); (b) flat/exit laws extended to non-regular CFG — new content is the 5-class flat law + depth-saturated exit + quantified baseline margin (Catalog scan: no prior work); (c) toy-scale AND the finding — load-bearing boundary not reached, next = semilength scaling / width-starved Dyck; (d) no leakage (held-out 1.0000 before probing); (e) 2×5 + 2×3 seeds, +3 outlier and 2/6 lossless failures reported not averaged; (f) documented metrics + close-bin caveat; (g) strongest windowed linear baseline loses by +25pp; (h) real lever: 69–81% lossless inference-depth cut on non-regular grammar + genuine caution that single-layer transformers solve canonical stack recovery at this scale.

## Verdict
(1) Load-bearing test fails THIRD time — depth flat on the canonical non-regular CFG; (2) exit law holds on 3rd task class (22/24 within ±1 of crossover, depth-saturated exit, lossless); (3) single-layer stack-top recovery is genuine (linear windows can't conditionally index; attention can). **Next:** semilength scaling (where does d=1 break — the actual load-bearing boundary), width-starved Dyck (dm=16/1 head), unbounded nesting, exit law at real-LM/BERT scale.
directions.title: NET-8: Depth is FLAT on Dyck-2 (non-regular CFG) — load-bearing test fails 3rd time; exit law holds on 3rd task class; single-layer stack-top recovery is genuine

**Round:** round-net-7 · **Speed axis, round 2** — the load-bearing-depth test of NET-6.
**Paper:** ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/7_ExitLaw_UnderLoad_Dyck.md · **Script:** /tmp/exp_net_speed2.py
**Verdict:** REFUTED (load-bearing premise) + CORRECTED (exit ≈ crossover, crossover task-dependent).

## Hypothesis
NET-6's exit*≈crossover≈d/2 was measured on attention-solvable automata (flat depth). Does the law hold — or fail (lossless exit impossible) — on a task where depth is genuinely load-bearing? Task: Dyck-1 balanced-paren next-token (semilength 12, nesting ≤12), the classic grammar where shallow transformers are expected to fail at deep nesting. (1) Does depth pay? (2) Is the exit law universal or bounded?

## Part A — depth is FLAT on Dyck-1 (grammar): d=1 solves all nesting ≤ 12
All 10 models (d∈{1,2,4,8,16}×2 seeds, dm=48, 4 heads, untied head, 6000 AdamW steps, 100k train/20k fresh held-out) reach test=1.0000 at **every balance bin including b4+** (nesting 4–10). The balance is a cumulative sum; one head computes it while another conditions the next token. "Shallow fails at deep nesting" is a width/context-starved artifact, not this scale. The flat-depth law now covers four task classes: lookups (NET-2), composition (NET-3), arithmetic (NET-4/5), grammar (NET-7). Load-bearing-depth regime NOT achieved — genuinely open.

## Part B — the exit layer tracks task difficulty, not d/2
Shared-head exit (trained final lnf+un on frozen LN(x_l)); exit* = first layer ≥ 0.95 (=0.95·full, all full=1.0):

| d | seed | exit* | l=exit*−1 → l=exit* | crossover | d/2 | saving |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0 | 3 | 0.7075 → 1.0000 | 3 | 2 | 25% |
| 4 | 1 | 2 | 0.6733 → 0.9613 | 3 | 2 | 50% |
| 8 | 0 | 3 | 0.5942 → 1.0000 | 2 | 4 | 62.5% |
| 8 | 1 | 2 | 0.6409 → 0.9737 | 2 | 4 | 75% |
| 16 | 0 | 4 | 0.7806 → 0.9927 | 3 | 8 | 75% |
| 16 | 1 | 4 | 0.8130 → 0.9814 | 1 | 8 | 75% |

exit* is **depth-INDEPENDENT {2,3,4}** across d=4..16 (≪ d/2 = {2,4,8}); crossover ∈ {1,2,3} (also ≪ d/2). The computation finishes in 2–4 layers regardless of total depth. **Saving: 25–50% at d=4 → 62.5–75% at d=8 → 75% at d=16** (vs ≈50% on automata). exit*−crossover = {0,−1,+1,0,+1,+3} → |·|≤1 in 5/6 (17/18 combined with NET-6), one +3 outlier (d=16 s1). REFINEMENT: lossless-at-crossover holds only 3/6 here (crossover earlier, exit* lags 1–3 layers); the reliable trigger is the fixed 0.95 usability bar.

## Law
**EXIT-TRACKS-TASK-DIFFICULTY** (correcting NET-6): the universal object is exit* ≈ crossover with the crossover TASK-DEPENDENT (≈d/2 on harder automata whose compute fills Phase I, ≈1–3 on easy grammar). On easy-to-moderate sequential tasks a trained transformer's inference depth can be cut ~75% (exit at layer 2–4 of 16) losslessly, no confidence gate.

## Barriers
(b) early-exit mature, but task-difficulty dependence of the exit layer + correction of the ≈d/2 claim + grammar-flatness new (Catalog scan 2067 packages: no prior work connecting norm crossover to a task-dependent exit); (c) toy-scale AND the finding — load-bearing test needs Dyck-2 / width-starved / unbounded nesting; (d) fresh held-out strings seed+77, all 1.0000 before probing; (e) 2 seeds×5 depths + 2×3 exit, +3 outlier reported not averaged; (f) exit acc = shared-head next-token acc, bar 0.95 = 0.95·full (full=1.0), crossover sustained-2 ≥1.02, by-balance exit moot (every bin 1.0000 at every depth); (g) full-model baseline at 1.0000, exit* gap ≤ 0.04; (h) real lever: up to 75% lossless inference-depth cut on easy sequential tasks.

**Next (round-net-8 candidates):** load-bearing-depth test via Dyck-2 (multi-type matching, genuinely non-regular) / width-starved / unbounded nesting; exit law at real small-LM/BERT scale; small-BERT PR + joint-aware allocation (compression); carry chain at larger scale.

# NET-6: DECODABILITY-CROSSOVER EXIT LAW (speed axis, first speed iteration)

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab, round-net-6. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/6_SpeedExit_DecodabilityCrossover.md. Script: /tmp/exp_net_speed.py.

## Hypothesis
NET-2's residual-stream two-phase law (‖x_l‖ stationary for l<≈d/2, then growth; final LayerNorm strips the growth) marks a compute/amplify boundary: Phase I = compute-in-place (NOT decodable by the trained head), Phase II = amplification (decodable from the crossover). Prediction: the network can be exited at the norm-predicted crossover layer with zero loss — a-priori-predictable ~50% inference-depth saving, no confidence gate.

## Experiment
Order-4 (1296-state) and order-3 (216-state) automata, dm=40, 4 heads, ctx=12, d∈{4,8,16}×2 seeds = 12 models, all trained to held-out test 1.0000. Per model: per-layer stream norms, Phase-II onset (crossover), shared-head exit accuracy (trained final lnf+un on each frozen LN(x_l)); exit* = first layer ≥0.98.

## Results
1. **exit* ≈ d/2, predictable a priori**: |exit*−crossover| ≤ 1 in 12/12 (exit*−crossover ∈ {−1,0,+1}, mean −0.25); exit*−d/2 ∈ {−1,0,+1}. Sharp cliff: exit*−1 acc 0.767–0.978 (always <0.98), exit* acc 0.980–1.000.
2. **Real, depth-growing saving**: compute fraction exit*/d = 0.75 (d=4, 25%), 0.50–0.62 (d=8, 38–50%), 0.44–0.56 (d=16, 44–56%, median ~50%). Lossless: gap to full (1.0000) ≤ 0.02, usually 0.0000.
3. **NEW NEGATIVE**: confidence-threshold dynamic exit is NOT the lever — mean per-token max-softmax-prob at the decodable layer is 0.70–0.96 (mean 0.80); a 0.999 gate fires only after the exit layer. The fixed norm-predicted exit is the artifact.

## Law
**DECODABILITY-CROSSOVER EXIT LAW.** The layer where the trained readout becomes linearly decodable (≥0.98) coincides with the residual-stream Phase-I/II boundary within one layer and is a-priori predictable (exit* ≈ d/2). Exiting at the crossover is lossless, saves ~50% inference depth at scale, needs no gate. Mechanism pinned: Phase I builds the representation in place (signal crosses the usability bar exactly at the boundary); Phase II is readout-amplification — why the final LayerNorm strips the growth and the second half is skippable.

## Barriers
(a) no circularity (exit measured with trained head on frozen streams), (b) partial — early-exit nets/probes known; exit-predicted-by-norm-crossover + fixed-beats-dynamic + depth-scaling new (Catalog 2067 packages: no prior work on the norm-crossover/decodability link), (c) toy-scale acknowledged, (d) clean held-out, all test 1.0, (e) 2×2×3 seeds, ±1 spread reported honestly, (f) exit acc = shared-head next-token acc, 0.98 bar consistent with NET-2, crossover = sustained-2 ≥1.02, (g) full-model baseline + measured confidence-gate baseline that fails, (h) real lever: halve inference depth on sequential tasks, predictor computable in training.

**Verdict.** CONFIRMED (exit ≈ d/2 predictable, lossless, saving 25%→50%); REFUTED at both extremes ("not decodable before crossover" — 3/12 exit*<crossover; "already decodable near layer 1" — exit* never near 1). Speed axis opened with a positive, exact, transferable law. Now 6 network experiments, assessment v6. Round-net-6 done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
directions.title: NET-6: DECODABILITY-CROSSOVER EXIT LAW — the residual-stream two-phase boundary predicts where a transformer becomes linearly decodable (exit at ~d/2, lossless, ~50% inference saving)

# NET-5: READOUT-UNTIE — the copy-self basin is a tied-readout artifact; the carry chain is readout-independent

**Program:** Network/LLM research lab, round-net-5 (depth axis, NET-4 follow-up). Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/5_CopyBasin_IsReadoutArtifact.md. Script: /tmp/exp_net_untie.py.

## Hypothesis
NET-4 identified the copy-self basin (per-digit ≈ 0.22–0.24, depth-independent) as a flat-loss attractor where the tied readout reproduces the previous teacher-forced digit (‖emb‖²-dominated logit). If the basin is caused by the tied readout, an UNTIED head (Linear(dm, VOCAB), no weight sharing) should eliminate it, making the decomposable-error depth law measurable without the stochastic-escape confound.

## Experiment
Identical to NET-4 except readout untied: pre-LN transformer, 4 heads, d_mlp=4·d_model, LSB-first base-10 a+b=c, n=6, per-digit cross-entropy, GO-shift teacher forcing, d_model matched to B≈100k±6% including the extra head weights. Part A: d∈{1,2,4}×3 seeds, 8000 steps. Part B: tied control 4000 steps (basin reproduces). Part C: untied length-gen train n=3→test n=4/5/6.

## Results
1. **Basin GONE**: escape steps untied [1000,1000,1000]/[2000,2000,1000]/[2000,3000,2000] vs tied [3000–6000]; per-digit at st=1000 already 0.60–1.00 vs tied 0.22–0.24 plateau. ‖emb‖² mechanism CONFIRMED.
2. **Carry chain READOUT-INDEPENDENT**: 3/9 untied configs still per-high/full-low (d1s0 0.8735/0.1143, d2s0 0.7499/0.0112, d2s2 0.8727/0.1089), all correlated-error (per^7=0.39/0.13/0.39 ≫ observed full).
3. **Depth law stays FLAT**: full-mastery d=4 3/3, d=1 2/3, d=2 1/3 — non-monotone, under-powered; escape now trivially depth-flat.
4. **Length-gen stays CHANCE**: untied d=2/d=4 train n=3 full=1.0000 both seeds, test n=4/5/6 full=0.0000 per≈0.09–0.18 at every depth.

## Law
**READOUT-UNTIE DECOMPOSITION.** The copy-self basin is a **tied-readout artifact** (untie ⇒ immediate depth-flat escape — first positive architectural cure in the depth series). The carry-chain dissociation is **readout-independent** (persists with untied head, correlated-error signature). Removing the basin does **not** expose a non-flat depth law — the carry chain is the same width/depth-immune bottleneck in both readout settings. Length-gen unaffected. The decomposable-error regime is now fully decomposed: a removable readout basin layered on an irreducible carry-chain credit-assignment wall — neither depth, width, nor readout-untying makes depth pay at this scale.

## Barriers
(a) no circularity (architectural treatment, measured; within-run tied control), (b) partial — untied embeddings are standard; NEW = the cure-for-copy-basin, readout-independence of the carry dissociation, untying-doesn't-unlock-depth negative (Catalog 2067 packages: no prior work on the decomposition), (c) toy-scale acknowledged, (d) clean held-out, (e) 3/2/2 seeds with spreads, (f) per/full separated, chance=0.1, correlated-error diagnostic, budget matched with extra head weights, (g) tied control at equal budget/same seeds, (h) real diagnostic (stuck tied model ⇒ untie first) + honest negative.

**Verdict.** Mechanism hypothesis CONFIRMED (basin is a readout artifact, removed by untying); the deeper hope REFUTED (carry chain, not the basin, was the binding constraint; depth stays flat). Now 5 network experiments, assessment v5. Round-net-5 done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
directions.title: NET-5: READOUT-UNTIE — the copy-self basin is a tied-readout artifact; the carry chain is readout-independent; depth stays flat

directions.description:
**Round-net-4 (network lab, depth axis — testing NET-3's constructive corollary).** Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/4_CopySelfBasin_StochasticEscape.md`. Notebook Part 4, assessment v4, network exp 4.

## Hypothesis (NET-3's corollary, taken in)
The ONE regime a non-flat depth law could live in: a task whose error signal decomposes over steps — digit addition with carries, each output digit its own supervision token. At fixed budget B, deeper should beat shallower; a carry-free control should stay flat; length-gen should widen the gap.

## Task
LSB-first base-10 `a+b=c`, n=6 columns, per-digit cross-entropy, teacher-forced decoding with a GO-token shift (copy shortcut adversarial at init: untrained per-digit ≈ 0.08 < chance 0.1). Pre-LN transformer, 4 heads, tied embedding, d_model matched per depth to B≈100k±6% (d=1: dm=88, d=2: dm=64, d=4: dm=44).

## Part A — copy-self basin + flat escape law
Every config sits in the same basin (per-digit ≈ 0.22–0.24, full 0.0, loss ≈ 2.0), identical across depths to three decimals — a shared flat-loss attractor where the tied-embedding readout reproduces the previous teacher-forced digit. Escape is abrupt (0.23→0.98 within one 1000-step interval) and stochastic.

**Depth law: FLAT in distribution.** Escape steps d=1 [5000,3000,6000] median 5000; d=2 [3000,5000,5000] median 5000; d=4 [3000,4000,3000] median 3000. Non-monotone at seed level (d=1 s1 escapes at 3000, earlier than d=4 s1's 4000); within-depth spread up to 2× exceeds between-depth differences. Full-mastery reliability mildly favors d=4 (3/3 vs 2/3 for d=1,d=2) but is under-powered (3 seeds). Decisive failure = the CARRY CHAIN, not the digit map: both stuck seeds are per-digit-high/full-low (d=1 s2: per 0.7402/full 0.0068; d=2 s0: per 0.8663/full 0.0991) with correlated errors (per=0.87 ⇒ full ≈ 0.38 if independent; observed 0.09).

## Part C — carry-free control fails its job, informatively
Carry-free is ALSO basin-trapped (d=2 both seeds per 0.4874/full≈0). The basin is task-independent — a property of tied-embedding per-digit teacher-forced decoding, not of carries. Refutes "carries are the depth-relevant ingredient".

## Part D — scale gates escape, not mastery
4× budget moves the per-digit escape 2–3× earlier (d=1@400k: st=1000 per 0.24–0.36 already above plateau, st=3000 0.87–0.94) but full-number mastery at 400k is LOWER (d=1: 0.4011±0.31 vs 0.9553±0.04 at 100k), again with correlated carry errors (d=1 s1@400k per 0.8703/full 0.0923; 0.8703⁷≈0.38≫0.09). Width rescues the digit map, not the carry chain.

## Part B — length-gen wall on arithmetic
d=2 and d=4 reach train n=3 full=1.0000 (both seeds) yet test n=4/5/6 full=0.0000, per-digit ≈ 0.09–0.16 ≈ chance at EVERY depth. Carries do not rescue length generalization; memorize-without-composition (NET-3 leg-2 wall) reproduced on the task class that was supposed to break it.

## Law
**COPY-SELF BASIN + STOCHASTIC ESCAPE.** On per-digit-supervised tied-embedding arithmetic, training is a two-state system: a depth-independent copy-self basin (per-digit ≈ 0.22–0.24, identical across depths) followed by an abrupt phase-transition escape that is flat in depth in distribution and gated by scale. The carry chain is the width/depth-immune bottleneck (correlated-error signature per^n ≫ full). Length-gen is chance at every depth even after perfect train memorization.

## Verdict
NET-3's clean prediction — decomposable error makes depth pay — is **REFUTED in its clean form**. The flat depth law now covers lookups (NET-2), composition (NET-3), and decomposable-error arithmetic (NET-4); the single-peaked depth picture fails everywhere; the binding constraint is optimization (a flat-loss copy attractor), never capacity. New objects: the copy-self basin (exact plateau, depth- and task-independent), the phase-transition escape, the per-digit/carry-chain dissociation, and scale-gates-escape-not-mastery.

## Barriers
(a) no circularity (GO-shift makes copy adversarial at init); (b) partial — copy shortcuts known, the per-digit copy-self basin + escape law + dissociation new (Catalog: no prior work); (c) toy-scale (n=6, ~100k params); (d) clean held-out batches; (e) 3/2/2/2 seeds with escape-spread reported; (f) per/full separated, chance=0.1, correlated-error diagnostic; (g) carry-free + width + length-gen controls; (h) honest negative + three diagnostics (check per≈0.23 plateau before judging a task unlearnable; high-per/low-full = chain failing; train-mastery + chance length-gen = memorize-without-compose).

Script: /tmp/exp_net_add.py (parts A–D; summary-print variable-shadowing bug fixed after the run — all data already in the log, no re-run needed).
directions.title: NET-4: The copy-self basin + stochastic escape — the decomposable-error regime also fails to break the flat depth law

directions.description:
**Round-net-3 (network lab, depth axis).** Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/3_CompositionDepth_Trichotomy.md`. Notebook Part 3, assessment v3, network exp 3.

## Hypothesis
On a task requiring genuine sequential composition with hidden intermediates, the fixed-budget depth law becomes non-flat — depth buys composition steps width cannot substitute. Task: input [x0, o1..ok, END] -> x_k = op_k∘..∘op_1(x0), 3 fixed random op-permutations on a 64-alphabet, intermediates NOT in context, test = held-out op-strings × fresh x0 (only a stepwise solution generalizes).

## The trichotomy (measured, all regimes depth-FLAT)
| regime | result |
|---|---|
| **L1 hidden + sparse** (k=6, 529 train/200 held-out strings) | UNLEARNABLE — d=6 train 0.90–0.94 at 8000 steps (2 seeds) = memorizing seen strings; held-out-string test stays at chance (0.023/0.028 vs 1/64=0.0156). Final-token loss does not decompose over the 6 random-permutation steps. |
| **L2 hidden + small** (train k≤3 → test k=6 length-gen) | MEMORIZED WITHOUT COMPOSITION — every depth d=1..8 reaches train(k≤3)=1.0000 but length-gen to k=6 = chance (0.0156) at EVERY depth; the model fits the 39-string lookup and never learns per-op maps. |
| **L3 intermediates given** (chain-in-context, k=6) | LEARNABLE AND DEPTH-FLAT — d=1 alone reaches held-out test=1.0000 (both seeds); once intermediates are context tokens, composition is one-step-per-token and depth is free. |

## The law
On the task class where depth is supposed to matter, the three achievable training regimes are all depth-flat: unlearnable, memorized-without-composition, or solvable at d=1. **Depth is gated by error-signal decomposability (credit assignment), not representational capacity** — the network has the depth to represent the stepwise solution but gradient descent cannot discover it from a non-decomposable final-token loss, and the only routes to learnability (small input space / exposed intermediates) both erase the depth requirement. This extends NET-2's flat law to BOTH sides of difficulty (easy lookups flat via attention-reads-context; hard composition flat via unlearnable/memorized/depth-free regimes) — the single-peaked depth picture fails to materialize anywhere; the binding constraint is optimization.

**Constructive corollary:** a task whose error signal decomposes over steps (digit addition with carries — each digit its own supervision token) is the one regime where a non-flat depth law could live (next target). Diagnostic: when a deep model is stuck, check error-signal decomposability before buying more depth.

**Barriers:** (a) clean, nothing injected; (b) partial — memorize-without-compose / length-gen failure known, the trichotomy-as-depth-law + credit-assignment mechanism + both-sides framing are new (Catalog scan 2067 packages, no prior work); (c) toy-scale, real-scale next; (d) clean held-out strings; (e) 2 seeds on decisive runs, 5-depth chance wall in L2; (f) final-token accuracy, chance=1/64 documented; (g) regime comparison only; (h) honest negative + diagnostic + decomposable-error pointer.

Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_comp.py (L1), /tmp/exp_net_comp2.py (L2), /tmp/exp_net_comp3.py (L3), /tmp/exp_net_comp4.py (L1 robustness).
directions.title: NET-3: The composition-depth trichotomy — why the depth law is flat on both sides of task difficulty

directions.description:
**Round-net-2 (network lab, depth axis).** Paper: `ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/2_ResidualStream_TwoPhaseLaw.md`. Notebook Part 2, assessment v2, network exp 2.

## LAW-A — the fixed-budget depth law is FLAT on attention-solvable tasks
At fixed total budget B ∈ {100k, 400k} × depths d ∈ {1,2,4,8} × 2 seeds (order-4 = 1296-state automaton, exact parameter match ±2%): **every config reaches held-out test ≥ 0.98 at the first 100-step checkpoint and ends at test = 1.0000** — the narrowest deepest (dm=32, 8 layers) ties the widest shallow (dm=180, 1 layer). The single-peaked depth hypothesis is REFUTED: one full-attention layer already reads the whole context, so at fixed budget depth is pure parameter overhead on attention-solvable tasks. Corollary: depth can only pay where tasks need sequential composition beyond one-hop attention.

## LAW-B — the residual-stream two-phase norm law (dm=40, order-3, all test=1.0000)
1. **Two phases:** ‖x_l‖ is stationary for the first ≈d/2 layers (d=16: 8.3→7.9 over layers 0–6), then grows monotonically with *increasing* per-layer ratio in the second half (d=16: 1.06→1.20 across layers 8–15); crossover at l≈d/2 in every seed.
2. **Bounded, depth-independent total inflation:** end/start = 2.2–3.3× across d=4…16 — extra depth is absorbed as a longer plateau, not more growth (‖x_l‖≈A·l^a, a≈0.3–0.4, sub-exponential; the "exponential residual growth" intuition is wrong on this class).
3. **Logit-scale invariance:** final logits 7.8±0.1 across d=4…16 — the final LayerNorm strips Phase-II growth; the readout is numerically depth-safe.
4. **Update orthogonality:** cos(x_{l-1}, dx_l)≈0, Phase-I slightly anti-aligned (holds norm), Phase-II aligned (drives growth); accumulation ratio ‖x_end‖²/Σ‖dx‖² grows 1.27→2.59 with depth.

**Barriers:** (a) clean — nothing injected; (b) partial — mech-interp residual-stream picture known, the two-phase/crossover-d/2/depth-independent-inflation objects are new (Catalog scan of 2067 packages found no prior work); (c) toy-scale, real-scale next; (d) clean held-out; (e) 2 seeds Part A / 3 seeds Part B; (f) 100-step speed resolution + batch-mean norms documented; (g) exact parameter match; (h) negative LAW-A + norm-budget diagnostic.

**Next:** a task that genuinely needs composition (digit addition with carries / recursion) to test whether the depth law becomes single-peaked; real-scale (small BERT) check of LAW-B.

Scripts: /tmp/exp_net_depth.py, /tmp/exp_net_depth_b.py, /tmp/exp_net_depth_c.py.
directions.title: NET-2: The depth law is flat on attention-solvable tasks; residual stream has a two-phase norm law

directions.description:
Network lab iteration 1 (compression axis). Hypothesis: per-layer quantization sensitivity is governed by each weight matrix's participation ratio (effective rank) PR=(Σσ²)²/Σσ⁴.

**Laws measured (3 seeds × 2 model classes, RTN per-row quantization, clean held-out):**

**MLP (5-layer, smooth 2D classification — generalizes, no grokking):** the minimal bits b* to keep ≥98% held-out accuracy is a MONOTONE step function of PR — high-rank bottleneck (PR≈5.4) needs 6 bits every seed, rank-1 readout (PR=1.0) needs 2 bits every seed. corr(PR, 3-bit damage) = −0.80/−0.92/−0.90; corr(PR, b*) = +0.87/+0.58/+0.94. PR-proportional equal-budget allocation beats uniform-4 on 2/3 seeds (+2.9/+3.5 pp at equal-or-fewer bits). PR is a DATA-FREE, BACKWARD-FREE sensitivity estimate (one SVD per layer).

**Transformer LM (2-layer, 2nd-order automaton, test=1.0 — perfectly generalizing):** the law REVERSES — every interior matrix (PR 12–25) is robust at 2 bits, while the LOW-PR input embeddings (PR≈4.4, 9.4) are the fragile layers (b*=3). Mechanism: per-row RTN at 2 bits has 1 level → collapses the 5-row embedding to ±max sign patterns. Joint quantization compounds: uniform-2 fails (0.59–0.91), uniform-3 lossless (0.98–1.0) → per-layer isolation undercounts joint damage.

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED within class, REFUTED as blanket transfer. Honest domain boundary: a data-free spectral law with a documented non-transfer; joint-aware allocation and real-scale (small BERT) validation are the next steps.

Barriers: (a) no, (b) sensitivity-based mixed precision is a known family (HAWQ/OBS/GPTQ) — new = data-free PR law + domain reversal, (c) toy-scale acknowledged, (d) clean held-out, (e) 3 seeds, (f) joint-compounding documented, (g) equal budgets (1 seed overshoot reported), (h) +2–3.5pp on MLP, no win on toy LM.

Script: /tmp/exp_net_quant.py. Paper: ResearchOutput/NetworkMathematics/1_SpectralQuantization_LawAndDomain.md. Round-net-1. Network exp 1, assessment v1.

## ABELIAN-TYPE-CHANNEL (round-23 #1, experiment 414, assessment v190, paper 79)

**The type-pair law is universal over all abelian cyclotomic conductors — and the >1-bit threshold is multi-stateness, not cyclicity (cyclicity amplifies). The motivating hypothesis is honestly refuted at the threshold: non-cyclic abelian groups DO exceed 1 bit when they have ≥3 type states.**

### Universality

Paper 78 proved I_pair = H(Π) − (1/φ(f))Σ_c H(Π_c) for cyclic fields (f prime). The same exact law holds on ALL abelian conductors — cyclic primes (5,7,13), cyclic prime powers (9=3², 25=5²), and non-cyclic abelian unit groups (C₂×C₂ f=8,12; C₂×C₂×C₂ f=24; C₂×C₄ f=15,20; C₂×C₂×C₄ f=40). Exact enumeration + 30k semiprime MC agree within 0.01 (f=8 0.2914 vs 0.2947; f=9 1.4749 vs 1.4739; f=15 1.0712 vs 1.0737; f=40 1.0216 vs 1.0226).

### Prime level on composite conductors

I(p mod f; T) = H(T) EXACT — first measured on non-cyclic abelian groups: C₂×C₄ (f=15) carries a **1.40-bit** multi-state type channel (1.4030 vs H(T)=1.4056), C₂×C₂×C₄ (f=40) 1.2700 vs 1.2718. **[T=1] splits-completely pins at H(1/φ(f)) EXACTLY for every composite f**: f=8 0.8092 = H(1/4) (= paper 77's V₄ = Q(ζ₈)); f=15 0.5397 = H(1/8) — the **FIRST C₂×C₄ pinning**; f=40 0.3352 = H(1/16) — the **FIRST C₂×C₂×C₄ pinning**. Thickening zero (f=15: I(p mod 225; T) = I(p mod 15; T)); coprime controls flat.

### Corrected structure law

The claim "non-cyclic ⟹ ≤ 1 bit" is FALSE: C₂×C₄ (f=15,20) I_pair = **1.0737** and C₂×C₂×C₄ (f=40) = **1.0226**, both exceeding the binary-fork cap. The true threshold is TYPE-STATE COUNT:

- **2 states ⟹ I_pair = Is(φ(f)) EXACTLY** (the type pair IS the split count): f=8 0.2947 = Is(4) — the full type channel of Q(ζ₈) is exactly paper 77's split-count; f=24 0.0906 = Is(8). Paper 74's Is(n) is the 2-state face.
- **≥ 3 states ⟹ I_pair > 1 bit**, cyclic and non-cyclic alike.

But **cyclicity amplifies** — a clean 1D > 2D > 3D character law among 3-state groups:

| group | I_pair |
|---|---|
| C₄ (cyclic, 1D) | 1.2500 |
| C₂×C₄ (2D) | 1.0737 |
| C₂×C₂×C₄ (3D) | 1.0226 |

A cyclic (1-dimensional) character concentrates the N-conditioning best; each extra generator erodes the channel.

### Two exact identities

- **Prime-power identity**: Q(ζ₉) (3², C₆) has EXACTLY the same type law as Q(ζ₇) (p, C₆) — I_pair = 1.4739 both. The type law of a cyclic field depends only on the cyclic order φ(f), not the conductor.
- **2-state identity**: for any 2-state type, I_pair = Is(φ(f)) EXACT (verified to 1e-9 on f = 8, 12, 24).

Semiprime checks: which-factor wall 0.0000–0.0002 (symmetric, factor-useless); coprime controls flat; s-projection recovers Is(φ) (f=15 0.0888 vs Is(8)=0.0906; f=40 0.0257 vs Is(16)=0.0267).

### Verdict

CONFIRMED (universal law + corrected threshold). New exact objects: the type-pair law on non-cyclic abelian groups, the composite-conductor [T=1] pinnings (first C₂×C₄ and C₂×C₂×C₄), the prime-power identity, the 2-state identity, and the 1D>2D>3D amplification law. Factor-useless: symmetric (barrier 2), pure p-mod-f residue dial (barrier 5), N-computable only behind the CRT split (barrier 6), cyclotomic fields + Dirichlet characters + CRT + Chebotarev 1922 (barrier 8). Unifies papers 74 (Is(n) = 2-state face), 77 (Q(ζ₈) = the 2-state type channel), 78 (cyclic prime type channel). Barriers 2/5/6/8.

## C2XC2-PINNING-CONTRAST (round-22 #1, experiment 412, assessment v188, paper 77)

**The first 2-dimensional abelianization G^ab = C₂×C₂, tested on the control pair of Q(√2,i) = Q(ζ₈) (Gal = V₄, ABELIAN) and Q(∜2,i) (Gal = D₄, non-abelian) — identical character lattice, same abelianization, differing only in abelian-ness. The paper-71 criterion in its cleanest form: abelian V₄ pins the identity; non-abelian D₄ cannot.**

### The control pair

Both fields share the three quadratic subfields Q(√2), Q(i), Q(√−2) ⟹ the identical character lattice — (2|p) cond 8, (−1|p) cond 4, (−2|p) cond 8, all N-computable via p mod 8 — and the same G^ab = C₂×C₂. Only abelian-ness differs: V₄ (x⁴−2x²+9, disc 384²) is abelian; D₄ (x⁴−2, disc −2¹¹, [D₄,D₄]=⟨r²⟩≅C₂) is not. Histograms over 22,997 primes (2^18): V₄ nr=4 0.2487 (1/4), nr=0 0.7513; D₄ nr=4 0.1238 (1/8), nr=0 0.6257 (5/8), nr=2 0.2505 (1/4) — the exact signatures.

### The criterion on the 2D abelianization

- **V₄ (abelian) ⟹ every fork pins**: [nr=4] ⟺ p≡1 mod 8, I = 0.8092 = H(1/4) = 0.8113 EXACT.
- **D₄ (non-abelian) ⟹ only the ⟨r²⟩-coset forks pin**: [nr=2] (rate 1/4) ⟺ p≡7 mod 8, I = 0.8120 = H(1/4) EXACT — the first **JOINT-AND 2D fork** (AND of (2|p)=+1 with (−1|p)=−1; no character mod 8 has {7} as a level set); complement [nr∈{4,0}] ⟺ p∈{1,3,5} mod 8 equally pinned.
- **The identity [nr=4] = {e} (rate 1/8) CANNOT pin**: e shares the commutator coset {e,r²} with r² (same C₂×C₂ fibre (+1,+1)) ⟹ **LEAKAGE** I = 0.2916 = H(1/8) − (1/4)H(1/2) = 0.29356 EXACT, CAPPED at every m (ladder m=4 0.1379, m=8/16 0.2936, coprime m=5 0). Large partner [nr=0] (rate 5/8) leaks 0.70443 EXACT.

### Within-coset: the e-vs-r² commutator coin

P([e] | p≡1 mod 8) = **0.4980** (D₄: e vs r² a fair coin in the commutator fibre) vs **1.0000** (V₄: pinned). I(p mod 16; [e] | p≡1 mod 8) = 0.0000 (z = −0.61) — the beyond-the-dial refinement invisible to every modulus. Cap check I(m=8)=I(m=16)=0.2916 < H(1/8) = 0.5436.

### Semiprime (30k)

The paper-74 order-4 split-count law holds EXACTLY on BOTH rate-1/4 forks, including the D₄ joint-AND 2D event on a non-abelian field: V₄ [split] s 0.2892 vs Is(4)=0.2947, OR 0.0349 vs g(4)=0.0359, AND 0.1323 vs A(4)=0.1345, XOR 0.1994 vs X(4)=0.2044; D₄ [nr=2] s 0.3003, OR 0.0363, AND 0.1376, XOR 0.2087. The D₄ [e] leakage fork — the SEMIPRIME COLLAPSE of prime-level leakage: s 0.0421 (law 0.0428), OR 0.0034 (0.0030), AND 0.0306 (0.0318), XOR 0.0138 (0.0135). Which-factor wall 0.0000 for all three forks.

### Classification table (C₂×C₂ row closed)

C₂→quadratic (54/72); C₃→cubic H(1/3) (71); C₅→order-5 H(1/5) (76); S₃/S₄→sign-only (65–71); A₄→cubic+within-V₄ flat (75); A₅→absolutely flat (76); **V₄→every fork pins [e]=H(1/4) EXACT; D₄→coset-forks pin ([nr=2] joint-AND H(1/4)), [e] leaks 0.2936 capped, [nr=0] leaks 0.7044** (this paper). The 2D abelianization adds pinning CONTENT but the e-vs-r² refinement stays commutator-invisible.

### Verdict

CONFIRMED. The paper-71 criterion holds on the first 2-dimensional abelianization; the control pair is its cleanest statement. Factor-useless: symmetric class functions with residue content only at the N-computable abelianization (barrier 2), a full 2D residue dial with invisible beyond-dial refinement (barrier 5), the C₂×C₂ fibre IS the quadratic-reciprocity content — computing the coset IS computing (χ₂(p),χ₄(p)) (barrier 6), all Galois 1832 + cyclotomic fields + quadratic/octic reciprocity + Chebotarev 1922 (barrier 8). Unifies papers 71, 74, 75, 76. Barriers 2/5/6/8.

## A5-PERFECT-FLATNESS (round-21 #2, experiment 411, assessment v187, paper 76)

**The splitting fork of a Gal(A₅) field is ABSOLUTELY unpinnable — closing paper 75's predicted A₅ row.** Papers 65–71 established: a binary splitting fork is congruence-pinned by a Dirichlet character IFF it factors through the abelianization G^ab of the Galois closure. Every group tested had G^ab ≠ {1}. This experiment tests the final prediction: **A₅ perfect ⟹ absolutely flat.**

### The theorem (provable a priori)

A₅ is perfect ([A₅,A₅]=A₅, A₅^ab={1}), so the only quotients of A₅ are A₅ and {e} — the splitting field L has NO nontrivial abelian subextension, hence **L ∩ Q(ζ_m) = Q for EVERY modulus m**, Gal(L·Q(ζ_m)/Q) = **A₅ × (Z/m)^×** (direct product), and by Chebotarev P(Frob_p ∈ F | p ≡ c mod m) = |F|/60 for every fork F and residue c ⟹ **I(p mod m; fork) = 0 exactly in the limit, all forks, all m.** No pinning (no character exists); no leakage (paper 75's leakage needs a pinned super-channel). **A₅ realizes only the flat state.**

### Machine-verified on x⁵ + 20x + 16 (disc 32000² = 2¹⁶·5⁶, Gal = A₅)

Part A — exact A₅ signature over 22,997 primes: nr=5 0.0163 (id, 1/60), nr=2 0.3334 (3-cycles, 1/3), nr=1 0.2496 ([2,2], 1/4), nr=0 0.4007 (5-cycles, 2/5), **nr=3/nr=4 ZERO** (no transpositions ⟹ G ⊆ A₅; distinguishes A₅ from D₅/C₅).

Part B — ABSOLUTE FLATNESS: all 5 forks × 12 moduli (3,4,7,8,9,11,13,16,25,31,59,101, incl. the discriminant's 16/25 and the C₅ control's 11) at the **shuffled-null** (300 shuffles, paper-70 honest test): **GLOBAL max |z| = 2.00.** The strongest residue-invisibility in the lab, provable a priori.

Part C — positive control: the abelian C₅ field Q(ζ₁₁)+ pins EXACTLY — I(p mod 11; [nr=5]) = **0.7198 = H(1/5) = 0.7219**, P=1.0000 on p≡±1 mod 11, coprime m=13 flat — the pipeline detects pinning when it exists, so the A₅ flatness is real.

Part D — semiprime (30k, 2^16 pool): C₅ obeys the paper-74 order-5 split-count law EXACTLY (s 0.2028 vs Is(5)=0.2027; OR 0.0203 vs 0.0215; AND 0.0995 vs 0.0979; XOR 0.1262 vs 0.1276; s-dist [0.64,0.32,0.04]), while A₅ forks give EVERY channel at null (|z|≤0.9) — no character to carry s.

### Verdict

CONFIRMED. The pinning-content classification table is **CLOSED**: abelian ⟹ pinned at H(1/n) (n=order), solvable non-abelian ⟹ pinned at the abelianization, **perfect ⟹ absolutely flat**. The three-state picture (pinned/flat/leakage) is exhausted. Factor-useless: symmetric class functions with zero residue content (barrier 2), the strongest structural-orthogonality seal (barrier 5), L∩Q(ζ_m)=Q behind the direct product (barrier 6), all Galois 1832 + A₅ simplicity + Chebotarev 1922 + cyclotomic fields (barrier 8). Unifies papers 71, 74, 75. Barriers 2/5/6/8. Round-21 COMPLETE 2/2.
directions.title: A5-PERFECT-FLATNESS: the A5 splitting fork is absolutely unpinnable (perfect ⟹ flat, all forks × all m) — paper 76, exp 411, v187

## OR-COLLAPSE-LAW (round-19 #2, experiment 407, assessment v183, paper 72)

**An exact universal law of the semiprime OR collapse.** Paper 71 proved the fork-pinning criterion (a fork is congruence-pinned iff it factors through G^ab) and measured one collapse (cond-7 cubic OR = 0.0728 bits). Here is the general law: for any abelian field whose split-completely event is pinned by an order-n Dirichlet character (split ⟺ χ(p)=1, P(split)=1/n), the semiprime OR [split(p) OR split(q)] obeys, for gcd(N,f)=1,

**P(OR | χ(N)=1) = 1/n, P(OR | χ(N)≠1) = 2/n, P(OR) = (2n−1)/n², I(N mod f; OR) = g(n) = H((2n−1)/n²) − (1/n)H(1/n) − ((n−1)/n)H(2/n)** — universal in the order n, independent of field, degree, and conductor structure.

### Machine-verified on 7 fields (2^22, 30k semiprimes, split sets empirically confirmed by nroots==deg)

| field | n | f | I(N mod f; OR) | g(n) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| x²−x−1 (Q(√5)) | 2 | 5 | 0.3076 | 0.3113 |
| x³+x²−2x−1 (cyclic cubic) | 3 | 7 | 0.0704 | 0.0728 |
| x³−3x+1 (cyclic cubic) | 3 | 9=3² | 0.0735 | 0.0728 |
| x⁴−4x²+2 (Q(ζ₁₆)+, units C₂×C₄) | 4 | 16=2⁴ | 0.0384 | 0.0359 |
| x⁵+x⁴−4x³−3x²+3x+1 (Q(ζ₁₁)+) | 5 | 11 | 0.0222 | 0.0215 |
| Φ₇ (Q(ζ₇)) | 6 | 7 | 0.0146 | 0.0144 |
| cyclic cubic (character-only) | 3 | 21=3·7 | 0.0700 | 0.0728 |

Per-class conditional rates match 1/n and 2/n within 1–2% everywhere; coprime modulus FLAT; m=f² invariant.

### UNIFICATION — the two biggest residue channels of the lab are two points of one law

- **The p−1 ℓ=3 symmetric OR (paper 54: 0.313) IS the n=2 case** with f=3 (split = p ≡ 1 mod 3, χ the quadratic character of Q(√−3)): reproduced I(N mod 3; OR) = **0.3126** including the N≡0 class, P(OR|N≡1)=0.4942 (law 1/2), P(OR|N≡2)=**1.0000** (law 2/n).
- **Paper 71's cond-7 cubic OR (0.0728) is the n=3 case.**

### The decay law

g(n) monotone → 0: 0.3113/0.0728/0.0359/0.0215/0.0144/0.0103/0.0077/0.0060 (n=2..9). The MORE the prime-level fork pins (H(1/n) ≈ 1 bit), the LESS its OR shows — no order-n Dirichlet fork ever yields more than g(n) ≤ 0.3113 symmetric OR bits.

### Factor-useless (barriers 2/5/6/8)

Symmetric (which-factor wall 0.0001–0.0002), a Dirichlet residue dial (QRLEAK family), sealed behind the CRT split, all classical (quadratic 1801 / cubic 1844 / higher reciprocity + Dirichlet characters + CRT). The residue-fork line is now quantitatively CLOSED at the semiprime level.

**Verdict:** exact law CONFIRMED on 7 fields spanning prime/composite conductors and cyclic/non-cyclic unit groups. Round-19 2/2 done. Barriers 2/5/6/8.

## Open conjectures for the next cycle



### Conjecture E′ (the fibre spectrum is a strictly finer invariant)

*The vector `(m_P)_P` of pattern multiplicities separates pairs of actions that the scalar moment
`Σ_g |X^g|^k` cannot; and `m_P = 1` for all `P` with exactly `j` blocks iff the action is
`j`-transitive (the block-graded refinement of the fibrewise criterion).*

The key insight is that the fibrewise criterion now proved treats all patterns at once, whereas the
transitivity hierarchy is graded by the number of blocks: restricting attention to the patterns
with `j` blocks should isolate exactly `j`-transitivity inside the `k`-tuple data, giving a
spectrum of invariants between the moments.

Why now? The decomposition, the fibrewise criterion and the exact defect formula are proved
(items 18–19), and cycle 3 also shows the scalar moment cannot separate actions (item 15), so the
only thing left to test is whether the refined vector can.



### Conjecture F (Bell defect bounds the failure of transitivity)

*The Bell defect `D_k(G,X) := Σ_g |X^g|^k − B_k|G| ≥ 0` satisfies: `D_k = 0 ⇒ D_j = 0` for `j ≤ k`
(proved), and quantitatively `D_2 > 0 ⇒ D_k ≥ c_k · D_2` for an explicit combinatorial constant
`c_k` depending only on `k`.*

The key insight is that the defect counts non-singleton fibres of the orbit-to-pattern map with
multiplicity, and a failure of 2-transitivity is inherited by every longer tuple by padding with
repeated coordinates, which multiplies the excess by a controlled partition count.

Why now? Non-negativity, the implication `D_k = 0 ⇒ D_j = 0`, and now the exact formula
`D_k = |G|·Σ_P (m_P − 1)` (item 19) are theorems; only the quantitative propagation between
different `k` is open, and it is now a statement about fibre sizes rather than about moments.



### Conjecture G (how much labelling an injective aggregate must spend)

*Every injective aggregate `A : (Fin m → QLaurent) → QLaurent` that is additive in each argument
must spread the coefficients over at least `m` pairwise disjoint infinite sets of exponents; in
particular no such aggregate has image contained in the series supported on a set of density
`< 1/m`.*

The key insight is that cycle 3 identified symmetry as the obstruction, so what remains is a
counting bound: injectivity forces the aggregate to reserve, for each index, an infinite family of
independent coefficient slots, which is exactly what the interleaving construction does with the
residues mod `m`.

Why now? The dichotomy (interleaving injective, every symmetric aggregate non-injective) is proved;
the missing piece is a lower bound showing interleaving is not just *an* answer but essentially the
*only* shape of answer.

directions.description:
For a class `{p_θ}` the minimax pointwise redundancy is **exactly** `log₂ Cₛ`
with `Cₛ = ∑ₓ sup_θ p_θ(x)` (`shtarkov_minimax`), and

* memoryless class over alphabet `A`: `Cₛ ≤ (n+1)^{#A}`, binary case `Cₛ ≤ n+1`;
* first-order Markov: `Cₛ ≤ #A·(n+1)^{#A²}`;
* binary memoryless lower bound: `Cₛ ≥ √n/4`, i.e. `≥ ½ log₂ n − 2` bits;
* deterministic ("one decompressor per file") class: `Cₛ = #X`, price `= n` bits;
* the price is additive over independent blocks (`price_prodClass_add`), and
  only *sub*additive when the blocks share a parameter
  (`shtarkovSum_tiedProdClass_le`), which specialises to subadditivity of the
  memoryless price in the message length, `Cₛ(n₁+n₂) ≤ Cₛ(n₁)·Cₛ(n₂)`
  (`iid_price_subadditive`) — so `log₂ Cₛ(n)/n` converges by Fekete.

So a specialised decompressor can move only `Θ(log n)` bits out of the message
for a parametric class, and *zero* bits for an unrestricted class. The gate of
the research plan is met (the Rissanen rate is matched from below), and the
verdict is: specialisation pays only when the data class is genuinely
low-complexity relative to the data.

   ideal collision of degree `K` and size `K + 1` fits in `{0, …, N}`.  The verified values
   `d(1..5) = 2, 4, 7, 18, 16` show `d(5) < d(4)`.  Conjecture: `d(K)` is non-monotone
   infinitely often, and `d(K) = Θ(K^2)` — in particular `d(K) < 2^{K+1} - 1`, so the Prouhet
   alphabet is never optimal for `K ≥ 3`.  *The key insight is* that ideal solutions of odd
   degree can be built symmetrically (the degree-`5` optimum `{0,3,5,11,13,16}` vs
   `{1,1,8,8,15,15}` is symmetric under `x ↦ 16 − x`), which halves the number of independent
   constraints, whereas even degrees admit no such symmetry.  *Why now?*  Symmetry of the
   optimum is visible already at `K = 5` in the search of §12, and the transfer lemma
   `PowerSumIdealPTE.minCollisionCard_eq_of_ideal_witness` turns any candidate witness into a
   theorem about `m(N, K)` mechanically, so each new degree costs one `decide`.
directions.title: S4 (non-monotonicity of the ideal alphabet)

directions.description:
Between the critical alphabet `N = K + 1`, where

   (`ComputationalEvidence.md` §12), and `m(N,3) ≤ 6` for `N ≥ 5` is the theorem
   `PowerSumIdealPTE.minCollisionCard_three_le_six`.  Conjecture: every intermediate value of
   `m(·, K)` is of the form `½‖c‖₁` for a *vertex* of the kernel polytope, and the number of

   the `K = 3` row is now bracketed from both sides by theorems, so the first genuinely new

directions.description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'Matrix group $Λ$-distributions' and formalize its key results. Abstract: The $Λ$-distribution of a compact matrix group is an invariant in algebraic probability theory that was recently introduced to study zero distributions of function field $L$-functions. It is encoded by the $σ$-moment generating function, a generalization of the Molien series of classical invariant theory. In this work, we compute the $σ$-moment generating functions of finite matrix groups in many new cases. In particular, we compute the asymptotic $Λ$-distributions for the infinite families of Weyl reflection groups of types $B_n/C_n$ and $D_n$, complementing the previously known case of reflection groups of type $A_n$, i.e., symmetric groups. We also establish a general result relating the shapes of $σ$-moment generating functions to the distributions of associated classical random variables, explaining a previous ad hoc observation for independent Gaussians arising from traces of powers on compact classical groups.
directions.proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
directions.title: ArXiv paper: Matrix group $Λ$-distributions

directions.description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'A Local Central Limit Theorem for Clique Counts in Sparse Random Graphs' and formalize its key results. Abstract: Let $X_H$ denote the number of copies of a fixed graph $H$ in $G_{n, p}$. Gilmer and Kopparty conjectured that $X_H$ satisfies a local central limit theorem (LCLT) provided that $H$ is connected, $p \gg n^{-1/m(H)}$, and $n^2 (1-p) \gg 1$, where $m(H)$ is the maximum density. Following the work of Berkowitz, Sah and Sawhney confirmed this conjecture for every constant $p$, leaving the regime where $p=o(1)$ open. In this regime, the only case addressed in the literature is when $H=K_3$, where, in a recent paper, Araújo and Mattos confirmed the conjecture for $p \in (4n^{-1/2}, 1/2)$. This, together with a general result of Röllin and Ross, essentially settles the conjecture for the triangle. We generalise these results by showing that an LCLT holds for $H = K_r$ (for any fixed $r \ge 3$) in the regime $n^{-1/m(H)}\ll p\leq 1/2$, essentially settling the conjecture for cliques.
directions.proof_strategy: Analyze the paper's main theorem and construct a formal Lean 4 proof.
directions.title: ArXiv paper: A Local Central Limit Theorem for Clique Counts in Sparse Random Graphs
